That my fate would be like this?  
Carrion crow,  
You may know my life,  
But I also know it forever.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hey fate, my fate, oh fate  
My life is like that of a woodcutter  
Goo ya goo ya, 갈가마구야, Jirisan, 갈가마구야  
Your fate and my fate are all the same  
“Wow, there’s a lot of wood, it’s already a load  
Let’s go cut more, iuhuhuhu”  
Sopal

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Afterwards - Huui Afterwards Huui Huuhu  
Daewonsan mountain, Gari Galgamaguya Ei Eh –ye  
Fate, fate, my fate, this damn fate, my life  
Some people have good fate, burying it under their fingernails and toenails  
Eating just plain rice like an outsider, wearing clothes on the outside  
Living well in comfort, but my fate is like a hat brim  
Even old shoes have pairs, straw shoes have pairs too  
The surface of pine needles is my fate, oh yeah  
When the day was born, I was born, and when the moon was born, I was born too  
My fate is like a hat brim  
Ah- this hu –

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Goya goya goya galgamagu  
Take me away  
Wherever you go, even Mount Taesan will bend down

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hey, heyhee - man, what a lucky fate some people have  
Living in an ancient, grand house, wearing a pink ribbon in their hair  
When the southeast wind blows gently, the sound of the ribbon is loud and clear  
This guy's fate is miserable, everything in heaven and earth has a pair  
Even shoes have pairs, and sleeves have pairs  
But this poor fate of mine is like a worn-out shoe — how come I have no pair?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Uh - Uh uh - Uheah  
Old man, our old man, in the harsh year of the rooster,  
ate nineteen bowls of barley and bean porridge  
and died from overeating, our old man.  
He died, he died.  
This year is a bumper year,  
but he couldn’t even get a single bowl of rice,  
and died.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Old man, old man,  
Hoo hoo hoo, old man,  
You are going crazy, going crazy,  
You are going crazy.  
Sending the old man to the mountain village pasture along the twelve o'clock path,  
The old man was sent to the water of the pond,  
But was trampled by the dog's hind legs,  
Hoo hoo, old man.  
After that husband passed away,  
She got a second husband,  
In the shade of the pine forest in May and June,  
She froze to death again.  
She got a third husband,  
Under a cabbage leaf in May and June,  
She was stepped on and died, hoo hoo, old man.  
It’s truly pitiful beyond measure.  
You are going crazy, going crazy.  
Even we, if by chance we should die just once,  
Let us promise to help each other in the afterlife.  
You die and become a flower,  
I die and become a butterfly,  
Your flower clusters hold me,  
When the wind blows and the flower clusters play,  
Fluttering wings,  
Let’s open wide and have fun together.  
In a good place with mild feelings,  
I die, what will happen?  
You die, what will happen?  
I die and become a water of yin and yang, unending for seven years,  
You die and soar high above the middle heavens,  
Spreading two broad wings wide open,  
Leaving behind all the blue, red, and yellow liquor,  
Like a parrot bird from a noble house.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hearing the waist song, Garigalgamaguya —  
Where have you been wandering, coming back to your hometown? —  
Over there, on that mountain stream, the maiden is gathering herbs.  
The watercress has grown thick and lush.  
Come over here, over there, the young man is cutting grass.  
The paulownia trees have grown thick and lush.  
Come over here, hey hey —  
If you go up, there's bracken fern; if you go down, there's more bracken fern.  
Carefully weaving them, tying them one by one,  
They’re sold at the sand market and the five-day market.  
Who should I give it to? Should I give it to you?  
Buy something tasty and give it to the maiden.  
Love and waist, hoo hoo ya,  
Garigalmagguya,  
Let’s live together, making a hundred-year vow, hey hey —

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Guya Guya Galgamaguyah  
Please listen and take me away  
Take me with you, serve me  
Please listen and serve me  
Nacha Nacha Ban Dal Nacha  
I trusted you and lived, I played  
Why are you so heartless?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Guya Guya, Gari Gari, Galgamaguya—  
Don’t fly too high, eheh  
You’re dizzy, and I’m dizzy  
Don’t fly too low, in the worldly field  
If you go there, you’ll get stuck, some people  
Are fortunate, living in a tall house made of ancient ore  
Hehe, they said to relax, born that way  
What sin was there in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter?  
Climbing up that mountain and river, tightly bound  
On that side is a girl gathering herbs, eheh  
Listen to what I say, listen carefully  
Wild chives have grown thick and abundant  
The young man cutting the grass over there  
Listen to what I say, listen carefully  
Oak leaves have thickened over the wild grass and chilled  
This fate is poor, in the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
Was I tied to this mountain and river?  
That girl picking herbs  
Like the day, through the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
That bottomless stye, through the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
With a waist belt, and this fate is poor  
Through the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
Knocking on the carrying frame and crutches, what is this nonsense?  
That girl over there, eheh—  
Listen to what I say, through the seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
Wearing that stye on the waist like that, eh—  
I can’t do it, I really can’t do it  
E gugugu.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
That fallow field over there was left uncultivated last year,  
And this year, just like the days, it remains uncultivated again.  
That long stalk crying in the cold wind of the midwinter month,  
Is your heart so deep that you weep so sorrowfully as you go?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Kuya Kuya Gari Gari Galmaguya -  
Don’t fly too high, hey hey  
You’re dizzy and I’m dizzy too  
Don’t fly too low, in the sorghum field  
By the roadside - it’s bothering me  
Oh my, what a lucky person  
They said to laugh heartily in a high house with ancient ore  
What sin does a lifetime hold?  
It’s hanging on the tip of a blade of grass  
That is the girl picking herbs  
Listen to what she says  
Come into my humble house  
The cress has grown thick and withered  
That is the young master cutting grass -  
Come into my humble house -  
The oak leaf and wild greens have grown thick and withered  
That is that girl too, what sin does a lifetime hold, huh -  
In spring, summer, autumn, and winter, wearing a dried gourd at her waist  
Hanging on the tip of a blade of grass, she’s doing it like that  
Ah - my fate is rough, through spring, summer, autumn, and winter  
Ah - when you beat the carrying pole and crutch, hanging on this mountain pass  
What is this talk, oh my oh my oh.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
@ Hey, fire-feather bird

Fire-feather bird of Jirisan,
If you fly high, it’s dizzy,
If you fly low, it sweeps through the mugwort field.

Even the flying geese,
They have pairs,
Even trees have pairs,
Even the door has a pair of hinges.

A broad field that is good for farming,
Is there a field for raising cows?

A house with a spinning wheel in the room,
A house with a loom in the room,

Is there a woman with a broad bottom?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hoohoo..!
I’m going to Jirisan, Garigamagooya.
The icicles in the dense mountain range are melted by the spring breeze,
And these deep feelings are hoohoohoo.
I’m going to Jirisan, Garigamagooya.
Who will untie these deep feelings?
Guguguya, hoohoohoo.
The fresh spring cabbages wait for the spring rain to come,
Chunhyang, trapped in the jade tower, waits for Lee Doryeong to come, hoohoohoo!
I’m going to Jirisan, Garigamagooya.
The sun setting on the western mountain wants to set,
And the beloved who left in the morning, do they want to leave?
Hoohoohoo!

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Guya Guya, Shin-gu, Sirisan Eomma, Gari, Galgamaguya  
Silver foot, brass foot, tussock foot, eleven and a half years holding the house,  
Crossing the small pine grove into the big pine grove—  
Putting hands into mother’s embrace, feet into father’s embrace, going to sleep—  
But whose arms do I put my hands and feet into to go to sleep?  
Guya Guya, Galgamaguya,  
At Shin-gu, Sirisan ridge, going to Gari, Galgamaguya, oh—  
The sound of water spreading over that field beyond—  
Like my mother calling me while serving black seaweed soup with white rice mixed in.  
The ringing in my ears, the tears in my eyes—  
Guya Guya, at Shin-gu, Sirisan ridge, going to Gari, Galgamaguya—oh—  
Whether it’s your fate or what I abandon, around the nose bridge full of resentment  
Wrapping my lover’s handkerchief, sleeping under my floral jeogori blouse,  
It’s no good, no good at all  
Guya Guya—Galgamaguya  
At Shin-gu, Shingok mountain ridge, going to Gari, Galgamaguya  

—“Song of Fate”

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Eh - hey, new mountain crow in the new year  
Eh - hey, even a stone has a mate  
Even a worn-out mat has a mate, and until I turned fifty  
How come I have no mate? It's my fate, it's my fate.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
The climbing silk tree flowers are late silk trees.  
Plucking knotweed, laportea, and lunchbox herbs,  
I placed them under the bush, and the cicada calls.

This cooking, come cooking,  
Hand over that big child picking greens,  
Under the knotweed, laportea, and lunchbox herbs,  
Here it is, come cooking.

"Now towards that side, the big child will receive it."

You come cooking, the master comes cooking,  
Beside this child's head, springtime faith, water sprinkling, pure and clear,  
Eh, here it is.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Whioooo wind, strong wind, do not blow  
The west wind, the fallen leaves have all dropped  

@ Eh huya huya hohoya huhya oraday  

Hio, famous mountains and great rivers, Shinbul Peak, Don’t mistreat guests who come at night  
Hioooo, Myeongsashipri, Hwagaenghwa flower, don’t grieve just because you wither  
Hio, next March will come again, next March will hurt again  
Hiooooo, heartless time, don’t go away, all the youth I knew are growing old  
Hioooooo, snow on the white surface—did my parents wear a dreamlike garment?  
With neat makeup and attire, they flew to the Jarangri field

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Crow, crow, crow  
Flying high in the mid-air, heading towards the twilight at seven hundred -  
Suddenly delivering news - Ihuihuhuiya  

Like the morning star, my body bears a burden like an ox,  
Coming and going over Mount Jutai, oh how weary my fate,  
I am a farmer by fate.  

Some people have good fate, enjoying wealth and honor,  
Living comfortably in ancient splendid houses,  
Oh how weary my fate - Ihuihuya  

The departed lover left in bitter cold winter, now it's the fresh spring of March -  
When the flowers bloom and leaves sprout, will you come?  
The crying child calls the father, the mother’s soy sauce is all melted,  
The lover gone to the battlefield might come on leave, but the lover gone to the distant mountains and rivers,  
Is nowhere to be found, oh how weary my fate.  

Even straw sandals have a way to hang them, so how much more us women -  
To grow old alone, what nonsense is that?  
All creatures marry in pairs and come and go east, west, south, and north -  
People of this world, listen to my words.  

Flowing are tears, and sighing,  
Sighs become a peony mountain to wash clear my heart,  
Tears become rain to dry my heart,  
Oh how weary my fate.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
With nothing to do in the prime of youth,  
Is it good to be doing this in the mountains under the trap?  
Whether to do it or not, I complain about my fate,  
No one comes or goes.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Mom, mom, my dear mother  
When you gave birth to me and raised me  
Through muddy and dry places  
Through hardships and struggles  
You went to distant mountains and rivers  
Yet today, there is still no news -  

Some people have good fortunes -  
They live in grand, noble houses  
Enjoying wealth and glory -  
But how is it with me?  
Living near the slopes of Palgongsan  
Earning my living by hard labor during the day  
Gathering wild plants and herbs from the mountains and fields  
Trying to survive carrying burdens on my back -  

Looking at the mountains and rivers, they are green hills  
But my hair has turned white  
It is pitiful and sorrowful  
With my poor, needle-thin body  
A crane-like illness has struck me  
Calling for my dear mother -  
Seeking comfort in cold alcohol -  

Lying on a bamboo bed for a hundred years  
A medical pot spread out before me  
"My dear, my love" -  
Don’t mourn as I go  
Be well -  

Bidding farewell at the shrine  
Wondering what the journey to the afterlife is like  
The gate opens, and it is the afterlife.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Magumagu, Galgamaguyu  
Jirisan, Galgamaguyu  
There is a path, I will go too  
Let's go together, ehehe  
What about the trees? Let's go home  
Hey - let's go quickly, let's go quickly  
Ihuhuuu, Ihuhuuu

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hey, hey - what a lucky guy  
Living in a grand ancient mansion with curtains and decorations  
When the southeast wind blows, the sound of the curtains is loud  
This guy’s fate is miserable, everything in the world has its match  
Even shoes have pairs, and doors have pairs  
But this guy’s fate is like a worn-out shoe, I wonder why he has no match

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Going, going, I am going. If I go now, when will I come back?  
Whether I go or not, will I really go? Whether I go or not, will I really go?  
Oh youth, oh youth, do not grow old.  
You young people in your prime, don’t hold on anyway.  
When time passes, it will take you alone.  
You young people in your prime, how is it that you grow old like this?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Child—  
What kind of miserable fate is this  
To end up carrying firewood?  
Goo-ya goo-ya, to Jirisan we go  
Crow, whether you or I,  
Our fate is the same—now we’ve taken on a load  
Let’s bind it and go  
Ihu-hu-hu

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Guya Guya Gamaguya Gugu, old monk of Cheongsan  
Wearing a white-haired necklace, he heads into the mountain village  
Guya Gamaguya  

“Ihu hu hu hu hu” / Sop'al

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
A.  
Going up, going up, climbing the great rocky mountain  
Oh dear, comrades, hold me for a moment  
Swaying, swaying, going up  

B.  
Going up, going up, climbing that mountain ridge  
Always climbing that mountain ridge  
When will I carry a load of wood and come down?  
Oh dear, I am annoyed  
Some people are lucky, living well in a tall house in the old city  
Living in wealth and honor  
Why on earth is my fate like this?  
What kind of fate is this?  
Oh dear, I am annoyed, oh well—

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Baekgu, don’t leap so high, the black magpies cry and fly away.

I can’t confess my youth, I can’t confess my youth,
These days, the world’s affairs.

A man who had a stroke of luck is like a planted penis, blooming well in spring,
But the man who holds his heart tight does not bloom even after spring is gone.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Going, going, I am going  
Climbing the mountains and forests  
If at the top there are many wild herbs  
I would gather a lot  
Where should I go  
Hey, should I go to Gari or Eori?  
Climbing the mountains and forests  
If I work here today  
Tomorrow I must go to that valley  
Oh, come here, mountain  
I am, I am  
Coming down as the only grandson of another family  
Why do I have such bad luck?  
Carrying a wooden frame like a backpack into the mountain valley  
What kind of life is this?  
Hey, should I go, hey, should I go?  
I want to go even a thousand miles to Hanyang  

– Sound of the wooden frame

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Some people are born lucky  
and spend their whole lives at a desk, doing nothing,  
but because we are so ugly and unremarkable,  
we carry heavy loads day after day,  
climbing steep mountains every day.  
I can't do it, I can't do it.  
Tonight I sleep, and tomorrow again  
I climb another famous mountain.  
No matter how much I think about it, I just can't do it.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hey carrier, hey carrier  
Whether you carry a load or haul badly,  
When God created humans,  
There was not much distinction,  
But why is this fellow’s fate just fate—what sin caused this fate?  
Every daybreak, carrying a shoulder pole and rake on his back,  
What is this talk about the ancestral burial mound?  
Hey farmers, listen,  
You clear that valley, I’ll clear this valley,  
Tearing and scratching at broken brushwood and fallen leaves,  
Dragging and pulling hard,  
With all your strength,  
Try earnestly caring for your parents and family,  
Hey carrier, whether you carry a load or haul badly.

— The sound of wooden clogs on a shoulder pole

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Gama-guya, gama-guya—  
Where shall I go, what shall I do—  
I have already passed sixty in this state—  
Gama-guya—  
The mountains are deep and Mount Tai is high—  
If I climb up, there will be fern shoots—  
Let’s go, let’s go, let’s go there  
If we go there, it will be late—  
Gama-guya—

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Daughter, daughter, my daughter, where are you going, my daughter?  
My daughter Bongdeok, where are you?  
Hey, daughter, daughter, my daughter,  
My daughter Bongdeok, where are you going, my daughter?  
My daughter Bongdeok, are you sleeping in the flower garden?  
Daughter, daughter, my daughter, where are you going, my daughter?  
It is an enemy, it is an enemy, a cousin enemy.  
My daughter Bongdeok, where are you going, my daughter?  
Daughter, daughter, my daughter, it is an enemy, it is an enemy.  
A cousin enemy, a cousin deceitful to me,  
No matter how many months and days I search, my daughter Bongdeok,  
Is she sleeping in the flower garden? Where are you going, my daughter?  
(Sighing sounds)

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Uh, heh-heh-ya, eh, ya
Throat is dry, chuckling,
Stomach is hungry, sticks to the back,
How did my fate come to be like this? - It turned out this way.
Mountains, rivers, and plants - all perished -
Just let the southeast wind blow - uh-heh-ya
Some people - have good fortune, in ancient grand houses - eh-hay
Woolen clothes - adorned with decorations -
The southeast wind blows - ding-dang, ding-dang - it goes
Ihu hu hu hu hu

>

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Guyah guyah galgamaguyah  
Over there, that eater, recently again an eater,  
This year, once more has eaten, gamaguyah  
Ihuhuhya  
Gamaguyah - galgamaguyah -  
One eating - this youthful life -  
Is a mother’s affection -  
Passing through all kinds of times  
I, at this moment, weep  
Ihuhuhhuya -

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Hey—  
Hey, hey, crow—  
Flying high in the sky, heading into twilight at seven hundred, quickly send word.  
Ibal 33, in the dead of night, the morning star has risen,  
Hey, the peddler’s big drum sounds, the eight provinces’ spirits dance,  
In March, apricot buds bloom, in the third lunar month the brass candlestick lights the room,  
In May, the orchid in the garden keeper’s hand holds a sword, seeking out the enemy,  
At sixty-six, flying kites, watching over the rivers and mountains of the eight provinces,  
The fringe on the braided hair sways with the southeast wind,  
Our brothers, eight brothers, study in the Hanseo Hall, waiting to pass the imperial examination in Gyeongju on the first day of the third lunar month—  
The old monk mumbling nonsense, ninety-nine prayer beads around his neck, holding a wooden clapper in his hand,  
Clacking here and there in this alley and that alley, one click, two clicks, please give two clicks—  
There’s a tiger in the Jangha forest, all the marksmen have gathered and caught the tiger,  
The spectators watching, carrying the tiger are pallbearers, the bearers of lanterns are the torch carriers.  
Hey—  
Walking along, I picked up a needle, should I give this needle away?  
If I give it, it’s a pity, if I keep it, it’s careless.  
I threw it into the empty hall, the fishing hook was struck,  
Caught on the hook, should I give it or keep it? Giving is a pity, keeping is reckless.  
I threw it into the Amnok River.  
I caught a carp, it covered all eight provinces,  
Cut it with a sword, husband and wife sit quietly, laughing softly,  
Eating but pondering why my fate has turned to that of a farmer,  
Using weeds as food, carrying a load as a baby,  
With a clay pot as water,  
Am I watching from the tall peak of Mt. Heoboktae?  
Why is my fate like this?  
My fate as a farmer—  
Ihoohoo—

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
A: Hehehe

B: Ehei

A: I ate greens, drank water, stretched my arms, and lay down

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Aye aye aye - aye  
A nineteen-year-old old widow  
Lost her twenty-nine-year-old daughter  
Where did my daughter Bongdeok go?  
I went out to find my daughter  
Did she go this way or that way?  
No trace left at all  
When the ridge of Black Mountain passes by  
Leaving behind stripped sorghum at Jjandeusan  
There is nowhere else to go  
Oh dear, I can't live like this

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Ehe eheyi  
We are the two who made a vow, have you so easily forgotten?  
Leaving your husband, where are you going? Are you seeking a gentleman’s favor?  
Are you seeking a refined lady? Hey, are you seeking Taeeun Taesa?  
On the far, distant road of Musan, you are seeking a wild fairy.  
On the day Musan’s evening falls, you seek Baek I Suje.  
On the day Bisul Mountain’s evening falls, you seek Jeoksoja.  
The East Sea winds in winding waves, the green mountains piled layer upon layer,  
You’re saying to meet a courtesan, wandering restlessly.  

Oh, my fate, my life, what am I to do about the young child?  
In the lovely springtime of March, when all the flowers bloom in abundance,  
You may bloom again, but can the Song lady not bloom?  
In the first lunar month, azaleas—did you not see the Song lady?  
In the decorated mountains and rivers, azaleas—did you not see the Song lady?  
Picking flowers and holding them in hand, thinking of the Song lady,  
Even the most exotic flower, can it compare to the Song lady?  
Eheyei

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
My mother, my mother,  
In the high mountains and deep valleys, oh  
The moon rises over Wolchul Peak,  
The sun sets behind Ilrak West Mountain, oh  
Looking around, a myriad of thousand peaks,  
My sea is the Chilan cliff, oh  
Where has my mother gone?  
She doesn’t know to find me.  
Even the black magpies, when the sun goes down,  
When will they go to the nest?  
Passing through the small pine grove,  
Seeking the thick pine forest, oh  
Under the water, among the pine needles,  
I will go find under the rocks, oh  
Where has my mother gone?  
She doesn’t know how to find me, oh  
My mother, my mother,  
Oh, and night is dim in the early morning,  
In the stillness of the fifth lunar month, oh  
In the night moon on Gongsan, the cuckoo cries, oh  
Where has my mother gone?  
Calling “Mother, Mother,”  
I call once, no answer, oh  
I call twice, no answer, oh  
Calling three times more,  
The mountain itself seems to answer,  
My mother, my mother,  
Where has she gone? She doesn’t know how to find me, oh  
Oh, oh, my mother, oh  
I am, I am, oh  
Oh, will you come, my mother?

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Goya Galgamot Goya Jisancheon Galgamot Goya  
Oh oh oh oh oh oh oh oh oh  
Hey, the nineteen-year-old widow lost her twenty-nine-year-old daughter  
Where are you going, my daughter Bongdeok?  
Oh oh oh oh oh oh oh

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
When we were young— let’s eat a lot, rest a lot, and have fun—
You— are fortunate— living in a palace— in a big house— eating well and dressing well,
But us farmers carry heavy loads on our backs,
Limping on crutches, just complaining about our fate—

“Hee ho ho ho ho!!!”

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Jirisan, Galgamaguya, take me with you, take me with you.  
Even the great hero Qin Shi Huang could not escape death.  
The world-renowned general Chu Pa-wang also departed from this world.  
The talented poet Li Taibai is residing in the capital's mountains and rivers.  
Even Emperor Wu of Han, who sought immortality, has left this world.  
Baek Ja-cheon-seok and Gab Bun-yang have also departed from this world.  
Can heroes not die, and great men not grow old?  
Do not boast of heroes, and do not speak of great men.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Eeeeeee  
Jirijilgok Mountain, Garigal Gamaguya  
That girl over there picking herbs in the field  
In this field, the chawanmul herb has withered from frost  
Garigal, Galmagoya  
Ihuhuya

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Even a stop sign  
has a pair,  
and wooden clogs  
have a pair,  
and a pair exists  
even for playmates in childhood,  
and those flying birds  
also have a pair,  
but what kind of fate is this  
that I have?  
Lying alone in solitary confinement,  
not sleeping,  
sleep is coming.  
Lying down,  
will you come, my love?  
Neither my love nor sleep  
comes,  
only sighs and worries

Crow crow, carrion crow, carrion crow—huff huff—

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Eh—  
Time, don’t go—our lives are all growing old—if I die,  
who will look for me—  
Time, don’t go—our youth is all fading—huh-huh—huyah—yo—  
(Dialogue)  
“Ah, that tree, that tree has a lot of branches. Today, the crows are bringing lots of fortune.  
Is it going to rain now? Dark black clouds are gathering again.  
All over Hallasan mountain—huh, it really rains too often.  
Oh, over there on that ridge, there don’t seem to be many trees. Well, let’s climb one tree.”  

Hiyo—wind, strong wind, don’t blow. The west wind makes all the leaves fall, when even a big tree dies,  
the birds that used to come won’t come, and when the water becomes stagnant,  
the fish that used to come won’t come either.  
When even the flowers fall, the butterflies that used to come won’t come.  
(Dialogue)  
“Ah, over there, why are those kids climbing up like that today?  
Huh, today I have to carry a load of wood.  
Ah, so many women are coming out today, the women from Deoksan are coming up with the girls.  
What kind of mischief are they up to today, I wonder?”  

Heh—eyyo—on the mountain full of old trees—if the outside is mixed, others will know, but who knows which ones are mixed inside?  
Who would know—huh-huh-huya—huh-huh-huya.  
(Dialogue)  
“Ah, that wind is refreshing. The wind is really strong in this area.  
Spring wind or autumn wind, how refreshing it is like this.  
Women, if you go into that back valley today, you’ll find many wild greens.  
Yesterday, when I went to cut trees, there were wild greens everywhere; after that, all the women too.”  

Ehe—hihiyo—Oh-oh, Myeongsasimni, the flower of Hae-danghwa, don’t be sad because it’s withering—  
It is March of the cyclic year again—eh—oh—  
The grandmother flower on the back hill sprouted again in March of the cyclic year—  
but for people like us, why can’t we come back once we go? Why can’t we come back? It is really frustrating—ihu-huh-huya.  
Now, let’s go—ihu-huh-huya, let’s go, let’s quickly go—when my mother flew, there were twelve winding curves,  
oh, we passed every hill well.  
Ihu-huh-huya.

Huyeo - uh -

translation:

Mountain spirit crow, Kamaguya, the house is built, and my beloved’s illness deepens day by day  
I can’t live like this anymore, oh my dear, my beloved  
Barley and yellow millet in the suongnyeon, and wheat flour for the hind legs…  
Oh beloved, my beloved, where have you gone leaving me behind?  
My mother, I... I was nurtured and raised by eating the Samsinpan’s sickly rice gruel  
What is this sickle and scythe business?  
Guya Guya, Kamaguya, mountain spirit crow builds the house and caws,  
But my beloved’s illness deepens day by day  
I can’t live like this anymore  
Oh beloved, my dear  
You came when you left, only making a fleeting sound as you went up  
You only come at the memorial ceremony, but you didn’t even come then  
At the Si-eol-ri Sangdal, the year of the grudge,  
On the day my beloved left, every year, month by month, he comes and goes,  
But my beloved, where have you gone? It’s been over ten years, and you still do not come  
Guya Guya, Kamaguya, a heron in the clear sky, flying high in the void, fluttering and crying  
Where has my beloved gone? Won’t you come even this time?  
Guya Guya, Kamaguya, I can’t live like this anymore  
The mountains, the sky, and those countless stars shine only upon me  
But in the midst of the drifting clouds, this life  
Life’s destiny is miserable, now with white hair, what is there left to do?

This path leads to mountain trails, and that way winds through thorny bushes.  
Arirang, Arirang, Aririyo, let’s have some fun and then go.  

That wild mustard field over there was barren last year and again this year, just like me.  
Arirang, Ariari, Arariyo, Arirang, let’s cross over and go.  

This alley, that alley, going down deep valleys, my fate only shrivels as I pass by.  
Arirang, Arirarang, my life, when will it blossom brightly like a flower?  

It’s no use, no use, no use, you and I are destined never to play together.  
Arirang, Ariri, Arariyo, let’s gently pass over the Arirang pass.

label: Lament_eosayong
translation:
Mom, mom, my dear mother  
When you gave birth to me and raised me,  
Through muddy and dry places,  
Through hardships, you raised me.  
You went to the distant mountains and rivers,  
But today, there is still no news—  

Some people have good fortune—  
Living in grand, spacious houses,  
Enjoying wealth and honor—  
But why is it that I  
Live near Palgong Mountain,  
Working from dawn to dusk,  
Struggling to survive with the plants and grasses of the land,  
Carrying my burden on a shoulder pole, trying to make a living—  

Looking at the mountains and rivers, they are green hills,  
But my hair has turned white,  
How pitiful and sorrowful it is.  
My poor body is as thin as a needle,  
Afflicted with a stork-like illness,  
The one calling is my dear mother—  
The one searching is a drunken wanderer—  

At the hundred-year-old coffin by the headfield,  
Laying out the medicinal bath vessels,  
My dear, my dear beloved—  
Don’t lament that I’m leaving,  
Stay well—  

After bidding farewell at the village shrine,  
As for the path to the afterlife,  
When the gate opens, that is the journey to the other world.

Ehee - now the sun sets in the western mountains

translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
No matter how hard the married life is,  
Even if the chili pepper is said to be spicy,  
It’s even spicier than that.  
I didn’t know for three years,  
Went deaf for three years,  
Became a burdensome person for three years.  
After living for three years, three more years, and yet another three years,  
This head, like a three-layered skirt,  
Has become like a pig’s tail.  
This wrist, like a burning fire,  
Has become like a sharp blade.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Just three days after coming to the in-laws’ house, they say I look like a weed.
They cover the ridges of the rice paddies with soil.
Is this how they treat the daughter-in-law in this house?
“That’s how the brother-in-law is.”
Child, child, wash your hands in the rice field and go inside the house.
When I came inside what they call the house, I didn’t know if it was my husband or my lord, but he was lying down.
Dear, dear, my husband, lying on the straw bed over the drying racks.
When will you wear a fine hemp garment and a impressed cloth robe? / Sopal

translation:
Mother, Mother, our mother,  
Did you give birth to me to be great?  
When he was born, I was born too,  
When I was born, he was born too.  
Why then am I so weary like this?

Mother, Mother, our mother,  
Did you give birth to me to be great?  
What kind of person am I,  
Having lived like a decent human in the world?  
Is this what it means to be called "I"?  
When he was born, I was born too,  
When I was born, he was born too,  
But did I not have the fortune of parents?  
Having met poor parents,  
Is this why I live like this?  
Mother, Mother, our mother,  
Even pitifulness itself is pitiful.

—Hunggul Song

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even though Baekdu Mountain is high, it cannot be as loud as the father-in-law’s voice.  
Even though a whale or tiger is scary, it cannot be as frightening as the mother-in-law’s voice.  
Even though the full moon is bright, it cannot be as bright as the father-in-law’s eyes.  
Even though trams and trains are fast, they cannot be as fast as the sister-in-law’s mouth.  
Even though the vast fields are wide, they cannot be as wide as my husband’s bike basket.  
“That’s the way it is whenever we meet.”

translation:
I called, yes I called, I called out to an old song.  
What use is it to dwell on past stories from long ago?  
Back when I was living as a daughter-in-law, the in-laws were harsh and critical,  
But now the world is better, a world where I live as I please, so what else can I do?  
Let's go pick mulberry leaves, let's go pick mulberry leaves, let's go to the mountain to pick mulberry leaves.  
Old man, old woman, I'm going to pick mulberry leaves, don't say you're hungry and can't pick them.  
Living as a daughter-in-law was too harsh, this is how it is for me.  
Dear, dear, oh dear, no, no, I can't play around.

Am I a cow to give you beef?  
If I send out pressed rice,  
Am I a dog to give you a dog?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother,  
Raised me to be respectable.  
This world is full of difficulties and hardship,  
How is it that I live so poorly?  
Mother, mother, our mother,  
Don’t you know how I live?  
Where has our mother gone,  
Leaving me alone to live like this?  
Not knowing this world is a proper world,  
I live unaware.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after getting married,  
I went into the kitchen,  
Caught a poisonous snake,  
Wrapped it in a straw rope,  
Tied a big bamboo stick around it,  
Climbed up the back hill,  
Picked bracken fern from the sunny side,  
Picked bracken fern from the shady side,  
Came back home,  
Laid out the sunny bracken ferns to dry in the sun,  
Laid out the shady bracken ferns to dry in the shade,  
Cooked the morning meal,  
Opened the love gate,  
The dog-like father-in-law  
Washed his headcloth and  
Had the morning meal,  
Opened the main room door,  
The bitch-like mother-in-law  
Washed her headcloth and then  
Had the morning meal,  
Opened the back room door,  
The old man-like husband  
Washed his headcloth and  
Had the morning meal,  
Opened the front room door,  
The fox-like sisters-in-law  
Had sunburns on their buttocks,  
Washed their headcloths and  
Had the morning meal,  
Tore the outer jacket to make a bag,  
Tore the jacket to fold a cone-shaped hat,  
Wore the folded cone hat,  
And goes on a 100-day prayer pilgrimage  
To Mount Geumgang, 128,049 hermitages,  
Praying to have sons and daughters.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother– Brother’s cousin– Brother,  
How was living with your in-laws?

Hey, Dong-sang, stop saying that—  
Even hot peppers are spicy, but living with in-laws is spicy.

Once you go,  
you can’t come back–

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In the front field, I plant skewers  
In the back field, I plant garlic  
The garlic is spicy like a bee sting  
Like a sister-in-law, it’s spicy and painful  
Dungdangae, all dungdangae  
Dangae dungdangae dungdangae all  
If you go to the mountain, it’s a thorn enemy  
If you go to the field, it’s a weed enemy  
When someone comes home, it’s a sister-in-law enemy  
Gathering them all in one place  
Just like a fence—-  
Under the roof, there is a spring well  
A big child washing clothes  
Let us pray, let us pray  
Let us pray for a drop of tears

label: Lament_lament
translation:
I met my husband when I was eighteen,
Living on a simple veranda, this is how I live in the world.
I just look at him and sigh, this is my life,
Eating meals, this is my life.
Sigh, sigh, I sigh again, no, no, I cannot play.
Having given birth to five boys, scattering them all around,
My son and I live alone in my house.
Sigh, sigh, I sigh again, no, no, I cannot play.
Raising my grandson without a mother until his hundredth day,
How must a wife's heart feel? Rotten inside and outside,
This is how I live, sigh, sigh, I sigh again.

translation:
My mother-in-law's body odor is so bad.
How could she give birth to someone like me and bring me here?
If she brought me here, she might as well have stir-fried me.
Stir-frying this, stir-frying that, stir-frying like beans,
I lived like this until today.

translation:
Mother, mother, crying mother,  
Did you give birth to me to be fashionable?  
If I fly well, does that mean I was born well?  
If I can’t fly, does that mean I was born poorly?  
If I serve the father-in-law,  
Or if I serve the mother-in-law,  
No matter what, I cannot live.  

In the barley field, the enemy  
Is the floodwater, the enemy.  
In the millet field, the enemy  
Is the withering heart, the enemy.  
No matter what, I cannot live.  

Living with the in-laws is a hardship.  
Whether I live this thought or not,  
Shall I drown in the Daedong River and die?  
No matter what, I cannot live.  
Living with the in-laws, I cannot live.

translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is life in your in-laws' house?

Even if chili peppers are spicy,  
Is it worse than living in the in-laws' house?  
This head of hair, like triple-layered,  
After living three years with the in-laws,  
Has become like a pig's tail.  
A face once as beautiful as white jade,  
Has all been darkened by the sunlight.

translation:
Sung-ah, Sung-ah, cousin Sung-ah, how was the life of a married woman living with her in-laws?  
On the wooden floor, it was hard to place the spoon.  
Even filling a small bowl with watermelon was difficult.  
After death, even speaking to the brother-in-law was hard.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Don’t come, don’t come, mother-in-law, you catch my eye.
Mother-in-law, you catch my eye, but you naturally catch my husband’s eye.
If you naturally catch my husband’s eye, then you catch the neighbor’s eye.
If you catch the neighbor’s eye, then you catch the village people’s eye.
If you catch the village people’s eye, even the leftover rice will only last a short while.

The lord of the house takes the male line, owning the house and the fields.
Parents claim the thousand pieces of gold; siblings claim ten thousand pieces of silver.
But I, a woman, with the dowry and household goods, claim my own share.

The wild goose flies away crying in the new spring wind and the cold wind.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mom, mom, my dear mom, lovingly raised me.
Did she raise me to give me away? I want to see her, I want to see her.
I want to see my mom, my mom, on the cold winter days,
Did she prepare boiled meat for me? I want to see it thoroughly.
Did my mom prepare chicken for me on the cold winter days?
I also fondly remember the sweet honey. On the cold winter days,
Did she prepare fish for me? I want to see the fish too.
Did my mom prepare wild chives for me on the cold winter days?
I also want to see the fresh greens. On the cold winter days,
Did she sit cross-legged on a mat? I also think of the winding paths.

translation:
Three days after coming to the in-laws' house, the new husband left.
He leaned next to the flower basket and headed to the back hill.
The climbing fern is the climbing fern you knew,
Snapping it off one by one, a little goes into the stone pot.
Oh softly, in boiling water, lightly boil the arirang,
Place the silver ladle and silver knife,
Place the brass ladle and brass knife,
In the brass bowl, layer softly, in the silver bowl, layer softly.
In the silver bowl, place the silver knife, in the brass bowl, place the brass knife.

Father, please get up, get up and have breakfast.
Father-in-law, see how he moves,
He's mixing, he's mixing,
Mixing because the greens are new,
Then turn around and go back.
Open the big room door,
Mother-in-law though the years,
Please get up and have breakfast,
See how mother-in-law moves,
She's mixing, she's mixing,
Mixing because the rice is dry,
Then turn around and go back.
Though the years, brother-in-law,
Please get up and have breakfast,
See how brother-in-law moves,
He's mixing, he's mixing,
Mixing because the scorched rice is dry.

translation:

Life as a bride is good, but the mistress of the house is strict.
It is difficult to speak.

Did I come to that room just to be treated like this?"  
The mother-in-law said.

Remaining faithful is difficult. In the village of Jungwoo,  
In-law relationships are hard to talk about.  
Filling round, round watermelons,  
Even filling meals is difficult.  
At the tilted hat house,  
In a rotting house exposed to rain and snow,  
In a house with a thousand dragons and a hundred tigers.

translation:
Over there, in the dry field,

Catch that magpie,  
Its hind legs trembling and shaking,  
Its throat clear, chest wide like a great gentleman,  
Its folded wings stretched out,  
Like our noble one.  
If the five viscera and six entrails rot,  
Then let me eat and rot as well.

translation:

Gona Hey  
Some people are born lucky  
A noble family with a tall, luxurious house lived in wealth and glory  
But we carry a shoulder pole day and night  
Climbing up the mountain, we go to the mountain pass  
Aiyo, oh dear, oh dear, this annoyance is unbearable, hey  

B.  
Deep, deep, if it is deep, come into my arms  
The pillow is high and long, so adjust to my heart, then stretch out your arms  
Your love and my affection will have a deep sleep, hey  

A.  
Over the fence, over the wall, that young man  
If you have some sense, take the rice cake from my hand and eat it  
Aiyo, oh dear, oh dear, this annoyance is unbearable, hey  

B.  
Dream, dream, merciless dream, the dream that comes with my beloved  
Don’t send away my coming beloved, just sleep soundly, hey  

-Hungtaryeong  
-Yukjabaegi

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Cousin, cousin,
How is living in your in-laws' house?
Living in the in-laws' house is good,
But I can't stand it because of my mother-in-law.
In the round, round neighborhood,
It's hard to keep one's chastity.
Because of my ruthless aunt-in-law,
It's hard to speak freely.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In the early spring season of March, flowers bloom on the flowered mountain,  
and leaves grow on the green mountain.  
The golden oriole flits back and forth on the willow branches,  
but where has my beloved gone,  
with not a single visit in sight? / Sop’al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Cousin in sight, cousin in sight  
How is the married life?  
On the turning board,  
Placing the spoon is affectionate.  
The sister-in-law who is half-crazy,  
Even speaking is affectionate.  
The brother-in-law who is half-crazy,  
Even speaking is affectionate.  
Round and plump little cooking pot,  
Filling it with rice is affectionate.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
When I was young, there was none like you  
Did you raise me in a family like this?  
Try putting on straw sandals  
Wearing a worn belt and new shoes  
They say it’s sticky, very sticky  
When you wear new shoes  
They say even the stickiness is sticky  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Life is something that comes and goes  
It lasts only for a moment then  
Did you raise me in a place like this?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
Stop singing flower songs and leave,  
Don’t even mention the hardships of married life,  
The flower-patterned outer garment’s buttons,  
Are all falling off from constant polishing,  
Here and there, rough treatment,  
Grievances will surely build up.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
I can't live like this, I can't live like this  
An old widower can't live like this  
I have five daughters, and  
I sent them all away  
To do the laundry alone,  
To cook meals, I can't live like this  
Who should I blame for this fate?  
Oh, oh, my miserable fate  
Please, old lady,  
Take me away tonight at least  
You wicked woman of the world  
From black hair to white hair  
I kept telling you to live, live  
And yet, so empty-handed,  
How could you say you left?  
I'm going to die, I'm going to die  
Please take me away tonight

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother,  
You left me to be stylish.  
In this world as precious as a prize,  
Am I the only one living like this?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is life in the in-laws' house?  
If only I had kept a half-dozen measures of rice,  
Both you and I could have eaten,  
When the pressed rice comes out,  
Would you give some to me, even though it’s yours?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At the fortress, at the fortress, at the fortress of Nombak,  
Don’t pray for me to come.  
If only a cup of rice was given,  
The fortress would eat, and I would eat.  
Their dogs are given plenty,  
Our dogs are given scraps.  
Their dogs die full,  
Our dogs starve to death.  
The river has flooded, the river has flooded,  
Beyond the rain ridge, the river has flooded.  
The lower water river is called a river,  
A pair of ducks, a pair of geese,  
They fly away in pairs.  

—Sounds of a folk song

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, daughter-in-law, mother  
What good is it if you only stitch the hem?  
The newlywed who was very blessed  
Received a betrothal gift and died  
The betrothal gift is received and hung before the ancestral tablet  
Thirty-two Jewish soldiers  
March in step and make a sound

label: Lament_lament
translation:
After living with my mother-in-law, I found there was yet another mother-in-law.  
After living with the oldest mother-in-law, I found there was a father-in-law.  
After living with the father-in-law, I found the child’s in-laws remained.  
After living with the child’s in-laws, the miserable and wretched household was gone without a trace. /Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was living in your in-laws’ house?
Living in my in-laws’ house was good, but it was difficult to place the sujae on the small wooden board.
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was living in your in-laws’ house?
Living in my in-laws’ house was good, but it was hard to talk to the brother-in-law who was a bit blunt.
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was living in your in-laws’ house?
It was difficult to cook rice with watermelon seeds scattered evenly.
It was difficult to place the sujae on the small wooden board.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sister, sister, how is life as a daughter-in-law during adolescence?  
Don't say anything, don't say anything.  
Even if the rooster’s tail is spicy, is it spicier than life as a daughter-in-law?  
Heavens above, could such a thing really happen?  
I would rather borrow a little bowl of rice in the fields.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The mountain is harsh and the water is harsh, words cannot be spoken, a deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river, and when I lose someone, I lose a part of myself too.  
When others lose someone, I lose someone as well. How could I not serve my husband faithfully despite this harsh fate?  
My poor husband, do not go—who will raise our young children? What sin do they bear in their youth? I just gaze up at the sky,  
thinking of my husband. When I think about it, I realized what my husband’s love truly was, but before I could fully understand, you passed away.  
How can I possibly raise this young, immature child alone? Ah, my grief…  
In this neighborhood alley, I wonder if my husband is here. Every day, whenever the sun rises, I think of my husband; even when looking at the moon, I think of him.  
I waited anxiously, hoping my husband would come home, but he has gone beyond this world. The cruel attachment remains even as I try to forget; no matter how much I steel my heart,  
your image from yesterday and today still appears vividly in my eyes.  
How could you leave me alone and go where you went?  
My in-laws complain morning and evening, my sister-in-law is troublesome, my brother-in-law is frantic,  
I carefully watch my behavior while trusting only my husband. With a single heart, I vowed to love you always,  
but why did you leave me and go beyond this world? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear.  
If I had known you were going to leave me, I would have built a fortress at the edge of the world where you went,  
If I had known it would come to this, I would have called a shaman to perform rites and exorcisms, to try to save you.  
I never imagined you would go beyond this world. They say that place beyond is better than this life; if I had known,  
every morning and evening I would have drawn holy water and prayed with my hands clasped, asking my husband not to die.  
Why did you leave me so heartlessly? Even today, I think of you. On the cold winds of winter’s end and the snow-filled solstice,  
the west winds of Bukcheongsan blow fiercely downward. That harsh winter has passed, and spring has come.  
The nightingale sings lightly and deeply, crying, and the mountains and trees—even dead wood—revive, sprouting leaves and flowers,  
but when will my departed husband come? Without a word, you torment me so.  
It is frustrating and painful; I cannot speak of it before me. A deep grudge arises, my heart burns like a winding river.  
Coal, anthracite, bituminous coal, straw coal, bear’s fat—when burning, they produce smoke and steam, but my longing for my husband burns without any smoke or steam, only sorrow flows quietly like a droplet.  
Who understands this bruised liver? Oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, my dear, oh, so dear, oh, my dear.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In a house as high as the sky, in a house as deep as the underground, in a family of five,

With just one word, it was said that the country ate old mullet roe on a wet day.

It was said that the day the country was broken, Yang Geum-dae was broken.

To die, to die, taking nine kinds of medicine and sleeping as if dead.

To die by drowning deep in silver and jade waters.

To die by hanging from nine strands of hemp rope.

In the clan, in the clan, in my ancestral shrine, in the clan.

Seoji-ae was studying and died, died.

The wife, like a sparrow, drowned in the deep silver jade water and died.

Holding a cold day by my side, holding a six-day period in my hand, sharing a cup of old wine.

The big room’s door must be opened because mother and father were sitting there.

The small room’s door must be opened, but the wife, like a sparrow, is gone as if she were sleeping.

The gold and embroidered blanket was shared by two, but the warm blanket was left alone and gone.

The mandarin duck quilt and pine pillow were shared by two, but the warm pillow was left alone and gone.

Gathering the book cover, packing the book; gathering the clothes cover, packing the clothes; preparing a wedding bed, laying out the bread.

Child, child, little child, hurry and finish eating and cleanse yourself.

Mother and father, if you’re really going out, hey, to be safe, stay there, go over there, go to that house!

In a house without walls and fences, a refined lady is sleeping.

What was done with the first wife, will it be like this with the second wife?

As the frost returns, a rare bird with no nest perches on my shoulders.

If you go, that’s the end; if I go, it’s the afterlife.

Is it your fault, or my fault?

Is it the fault of your parents, or the fault of your siblings?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, how is married life?  
Even if married life is hard, the chili pepper is even spicier.  
Please deliver a letter to that goose flying over there.  
When my older brother received it, he talked about the mountain village dialect.  
When my father received the letter, he was deeply sorrowful like Mount Taesan.  
When my mother received it, her crying echoed loudly.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
If a mountain dies, does it have a grave?  
If a magnetic surface dies, does it have a magnet?  
Is there rage and fury?  
Is there a field of broom plants?  
If it dies, does it have a grave?  
It's my fate, it's my fate.

translation:
A.
Going up, going up
Climbing the mountain of hardship

Using a cane, I climb up
What a fortunate person’s fate
Living well in a high and grand house
With wealth and glory
Why is my fate so miserable?
What is this situation?

B.
Going up, going up
Climbing the mountain and stream of Seongjeok
Quickly crossing this mountain and stream
Entering the deep valley
Gathering medicinal herbs to eat
Hastily carrying a load of wood
Let us return home

Why waste such effort?
What a fortunate person’s fate
Living well in a high and grand house
With wealth and honor

When others were born, I was also born
But why did our parents have to bring me into this world
What a fortunate person’s fate
Living well in a high and grand house
With wealth and honor
Why is my destiny like this?
It’s lamentable, it’s lamentable
Lamenting toward my parents
What can I do, what shall I do?
What shall I do with my life?
I pray, I pray
I pray to God

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Going up, going up  
Carrying a shoulder pole and crutches  
Climbing up a high mountain path  
Some people are born lucky  
With a grand house in Odae-gwangsil  
Living in wealth and prosperity  
But this fellow’s fate is hard  
Carrying a shoulder pole and wooden clappers  
Singing a mournful song as he goes  
Where will I go to cut wood?  
Such a frustrating life  
Oh, woe is my fate  
This miserable life of mine  
Who would understand it?  
Oh, woe is my fate  

Horse: Oh, where shall I go to cut wood? Where will I go to cut wood?  

I’m about to burst, can’t live like this  
Even if I go empty-handed  
My master will chase me away  
I won’t even get to eat supper  
This miserable life of mine is pitiful  

Horse: Come on, stop. Wherever it is, diligently load a bundle of wood and carry it home. There’s no other choice. Quickly, quickly, let’s go.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, oh brother, how difficult is married life under the in-law's roof.  
At first, the wound burned, and then, hanging on the end of the pole,  
coming and going, my tears soak me through.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Is the sickness from my own heart,  
Or a sickness given by the people of the world?  
Is it a small fire burning,  
A sickness born from hating me?  
Is this what "modoga golbaengi" means?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The front mountain is layered, and the back mountain is layered too,  
So where does the soul go? Where is the afterlife?  
Is it really that easy to go? If it is so easy,  
Then you shouldn't have come out in the first place, or if you came, you should just leave.  
Leaving behind a hundred-year name on the place you lived,  
Though the one leaving will forget everything,  
The friends left in this world will weep for a hundred years.  
If anyone knew who it was that wept, even if they roamed the world,  
Where could they meet again, those heartless and cruel spirits?  
If youth had taken my wife away, and wandered far and wide,  
Even if I entered a cage, I wouldn't forget her—would it be just this fate?  
To become a traveler to the afterlife at twenty-three,  
Could we live without parting?  
Ah, ah, the grief pours out, and tears flow.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The roof made by Jaeduchi  
Built for two to sleep under,  
But one lies alone,  
Is my love coming or is the guest coming?  
Tears flowed all night long.  
The roof becomes a cow beyond,  
The shoulder becomes a river beyond,  
A pair of ducks, a pair of geese,  
All flowed towards the Daedong River in Pyongyang.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Hiya hiya cousin hiya, how is the life of a married woman?
It's really hard to place the spoon on the spinning lid.
It's really hard to serve rice in round, round watermelon-shaped bowls.
Hiya hiya cousin hiya, who got mad saying "you came"?
Do you get mad because I came? If there's just half a bowl of rice,
You eat and I eat too, even if there is leftover water.
I give your cow that's nearby, but do I give my cow that's far away?
Even if the scorched rice is burnt, I give your dog that's nearby,
Do I give my dog that's far away?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Hung-ah, Hung-ah  
Cousin Hung-ah  
Living in the in-laws' house,  
How was it?  
Living in the in-laws' house—  
That's what she told me.  
On the wooden floor,  
Even placing the spoon  
Was difficult.  
Hey, hey, don’t say that—  
Living in the in-laws' house—  
The mother-in-law  
Even stuck her toes out  
And glared,  
The eldest son-in-law  
And the younger son-in-law,  
The mother-in-law’s sister-in-law,  
The mother-in-law’s sister-in-law,  
Look at the sister-in-law’s eyes—  
The sister-in-law’s eyes  
Are like a full moon,  
Even brighter,  
If you ask why,  
Because when you go in,  
It feels like being trapped in a jade prison.  
Looking at the loom,  
Feels like staring at a well,  
And the needles—  
Looking at them,  
It’s like a sewing needle,  
You can’t live like that,  
You can’t live like that.  
The eldest son went to Miryang,  
The steed went to gamble,  
The small boat went under the water,  
Living somehow or other,  
After living in the in-laws' house,  
I managed to live my first normal day.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
Trying to be stylish, pushing me forward  
Making me do all the things I can’t do  
In times of hardship, I gave birth too  
In times of hardship, others gave birth as well  
Because of the sin of being childless in a past life  
Is this why I endure this hardship?  
What kind of person is truly lucky?  
Who attains wealth and honor?  
Because of the sin of being childless in this life  
We must all live through this harsh and difficult world  
Will God even know?  
Which person endures such hardship like this?  
Which person calls it toil?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At my parents' house, it used to be a rice tail and a tied bundle,  
but after a stranger came, it’s like dog food or acorn jelly,  
washed in water and plucked off, fluttering here and there,  
stirring me this way and that, am I a fighting rooster or a lost soul?  
Crying by day, crying by night.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sister, dear sister, cousin sister,  
How can I endure this married life?  
Oh dear, don’t even mention it.  
I pick up the torn cloth and throw it away,  
They don’t even let me have dinner,  
So I spend the night outside in tears.  
I can’t go to my parents’ house,  
If I go, I feel like I’ll drown,  
So I can’t go to my parents’ house.  
I wander here and there all night,  
Spending my days in tears.  
Oh, my child,  
Though I want to hold and carry you,  
I can’t carry or hold you because they don’t allow me.  
Oh dear sister, don’t even talk about it.  
“Oh dear, I’ve forgotten and it’s all messed up.”

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother  
I tried to be admirable  
But life as a daughter-in-law is hard  
I gave birth to a son born in the Year of the Rat  
Even though I gave birth to a son born in the Year of the Rat  
Life as a daughter-in-law is hard

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Under Namsan, by Namdoreong  
Even if all the plants on Namsan wither  
The deutzia bushes must not die  
Plant them now and grow them next year  
Let them bend with the falling rain  
Bending the branches, bending the leaves  
Bending all the sleeves and hems  
Leaving a needle under the inner sleeve  
That little bent thing there  
That, too, is precious  
Having been senior at the village school  
Going to this room and that room, all around  
Entering the stitched quilt room  
The hardship of married life  
What kind of thing is taking a nap?  
Bending with the falling rain  
Going down to the jade rice bowl  
Catching the wealthy in half-hearted attempts  
Wrapping straw horns with small pieces and eating gently  
They say the sleeping place is gone

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The leaves bloom as Cheongsan, and the flowers bloom as Hwasan.  
My body goes nowhere but Jeolgol.  
Though the old sheep is not sorrowful, the old ox is indeed sorrowful.  
Myeongsashimri Hae-danghwa, do not be sorrowful because your flowers are falling.  
Did I want to lose? I must always be unwavering; I have lost.  

(Sewing song?)  
In the world or at Mingyeong, pouring plum blossom syrup into a jade cup,  
Even if I quilt a lambskin jacket sleeve or a top,  
My beloved neither comes nor sleeps, and the rooster crows loudly.  
Neither holy water nor shamans' prayers help.  
No need for five layers of silk satin, nor five layers of fine silk.  
I embrace the eternal farewell and go forth.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The Seonglo flower marries, and the pear flower goes to the market,
Teeth are falling out, applying patches, adorning the head, and wearing makeup.
Baekdu Mountain, don’t be dazed; Cheongsan, don’t laugh.
When one furrow turns, the kid goat dances.
When two furrows turn, the black sparrow flutters.
When three furrows turn, the weaver weaves the warp.
Turning back home, mournful cries resound. / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
You said it would be good if your mother-in-law died,
Then you remembered the barley pounding and watering the rice field.

On the day the sun set and faded, where will you go, acting like a flower petal?
If you are going to your concubine's house, at least see me die before you go.
My home is a flower garden, and your home is a pond.
Flowers and butterflies last only one spring season, but longing and jealousy last all four seasons. /Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At one year old, my mother passed away; at two years old, my father passed away.  
Who will live a life of gratitude? Father and son come and go.  
When I went to the in-laws’ house,  
My husband, like the sky,  
Scolded me for being small,  
Scolded me for being short.  

Look at my mother-in-law’s behavior,  
As she went out slowly,  
She scolded me for being small,  
She scolded me for being short.  

In the main room, father was  
Opening the glass door with sunlight coming in,  
He washed his face in the wash basin,  
And ate breakfast.  

Oh, you wicked woman,  
You keep it all for yourself and throw it to the dogs.  

In the inner room, sister-in-law was  
Opening the glass door with sunlight fading,  
She washed her face in the wash basin,  
And ate breakfast.  

You stingy, miserly woman,  
Walking around like a plate,  
Keep it all for yourself and give it to the dogs.  
Such bitterness, such bitterness.  

I’ll take care of the bitterness,  
Going into a poem,  
The older person sleeps,  
The younger person wears new clothes.  

Oh, middle person, oh great middle person,  
Please cut this hair for me.  
Cutting doesn’t matter much,  
But I can’t cut the hair of the counselor — he’s difficult, very difficult.  

Please cut this hair for me,  
After cutting one side of my hair,  
I start thinking of my family’s home.  
After cutting even that side,  
I start thinking more of my family’s home.  

Oh, middle person, oh great middle person,  
With 108 beads around my neck,  
Please take me to my family’s home.  
Please take me, please take me.  
The daughter is out washing clothes,  
The daughter-in-law is requesting a ride.  

Oh, middle person, oh great middle person,  
To the forest fields, to the bamboo grove,  
When I went, no one was there.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sung-ah, Sung-ah, cousin brother-in-law,  
How is it living in the husband's house?  
Living in the husband's house is difficult.  
The rolling pin is the father-in-law,  
The pestle is the mother-in-law,  
The bean pod is the uncle-in-law.  
On the turning wheel,  
Putting the finishing touches is difficult.  
Round and round, the catbird,  
Filling the rice bowl is difficult.  
The bare father-in-law,  
Even speaking is difficult.  
When coming to the husband's house,  
The load of twenty-two years piled up,  
The carpenter searched for the timber,  
Wiping tears, everything rotted.  
The cutlass man is the new son,  
The doorman is the generous son,  
The remaining rice cake, injeolmi, is now fine,  
The cold rice cake is topped,  
The leftover radish at the daughter-in-law’s place, and the remaining eggplants of the common variety,  
When three years pass, son and daughter are served, and when the in-law is born,  
Living in the husband's house is difficult.  
Sung-ah, Sung-ah, cousin Sung-ah,  
Living in the husband's house is just like that.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The brother is coming, the brother is coming, coming through Bungokgae  
Who should go to meet the brother? I, like a half moon, will go  
What kind of half moon are you? You are a crescent moon, not a half moon  
Brother, what will you eat?  
Red bean paste like a cherry in rice like milk from an outer family  
The climbing baby fish, the descending baby fish, laid out in pieces  
The house in front brings a plate of porridge, the house behind brings a plate of porridge, all placed on the brother’s table  
Brother, brother, young brother, how is married life?  
Married life is good, but the triple-layered hairdo looks like a pig’s tail  
The hem of the skirt used to wipe tears is all worn out  
The ramie jacket used to wipe sweat is all worn out  
The hands, as delicate as flowers, why do they look like a hoe handle?  
The straw sandals worn in Piyang, why do they look like royal straw sandals?  
The flower-like face of a delicate girl blooms like water parsley flowers  
The triple-layered hairdo looks like a pig’s tail  
The delicate hands look like hoe handles

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother is coming, brother is coming  
Coming through Bungogae  
Who will go to meet brother?  
Like a half moon, I will go  
Aren't you a half moon?  
The waxing crescent is the half moon  
Brother, brother, cousin brother  
How was your married life?  
Hey, hey, don't even talk about frostbite  
Married life lasted three years  
Row upon row of millet porridge  
Covered in tears and snot, all worn out  
Brother, what side dishes do you make?  
Braken under the shade  
Braken on the sunny side  
Rice like the Oe clan’s meal  
Next door’s dotjuk, dotjuk  
Our house’s dotjuk, dotjuk  
Dotjuk, dotjuk, row upon row of millet porridge  
It all went to brother’s side dishes

label: Lament_lament
translation:
When my mother gave birth to me, did she sleep with the royal sword spirit?  
Modi Modi, only bitterness accumulates.

- Heunggeul Taryeong  
>

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is life after marriage?  
Hey, don’t even mention those old stories.  
They say married life is good,  
But after three years of marriage,  
A head like a triple-layered knot,  
Has become like a twisting dance.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
(Cousin, cousin, cousin  
How is the life as a daughter-in-law?  
Like a three-tiered cake,  
It has become like a pig's tail.  
That’s how life as a daughter-in-law is.  
Like being pricked with a needle through the door crack,  
Cousin, it’s that harsh.)

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Stop it, you can't even do this.  
Go into my room,  
open the wardrobe,  
take out the twelve-panel skirt,  
tear off one panel,  
make a monk's robe,  
give the remaining panel to the bag,  
make clothes for the other monk,  
then go up slowly,  
"Head disciple, please shave my head."  
After shaving one corner,  
thoughts of my parents naturally arise,  
after shaving the last part,  
thoughts of my beloved naturally arise.  
That’s when I realized the place,  
went to see, only three years have passed,  
but since they left, it’s become a field of mugwort.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seong-a, Seong-a, cousin Seong-a, how was it living with your in-laws?  
Living with in-laws is good, but  
it’s hard to embroider such a small piece of cloth.  
It’s even difficult to speak about the widow’s clothing after the husband’s death.  
Hing-a, Hing-a, our Hing-a, how was it living with your in-laws?  
Where flowers used to bloom, no flowers bloom anymore.

Holding a drink, I climbed up Yeongnamnu in Miryang,  
Was it Yongdusan or Myungwol? By the Namcheon River, the clear wind and bright moon—endless clear wind and bright moon—  
I am now a person without a loved one. Oh, how nice, wonderful,  
What else is there to do but enjoy it?  
If it’s this good, I will have a daughter. Oh, how nice, wonderful.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sunga, Sunga, all right Sunga  
If I had just one cup of rice  
You would eat, and I would eat  
If there was leftover dishwater  
I would give my cow in the yard  
Not the cow far away  
If there was leftover scorched rice  
I would give my dog in the yard  
Not the dog far away  
Your family is rich  
Covering the gate with mulberry paper  
Our family is poor  
Covering it with factory silk  
Your family is rich  
Decorating with wooden plates  
Our family is poor  
Decorating with brass plates

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother Seong, cousin Seong,  
Do not worry just because I came out.  
If you set aside just one cup of rice,  
Seong's family can eat, and I can eat too.  
If the holiday water flows away,  
Is it Seong's matter or mine?  
If the rice crust goes away,  
Is it Seong's matter or mine?  
If the radish greens go away,  
Is it Seong's chicken or mine?  
Seong's house is in a prosperous village,  
They tie a crossbar with a protective rope.  
My house is in a poor village,  
We tie a protective rope with watercress.  
Seong's house is in a prosperous village,  
They build the fence with yeast cakes.  
My house is in a poor village,  
We build the fence with brass plates.  
Seong's house is prosperous,  
They hang ornaments on their ears.  
My house is poor,  
If I hang ornaments on my ears,  
When the southeast wind blows strongly,  
The sound of the ornaments is said to be even more pleasant.

>

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even if living in a husband’s family is good, the real pleasure is in showing love.  
Giving a small portion of rice cake like a jujube to the mother-in-law,  
When she orders me around saying the rice is not enough, the child given and the newly born bird,  
They went to the study room and came back, only listening to the parents’ words.  
Why do they put away the black rod and only hold the white rod looking at me?  
During the long, long months of February, March, and April, starving at lunch and weaving hemp,  
Leaving off hand in hand and stepping foot to foot, they kick me.  
Even tiny threads can hold all kinds of water,  
But can my husband not hold even me?  
After living in the husband’s home for three years, light flower petals bloom on my face,  
The three-foot-long hair that used to be, now trimmed and dressed,  
Ah, it can’t last.  
After wrapping up twelve folds of hunger, it all burns slowly away,  
Let’s pack a knapsack and head to Cheongtaesan Mountain.  
Young monks sleep while climbing Cheongtaesan,  
Old monks endure and let me empty my mind,  
Let me serve as a monk, let me empty my mind.  
Neither forward nor backward can I go to the fence posts,  
What kind of monk’s life is this?  
Empty me, empty me, please empty my mind.  
Folding my knapsack on my back, folding the Songnak on my head,  
I will go to return to the eternal mountains and rivers. / Sop’al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Looking ahead, there are clear mountains,  
Looking behind, there are green waters.  
In the world of green waters and blue streams,  
That young maiden is doing the laundry.  
I will give gold, I will give jade,  
But I neither want jade nor gold.  
Mother, mother, don’t say that,  
Eighteen or nineteen years old—  
What does it mean to say I am too young?  
Even if swallows are few, they go south of the river;  
Even if sparrows are few, they still hatch eggs.  
Child, child, my child,  
How can one bear a life of marriage?  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
A father-in-law like a rooster,  
A mother-in-law like a hen,  
A sister-in-law like a magpie,  
Oh dear, I just cannot live like this.

label: Lament_lament
translation:

When my father-in-law died, it also felt somewhat good,  
But when the cattail seed pods fell, I thought of my father-in-law.  
It was good not having a sister-in-law,  
But when the thimble fell, I thought of my sister-in-law.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In the front yard, my mother, like an outer leaf, hides the pear tree,

Spicy and salty, the eldest cousin, sitting at the end of the phrase,  
Buzzing, buzzing, sister-in-law, sitting at the end of the phrase.  
Rustling, rustling, the young man, an owl perches on the pine branch of Nam Mountain.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Clouds drifting in the breeze

Please deliver a letter  
What letter?  
In March or April, in the busy year  
Skipping lunch, weaving hemp cloth

If my elder sibling hears this  
He will grab a sharp sickle  
Saying "If you go, I’ll go too"  
And "If you come, I’ll come too"

label: Lament_lament
translation:

Don’t bury me on the back hill

When it rains, cover me  
When it snows, shovel the snow away  
When my loved ones look for me  
Give them a pair of lotus flowers

label: Lament_lament
translation:
That field of grain,
Is it uncultivated because there is no owner?
Is it uncultivated because there are no seeds?
It lies fallow, just like my body.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Your home is worth a thousand seok, so I came looking at a thousand seok?  
Your home is worth ten thousand seok, so I came looking at ten thousand seok?  
I left for a distant land tens of thousands of li away just to see you, a little one.  
When I see you, I see blossoms; but when you see me, you see only muddy ashes.  
Oh dear, oh dear, how unfair this is—how am I supposed to live like this?

label: Lament_lament
translation:

On the spinning board, it's hard to keep one's chastity.

Three years as a servant, three years as a servant,

My face like white jade,
The sun and moon flowers all bloomed.

label: Lament_lament
translation:

label: Lament_lament
translation:

You wouldn’t know it’s salty.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin-in-law, how is the life of a married woman in her husband's house?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Under Namsan, in Ssari Valley, is the place where Jinju Daejeong lived.

Baby, baby, Minle baby,

Spread the flower cushion, mother, please sit here,
Spread the flower cushion, father, please sit here.

The silver is dark,

Oh my, I didn't know,
Entering with love,

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Chrysanthemum, oh chrysanthemum,
