When you go to the fields, you are a wild chrysanthemum,  
Where do you place the four seasons of spring, summer, autumn, and winter?  
In old October's fresh autumn leaves, you come out alone with me—  
Are you by yourself?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On the cold winter night of the lunar December,  
Having finished all the work in the meditation room,  
Wearing coarse hemp clothes in the main room,  
Lying down on the bed, turning this way and that,  
Resting both sleeves fully,  
In the room where the water flows down,  
Sleeping together after lying down,  
Bit by bit, the mother-in-law,  
With the sound echoing through the oak hall,  
The sound of thunder and heavy rain all resound,  
In the blue room, the monk said,  
Call the seamstress from the lower room.  
The young lady Kim Dan-ok,  
Perhaps she only looks for her lover.  
Like a needle, this body,  
Has gotten a sickness like a leech,  
Helplessly, I will die.  
When this year’s season passes,  
And that year’s season turns,  
Will the disease ever heal?  
Will those parents live long?  
Let us both live long.  
Dung-dang-eh, more dung-dang-eh,  
Pulling dung-dang-eh, dung-dang-eh more,  
Who made the dung-dang-eh sound?  
The cheeky big child, I made it.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother-in-law, how is married life?
They say chili peppers are spicy, but marriage is even spicier.
At Honggap Temple, the twelve panels are soaked with tears and snot.
The water parsley flowers in the cesspool make my face look even worse.
Sowman.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother  
Did you give birth to me to dress up?  
Coughing, in the large field,  
The hoe is sharp like a sickle.  
The work is like fire,  
Did you raise me to go through such hardships?  
Because I was dressed up,  
By day, they look at me like a worm,  
By night, like a lover,  
Did I come to see my lover?  
I came to see the fruit.  
Even if the garlic clove is spicy,  
Would it be as spicy as a sister-in-law?  
Oh, what a hardship it is.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Some people have good fate,  
living well with wealth and honor in a grand, spacious house.  
But why is it that I, with such a fate, go out to sell low-quality goods? / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At the mountain ridge, I tied the spirit field cloths and came here.  
I made soybean porridge and served it as a top soup, and red bean porridge and served it as a top soup.  
On the shelf at the end of the pepper tree, the pot is gently boiling.  
The grandmother next door turned around and, softly chiding, said, “Eat that porridge.”  
After hearing that, I went downstairs to the lower room.  
After removing one ear, I became a cow over the shoulder.  
After removing two ears, I became a cow over the shoulder.  
After turning one corner, the bell sound jangled.  
After turning two corners, I’m the one who went to the civil service examination.  
The one who sat on the horse jumped off barefoot.  
In front of Aram, the red waist moves inside Aram.  
Let’s go, let’s go, let’s go back, let’s return the way we came.  
A smiling baby, who wouldn’t like that?  
A toddling baby, who wouldn’t like that?  
Please hurry, quickly go, the way to my beloved is Jangcheon-ri.  
My way is ten thousand ri (a great distance).  
When I returned home, my father was bitterly grieving,  
“My precious child worth a thousand gold coins, my precious child worth ten thousand gold coins,  
Why can’t you come back? If our home is so strange, pack your bundles under the waning moon,  
And flee under the dawn moon.”  
My mother was also bitterly grieving,  
“My precious child worth a thousand gold coins, my precious child worth ten thousand gold coins,  
Why can’t you come back? If our home is so strange, pack your bundles under the waning moon,  
And flee under the dawn moon.”  
Father said the same, mother said the same, I heard those rumors too.  
Hey you, strange one, not going to the civil service exam, came here after hearing women’s gossip?  
Going down to the lower room, the mandarin duck bedding and pillows seem to have been taken off,  
The chamber pot, like a new field, seems to have been removed,  
The fine table on which the pledge was laid seems to have been removed.  
Gone, gone, heading to Shindanggol (Spirit Shrine Valley), gone.  
If my father were a herbalist, he would cure this illness.  
If my mother were a shaman, she would cure this illness.  
Send a letter, send a letter, send a letter to Shindanggol.  
A letter came, a letter came, a letter came from my beloved.  
Turning one corner, the sound of weeping echoes.  
Turning two corners, the sound of mourning echoes.  
My love, my husband, on the road to Iyanggi,  
Please smell the sweat on my shoes and go, I lay my inner garment on top of the mourning clothes.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, crying mother,  
In my youth, that scoundrel was also young.  
I gave birth to him, and he also gave birth,  
But that scoundrel, what is he? The old man forgot,  
Raising even five sons with magnets,  
Living through hardship and suffering,  
Nowadays, my own son is good to me.  
Even enduring hardship with patience, it seems I lived that way.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
There, on the brass land,  
That big elder brother who always drinks,  
In one night, he finished a red garment all in tatters;  
He says nothing grown up.  
Window paper, please block the wind;  
I am the only family member here.  
Rice is wrapped in lotus leaves,  
Rice wine is wrapped in lotus flowers,  
Carrying a rake,  
To the blue river like reed leaves,  
Let's go fishing,  
Let's go fishing.  
Catch it, catch it,  
Catch a pair of pufferfish,  
Bring the pufferfish back home,  
Skewer it on a straw fire,  
Roast it over a hundred-mile fire and eat it.  
Twelve mountain ranges, I sleep alone,  
Spread out the quilt I used to sleep on in the big room,  
The worn curtain is pulled down,  
The quilt I used to cover is pulled down,  
Lying down asleep on the mat,  
Is my beloved here, is my beloved here?  
Neither my beloved nor sleep is here.  
In the upper room, the elder sister-in-law  
Says to arrange everything neatly;  
She only jabs with the big ladle and comes out.  
In the back room, the sister-in-law's child  
Says to arrange everything neatly;  
She takes the big ladle and comes out,  
Walking with a clattering sound.  
For us, elder siblings’ married life,  
How can we take a nap in the riverfront?  
Hurry, get out of bed,  
Make rice, make rice.  
I can't do it, I can't do it,  
No matter what, I just can't do it.  
At the village school, the green groom  
Half opens the big window,  
Then climbs inside,  
With a sturdy foot like a boss,  
Kicks this way but doesn't get up,  
Kicks that way but doesn't get up.  
Three times he kicks repeatedly,  
When I reached out my hand to his heart,  
There was no warm load,  
Only cold burdens,  
The window was opened suddenly,  
In the upper room, my mother,  
She brought that man’s magnet,  
And made a black rock soldier die, what is this story?  
Under us, plow the field,  
Take good care of the seedlings,  
That man’s magnet is unbearable,  
But his own magnet is acceptable.

label: Lament_lament
translation:

There are many words at the in-laws’ house, and many complaints at the parental home.
At the thatched-roof house with a round hat, the sliding door is hung.
The empty chestnut burrs are blowing twin horns.
Lying down with my beloved in the room across,
The moon rises in the star-covered roof, and stars appear on the ceiling.
Spent the night in tears, and at dawn,
I cook breakfast and prepare the meal table,
But it’s hard to place the spoon on the round table.
Hey, hey, hey, don’t even talk about married life.
Don’t even talk about married life.

translation:
Kim Dong-ji's baby daughter-in-law  
On the day of her wedding

Mother-in-law came out,  
The kettle was rolling empty.  
Child, child, daughter-in-law,  
Go visit your natal home  
And bring back the wooden bucket.  
Father-in-law came out,  
The field was rolling empty.  
Child, child, daughter-in-law,  
Go visit your natal home  
And bring all the plows and tools,  
Bring back only the wooden bucket.  
Sister-in-law came out,  
“How bold is this sister-in-law?  
Is she really this daring?”  
She spread out a flower cushion,  
“Father, please sit here,  
Mother-in-law, sit here,  
Groom, sit here,  
Sister-in-law, also sit down.”  
Listen carefully to what I say:  
When I came to marry,  
Riding a horse like a cloud,  
With a floral folding screen around me,  
Under the twelve-panel screen,  
Entering the village gate,  
Receiving blessings from every direction,  
While the five stars shone brightly in the midnight,  
I came with all my being,  
What are the wooden bucket and family mortar to me?  
Ha ha, my daughter-in-law,  
You have spoken well, my daughter-in-law.  
Those words are indeed polite.

translation:

translation:

translation:

translation:

translation:

I grit my teeth tight like fangs.  
I open my tired eyes wider,  
But no matter how hard I try, I can't do it.  

Hey, hurry and tie the saddle, friend,  
Hey, please give me the saddle quickly.  
I can't do it, I can't do it,  
Mother, mother, I really can't do it.  

When will we finish? The sun is already setting,  
The field is steep and rough.  
When will our home be near?  
My stomach is empty and I’m upset.  

The child crying for food,  
I said I’d buy rice cakes and gently offered money.  
The child crying for milk,  
I said I’d buy candy and hurried along.  

Carrying the field burdens so far away,  
What am I to do with this situation?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin, cousin,  
How is the life of a married woman living with her in-laws?

Living with in-laws for three years,

A hairstyle like three layers  
Has become like the tail of a rat or pig.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
A year older, I lost my mother; two years older, I lost my father.  
I went to my uncle and aunt’s house.  
My uncle is a farmer, and my aunt is from Drichan.  
They went to tend a large and wide field.  
Even if Hari spends twenty hours tilling the entire field,  
the meal they offer is  
a little millet porridge with twenty-six love leaves.  
There is also a large bowl, but it is filled with bean paste.  
Unable to eat even that, I ended up stopping midway.  
Chuna, Chuna, Mankyeongchuna, will you live on that?  
After sealing the soil, handing over a spade, sweeping the yard, giving a slap,  
after shooting arrows and quickly following, I crossed a bottle of liquor.  
With red plums entwined and plums hanging down dripping,  
I just went to pick the plums, wondering how far I would make it.  
Entering the big, big house and its yard,  
looking around here and there, it’s a heap of firewood,  
looking over there, it’s also a heap of firewood.  
We lived uprightly and hard, but we lived well.

- Mankyeongchun  
- Sung in a lively tone.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, why did you give birth to me?
When raising me, wasn’t the land scarce and rough?
Wasn’t food scarce and hard to find, yet you raised me with just rice?
Though the family is good and the surroundings peaceful, I struggle to grow.
You sent me away, and like fire in the sunlight, I am a strong weed in the field.
Wearing shoes every day in the heat, mother, I become like an ox.
Mother, mother, please take me back; if I go out, I won’t survive in this place.
They tell me not to come back and to stay away, so I keep returning.
With a bundle of clothes, I hide in the tree shade without a trace.
When I opened the pot, my sister-in-law took everything, leaving nothing.
There was no scorched rice, so I sat on the hearth, just cleaning the embers.
No matter how I try to live, I can’t survive in this place.
I need to go hoe the field again tomorrow, but I’m too hungry to go.
Wind from the east, wind from the north, frost wind, and the elders’ strict words—
Mother, mother, when I was born, I had no sister-in-law or elder sister, but now I have to grow. / Sophal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother-in-law's words:
She told me to weed the field like a huge plain.
With a wooden hoe in hand,
Weeding one row, weeding two rows,
Weeding three rows, I found
The scorching hot sun
Was like the vast plain.
Weeding this row and that row,
By the time I finished, it was noon.
Throwing down the wooden hoe,
I went inside the house,
And mother-in-law said:
"Why did you come back without weeding your feet?"
Weeding three rows of the vast field,
By the time it was noon,
I came to eat lunch.
Oh, that woman has a strong appetite,
She knows what hunger is.
The vast field
Had not even been half weeded.
Hearing that, I turned back,
Took off my shoes and held them beside me,
Steadily trudging up the mountain path.
The black crow cawed loudly,
"Obituary, obituary!
News of my mother-in-law’s passing."
The right hand received the news,
The left hand grieved,
My mother-in-law had passed away.
Slipping my shoes back on,
Steadily following the path,
But there was no sign of where mother had gone,
My mind was in turmoil.
Having missed lunch,
Is this all a young woman is for?
This is enough of living with an in-law,
Let's stop once more and go somewhere,
To deep water like the Han River,
Dressed in a funeral dress like a lotus flower,
Diving in to die,
Who would care?
The rough willow branches were stirred,
Grabbing a willow branch,
I asked sharply,
"Didn't that young master leave without reason?
There’s no way he would die like that."
I thought again,
Follow me with this hand,
Grasping the young master's hand,
Crossing one ridge lovingly, then the second,
Passing the third,
Coming to a house like an uncle's,
Where a flower garden spread out and sat playing.
This much is living,
It's not like dying and never seeing again.
Meeting that young master,
We made a hundred-year vow,
Had a son and a daughter,
And my life was enriched and continued,
I was born anew.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Silver bowl, brass bowl, bronze bowl, iron bowl, all piled up,
Even a thin thread won't hold; in the cold winter, it doesn’t melt away softly.
If the string on my neck snaps sharply, can I not live? / Sop’al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, cousin, how was life in your in-laws' house?  
Don’t even mention life in the in-laws’ house, it’s a strict and harsh world.  
It was hard to even set the spoon. When I started living in the in-laws’ house,  
even walking was difficult, and there were other hardships as well.  
It was hard to speak, as my parents said,  
“Three years of being deaf, three years of being blind.”  
Somehow, I managed to live through it, and three years passed.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother

Even if I can’t live well,  
They say three words are quarrelsome.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother,  
Why did you give birth to me?  
When raising me after birth,  
Did you intend to marry me off?  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
You gave birth to me.  
Mother, mother, when I was young,  
What did you want to eat?  
Giant bamboo field, giant bamboo shoots,  
Thread bamboo field, thread bamboo shoots,  
Plucked and crushed them,  
Mixed them with sheep’s intestine,  
Mother, mother, why did you give birth to me?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after marriage, my sister-in-law, who picks cherries, urges me to weed the baby field.  
Look at the behavior of my mother-in-law.  
She washed her feet with cold water and urges me to weed the field.  
After weeding the first hill, then the second and third hills,  
it is almost lunchtime. As I arrive to have lunch,  
the sharp-tongued mother-in-law stirs her cold water feet.  
"Yesterday you came, my dear daughter-in-law, and today again, my dear daughter-in-law,  
what kind of work is this, coming only for lunch?"  
Hearing that voice, I was so overwhelmed that I couldn’t speak.  
Returning to my room, I tore seven pieces of cloth.  
I used two pieces to make a patchwork pouch, three pieces to make a bag,  
and one piece to make a simple sash, cutting and cutting,  
cutting my hair to look like a monk.  
I was going, but my husband said to go.  
He said he would ride a horse and go to the Seonbun family.  
Wearing half a plain sleeve, I turned around the side door.  
My husband said, "Dear, Shinjung family,  
don’t start any trouble with people.  
Dear, wearing half a plain sleeve,  
turn around the side door."  
At the end of his words, I suddenly grabbed his hand fiercely,  
trembling all over. "What’s wrong with you?  
What’s the matter with you, who usually wears a silk brocade waist bag?  
Why suddenly shave your head, who used to wear a golden hairpin and chop its hair?  
Why wear straw shoes over your worn shoes?  
Let’s go, let’s go back home."  
"I can’t go, I can’t go.  
Your parents' family is good, but I’m different, I have to go."  
Returning home, I asked my mother, "Where did he go?"  
"Since you left, he went away." The words made me so overwhelmed.  
Inside the three-foot coffin, inside the coffin, I cut my neck and died. / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother  
Don't treat me badly just because I showed up  
If I brought just a measure of rice  
Both you and I would have food to eat

Would you give it to me, the outsider?  
Even if the old pond overflowed  
Would you share it with me, the outsider?  
Guests who go to your house  
Are only those of wealth  
The ones who come to my house  
Are only the poor and humble

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother,

Sent me before my husband,  
Only longing deeply for my hometown.  
There was no one who cared about me, not a single person.  
My husband was also indifferent,  
At night, he wove sheets,  
In the morning, he washed and prepared the bedding.  
He said to loosen the ropes for the bedding,  
Do this, do that,  
The child couldn’t even open their eyes,  
Got up and cried loudly.  
After everything, in the morning, he went to the mill room,  
Changed the grindstone,  
He acted all mischievous,  
In the morning, he washed and cooked rice,  
But because I said the rice was late,  
He scolded and tied me up,  
Saying if I don’t go out to the field quickly, it would be trouble.  
The child had to wash rags,  
Do the dishes, work as a farmhand,  
Cook meals, and live like that,  
That’s how it was before.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At sixteen, I married,
The year I first wore a gat, I lost my husband,
Thought I would die, oh youth,
Wanted to live, but hardship awaits.
Clinging to the pillar of the veranda, I turned around,
Stepping outside the main gate,
Out of nowhere, a wild goose
Brings news of my beloved.
On the long, long night of the winter solstice,
As I sit, sleep does not come,
As I lie down, my love does not appear.
After crying all night long,
My sorrow has deepened.
The river of tears is indeed a river,
A pair of ducks, a pair of geese,
Two pairs, four of them, have come flying.
The green ones are willows,
The yellow ones are orioles,
The golden orioles,
Wearing armor like gold,
Go to find my love in the Tumen River.
Do not recklessly shoot,
I lost my love like this,
Wandering in search of him.
Looking up, there is a cliff,
Looking down, barren land.
A bent old general,
Unable to withstand the harsh gale,
Only dances wildly.
Climbing the mountain, eating wild plants,
Turning back, it is a famous mountain.
Plucking flowers to place on my head,
Tearing off leaves to play the zither,
Breaking pine branches to use as a cane,
Climbing the mountain to enjoy the scenery,
Passersby,
See only me and cannot leave.
Only when I climb the hill behind,
Do I think of my beloved,
On the green grass leaves, I realize,
The dew has all arrived.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
I won't do it, I won't do it, I won't follow the women's trend

Distancing myself from my parents' intentions, before the age of twenty I entered the convent

Making the intentions of others my own, pairing with virtuous people  
I envy, I envy, I envy the life of a man  
Born a woman in heaven without any sin  
I won't do it, I won't do it

translation:

but they just keep spinning the wheel and napping in the afternoon.

she was scolded to go chase after my son’s room and bring him back.  
The mother-in-law says, “If I go after such things,  
I’ll have to cook rice at my own house. Why don’t you go back to your home?”

I prayed for my mother-in-law to die,  
but then I received news that my own mother has died.  
I jumped over the fence, let my hair down,  
pulled out my hairpin and stuck it in the ground, returned to my mother’s flowers,  
and when one person passed away, the wailing echoed loudly.  
When two passed away, a tinkling sound could be heard.  
Father, please delay, so I can see my mother’s face again.  
Hey, hey, baby, frozen baby, if you want to see mother’s face,  
I came yesterday and you didn’t come below; I can’t do as I please. /Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law  
How is living in the husband's house?  
Don’t ask about living in the husband's house.  
…Cut off one blind tail.  
What about the horse's back?  
Try eating red bean powder.  
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law,  
Yes, it’s really hard.  
It’s like a death sentence from the dish towel.  
I wiped away all my tears and snot.  
My hair is like a three-layer cake,  
I will cover it with a dance of bitterness.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
One year older, the mother died, two years older, the father died.  
Somehow, I grew up, and then got married.  
Shortly after the wedding, we roasted five mal of sesame seeds and five mal of perilla seeds in two mal of oil,  
earning some money from selling perilla cake and sesame cake as well.  
Dear little one, go often to your home,  
even if you plow the fields with the ox and plow, you can buy perilla cake and sesame cake.  
Look at the mother-in-law’s behavior—she sips from a small soup bowl while casting sly looks,  
fiddling with a reed flower here, poking with burdock there.  
Go often to your home,  
even if you plow the fields with the ox and plow, you can buy perilla cake and sesame cake.  
Cut, cut, cut my hair, and the servant boy takes me out.  
Cut it, please cut it, cut my hair now.  
After shaving one side of my head, my forehead became wet with tears.  
After shaving both sides, I became a river of tears.  
Duck, goose, since you have nowhere to play, go to the river of tears and play there.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
For seventeen years, for ten years, for seven years,  
putting the sick head of the household to rest, leaving the young children behind,  
what is the matter with the patchwork cloth?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
If you want to see Jinjunang-gun, the son-in-law,
Go to Jinjuga and do the laundry; when you go to Jinjuga to do the laundry,
Both the stones and the water are good; placing the jade stone in front,
Washing the laundry briskly with a pear wood bat,
Suddenly the sound of a horse comes faintly,
Walking along the neighboring rice field, carrying a heavenly coffin,
Riding a cloud-like horse, with concubines in front,
Pretending not to see, going about, washing the black laundry thoroughly,
Washing the white laundry cleanly, then returning home,
The mother-in-law says, "If you want to see Jinjunang-gun, my dear daughter-in-law,
Go down to the back room."
Dressing beautifully with seven-colored embroidery, going down to the lower room,
Placing a guest's cup on the colorful branch and setting down colorful liquor,
With the concubines beside him, telling me to drink, telling you to drink,
The heart feels strange, I cannot bear to watch, so I go up to the upper room,
Wearing a one-foot-long dark headband towel around the neck, he is dead,
"Get up, get up, dear husband, get up,"
Without a word, like a frog in its shell, oh why did you go so easily?
The concubines are for three years, the main wife is for a lifetime,
Why did you leave so easily? Everything is a tragedy.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
Where did you put the flower of service?  
Because I am weak to the pear blossoms,  
When I enter my lover’s room,  
My lover is not there,  
Only the old me is restless.  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Mother’s affection grows distant,  
My lover’s affection seems close.  

In the sorghum field covered with frost,  
That tall boy picking ears,  
Tied a silk thread at the tip of your hair,  
Please tear off just a little for me.  
Are you getting married to that house?  
They say to wear a manggeon [traditional headband] tight.  
The groom will come,  
But don’t come on a rainy or snowy day.  
The artisanal hat shop  
Has no place when carrying an umbrella.  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Poor, poor our mother.  

-Hungul song  
-A different lyrics version is sung.

translation:

I will prepare the meal for the elder brother  
A pancake like Oe’s rice cake  
Deodeok pickled like ox horn

Going to the house in front, there’s wood vinegar porridge

A brightly colored skirt,

To live is to suffer,  
To die is youth.  
Hooray, oh hooray,  
No, I cannot play around.

translation:

Round and round, like a watermelon rind, it's hard to serve the rice.

Living in the in-laws' house has many difficulties, and living at the host’s place comes with lots of talk.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is life living with your in-laws?  
You say the chili is spicy,  
But living with the in-laws is spicier.  
These clumsy hands of mine  
Have become like a sharp sword.  
This hair of mine, like a three-layered thing,  
Has become like a pig's tail.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother  
Why did you send me away?  
Did you send me to Myoryang land?  
There is also Jeollabuk-do land,  
But did you send me to Myoryang land?  
Did the wind blow me here?  
Did the mountains and rivers lure me here?  
Was I carried here by the current?  
I followed a little baby crab and came here.  
I have suffered and struggled while living,  
But today, I also want to live for a while.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
My baby, my daughter, how is married life treating you?  
Married life is good, but at the dining table  
It is difficult to set the spoon.  
It's also hard to serve rice in the big stoneware bowl.  
The younger brother-in-law who is not fully grown is also difficult to talk to.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Let's go, honey, let's go, honey  
Let's quietly go  
A star attendant sits on the upper rice field ridge  
And a headman sits on the lower rice field ridge  
They tell us to sing a respectable song  
In the hands playing with the ink brush  
What’s going on with the cotton puff?  
In the hands playing with the rouge  
What’s going on with the comb?  
In the hands playing with the needle case  
What’s going on with the sleeve guard?  
Oh honey, oh honey, daughter-in-law  
I didn’t know you would be like this  
Hurry and go inside the boat

label: Lament_lament
translation:
After living three years in marriage,  
The triple-layered outer garment has become worn,  
The forehead and hairline have become like a scratched comb.  
After living three years in marriage,  
The triple-layered outer garment has become worn,  
The forehead and hairline have become like a scratched comb.  
After living three years in marriage,  
The face, once as beautiful as makeup,  
Has withered like water parsley flowers blooming.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Riding a white horse, I ascended to the pearl planet Jupiter  
The lotus reveals its essence, and the willow branches dance gracefully  
The willow branches dance gracefully, but can life itself dance well?  
Somehow, wearing the three-generation belt  
All other tattoos appear, but this one does not  
Searching and searching, I find the father-in-law in the yard  
He puts aside what he was planting and says, "Hey, step back!"  
What kind of boat are you drawing, coming to find a tattoo?  
Mother-in-law is planting in the yard, puts aside what she was planting  
"Oh dear child, oh dear child, what kind of boat are you drawing?  
Coming to find a tattoo," the sister-in-law was cooking  
"Sung-ah, Sung-ah, come here, Sung-ah, what kind of boat are you drawing?  
Why do you come seeking before the time? Your husband has gone to Seoul  
Riding a heavenly steed, running like a cloud"  
"Cut it, cut it short, cut this hair short"  
"What is this, what is this, why without saying a word?"  
"I'm scared, I'm scared, I'm scared of my own parents"  
"If you fear your parents, can you live a thousand or ten thousand years?"  
"I'm afraid of the mother-of-pearl statue; if you fear your younger sibling  
Can you live a thousand or ten thousand years? Cut it, cut it short  
Cut my hair a bit"  
After cutting under one ear,  
The sides of my forehead are wet, and after cutting under the other ear  
I have become a tear-soaked mess.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
As the rumor spread that living with the in-laws was good,  
the daughter-in-law was last, but the mother-in-law was first.  
Mother-in-law, mother-in-law, the daughter-in-law is there.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
If the drifting clouds part the western mountain,  
Please deliver a letter—what letter could it be?  
In the months of February, March, and April,  
I am starving and weaving cloth.  
Just send rice.  

On the coldest lunar month nights,  
I walk barefoot.  
Send shoes.  

If my father hears this, he will put down the meal set before him  
And wail loudly with deep sorrow.  
If my mother hears this,  
She will wail loudly as well with great sorrow.  

If my older brother hears this,  
He will take off his mourning cloth  
And dance the grieving dance, and you should join him too.  
I will join as well. What about your parents?  
Will your parents care for you?  
Will my parents care for me?  

Dundangae deong dundangae deong  
Dangi dundangae dundangae deong / So-pal

translation:
In July and August, the cicadas fly and tremble over there,

If I go to my husband's house, I am welcomed, but at my husband’s home, my sister-in-law is an enemy,  
What am I to do with this miserable situation?

In July and August, the cicadas fly and tremble over there,

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The youngest daughter of Mr. Park  
The daughter-in-law of Mr. Kim  
Just three days after getting married  
She was seen at the ten o'clock rice pounding place  
She watched carefully and pounded  
Watching carefully and pounding  
They are coming, they are coming  
Her beloved husband is coming  
Pounding and then pausing  
Standing outside the gate waiting  
They are coming, they are coming  
Oh, a hundred years’ worth of rice  
Let's crack the ice all at once  
Come on, eat quickly, come on, eat quickly  
If you’re cold, I’ll warm you  
If you’re thirsty, I’ll fetch water  
That hairpin on your head

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Washing, washing, washing clothes by the Ok-nang River  
At Oraenamu, Oraebangti, filling the hemp sack and carrying it  
Pine nuts, pine nut baskets, holding them in hand and carrying them  
Washing clothes by the Ok-nang River, scrubbing the laundry thoroughly  
An unexpected fruit vendor dances in front of me  
It drifts, it drifts, the bathwater drifts around  
After washing hands and feet in the bathwater, I poured out the bathwater  
Not eating and leaving, the dark laundry washed off the grime  
The white laundry washed its whiteness, and I returned home  
The sound of laundry after three days resounds  
Feet swell, feet swell, only outside the door do feet swell  
Laundry sounds shake and the gate slams shut  
Hearing that sound, the father came outside and hurried to open the gate  
The twenty-five-year-old funeral guard has gathered and stands  
The front guard says, “Hurry and come out quickly  
Bow once, please bow,” but he refuses to bow  
Even after bowing three times, the recognition doesn't come  
The father says, “My son, my son  
Come and bow, I will give you three thousand nyang*  
Even after bowing three times, no recognition is given”  
The front guard says, “Call your daughter in  
Call your daughter in”  
Bringing only my daughter, having bowed three times  
the figure disappears, and my mother says  
“My daughter, my daughter, what I said was to go wash clothes  
Why did you go to wash clothes?  
I wrapped a white scarf for you  
Put on a white jacket and step out quickly  
Hurry along, hurry along, oh my, how frustrating my situation is  
Should I mourn with my hair undone, calling the one I have waited for?  
Heading and crossing nine hills, twisting and turning along the way  
After bowing at the nine hills and entering the house  
Making fences with yeast, discarding the passing needle  
Using thick needles, living three years with careful edging  
Fingernails and toenails all fell out after living three years  
Even my hair fell out, and my made-up face  
Why has it become yellow-stained?  

-Recalled  
-Document Unique

*“Nyang” was a traditional Korean currency unit.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sung-ah, Sung-ah, don’t be selfish just because you’re going through puberty. If you’ve only cooked one mal of rice, you eat some, and I eat some too.  
If you get it with hot water, should I give it to you or should you give it to me?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Hypothesis or hypothesis, is my sister-in-law’s husband a scammer?  
At our doorstep, we gather debts from each other and go.  
We, too, break cockle shells to make roofs,  
Wrap rice paste in tightly rolled bundles, and hang daylilies at the gate.  
In the ancient empty room, a tall house is adorned with a pendant on your ear,  
Which wind has blown in that we also get to live for a while?  
Open the gate, girl, whose soy sauce are you going to brew?  
You’re so pretty, aren’t you? What kind of flattery is this?  
What kind of flattery is this? You are a flower among women.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Older brother, older brother, adolescent older brother  
How is married life?  
Married life is said to be good,  
But from the beginning of going to another's house,  
The nose runs and tears fall.  
The three-layered hair  
Becomes all messy,  
The pure, fair face  
Turns into a withered flower,  
The wrists like pear blossoms,  
The hands that used to wear silver rings  
Become all rough and calloused.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is the life at your in-laws' place?  
Brother, brother, don't even talk about it,  
Hanging on to a dishcloth like dementia,  
All the tears have dried up.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
It’s been thirty years since I got married, the date we met was like this.  
Was the date wrong, or was it because the year was changing? I didn’t know it would turn out this way.  
When we faced each other at the ear-splitting moment,  
Did we receive a good day? Even if we did, was the day unlucky?  
When we even untied our ear-splitting moment and met,  
We made a hundred-year promise; I didn’t know it would turn out like this.  
We endured seven years in distress and parted ways,  
I didn’t know it would be like this, even though we said we would live a hundred years.  
Who would have known it would end like this, living seven years and then parting?  
In between, we bore no fruit, nor did we sprout a single branch,  
What kind of fate is this, how can I live on? Oh, it’s so frustrating.  
I lived without knowing whether it was autumn or spring,  
The news that came was like a silent mountain, no word of the departed.  
What is there for me to live for? The water is too deep to come, the mountain is too high to climb,  
It’s so desolate like this; every night and every day,  
I counted and wished, but it was all in vain, it was all in vain.  
Where is the futility of this matter?  
Having lived without knowing the right time or season, I didn’t realize the season was passing.  
The coltsfoot flowers on the back hill resembled me, my face like a flower,  
Alone in an empty room in solitary confinement, my youth has completely faded.  
I am gone, and you survived, but shoots have sprouted and buds have blossomed,  
Even if you live well and enjoy yourself, is it because of undergarments?  
You cut short your lifespan; that field over there was fallow last year,  
This year, it’s fallow again.  
It’s become a useless field under the shade,  
It should have been sown with grains but turned out patchy.  
Now there is no ownership, even old bones come in pairs,  
And even straw sandals come in pairs; either way, it’s the same as everyone else.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How was living in your in-laws’ house?  
Oh dear, oh my,  
Don’t even mention living in your in-laws’ house.  
At Doridori Saetgat’s house,  
In the room with the blue dragon, yellow dragon, and giraffe on the rice chest,  
The door frame is made of thick bark,  
After living in my in-laws’ house for three years,  
My hair, once three-layered,  
Has all turned gray.

label: Lament_lament
translation:

label: Lament_lament

In a tall house with dark walls,  
Dark walls and many buildings,  
Telling me to come out and be humble,  
The old lady said I ate it,  
"Die, die," she said,  
In clear water,  
"If you fall in, you will die," she said.  
Looking back at the underworld,  
Taking one pair to put in the mouth,  
Taking two pairs to hold in the hand,  
I've been caught, I've been caught.  
You sly woman,  
She said I ate it.  
Don't send messages to mother,  
Don't send messages to father,  
Mother knew too,  
Father knew too,  
The whole village knew,  
After being hit once,  
I think of my mother,  
After being hit twice,  
I think of my father,  
"Die, die,"  
Leaned on the doorframe and looked out,  
Seeing a golden light.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In Muan land, the golden maiden  
desired to be married.  
Soon after getting married,  
in the room where water liquor was made,  
she was told to spend the night.  
They lit a big charcoal fire,  
used the jade lamp for light,  
hung it over the bed,  
and placed a reed mat.  
They laid down eastward, westward,  
and seeing the silk bundles left,  
they placed a mat on the floor,  
and after a short sleep,  
whispered secretly,  
looking out at some city,  
and conspired to kill.  
Whispering secretly, again,  
looking out at some city,  
and conspired to kill.  
Tomorrow at the market, at Muan market,  
there will be a special event for five don coins.  
With soybean paste soup like poison,  
stirred up and placed on the table,  
the water liquor single-layer blouse,  
worn very nicely and tightly,  
the water liquor black skirt,  
worn very nicely and tightly.  
At the mat stone floral seat,  
who would pair up and spread it?  
With the hair parted in two,  
swept beyond the comb lines,  
after taking a sip,  
all the four limbs loosen up.  
After two sips,  
the six thousand horses all collapse.  
After three sips,  
off they go and get tipsy.  
An older schoolmate who went to Seoul,  
like the Oe family’s elder,  
kicks off the Yangje side by foot,  
complaining about married life being tough.  
Why would she take a nap?  
In the inner chamber, parents say,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Like a morning star, the chamber pot’s dignity,  
she is the golden maiden, she is hers.  
Half open the main hall door,  
tell mother to leave,  
tell father to leave,  
if the groom's mother-in-law knows,  
what kind of responsibility would she take?  
Plow the front field to buy servants,  
plow the back field to buy hired workers,  
manage the treatment of injuries well,  
an illness that lasts three or four days  
was cured in one day.  
After three or four days of coming to see,  
it had turned into a wormwood field.  
Alas, hurrah!

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother  
Why did you send me out?  
Leaving behind all the neighborhoods,

The heartless train  
Carried me away,  
Does it not know where it’s taking me?  
Mother, mother, my mother  
Why did you send me out?  
Are you trying to raise me like this?  

—Called Twice

label: Lament_lament
translation:
After marrying into the in-laws’ family, I endured three months of household hardships.  
After three years, I went to the Namgang River in Jinju. My mother-in-law said,  
“Go into the inner room, wearing a seven-foot cloth around your neck, with the marriage certificate in front of you.”  
(Background noises)

Having lived in a house with neither walls nor fences for three years after marriage, my mother-in-law said,  
“Child, dear daughter-in-law, Jinju, go do the laundry at the Namgang River.”  
Jinju went to do laundry at Namgang River; the water was good and the stones were good.  
The black laundry was washed cleanly, the white laundry was washed brightly.  
At Cheoncheon, the sound of bamboo water pipes, when I looked up,  
My husband, like the sky, riding a horse like the mist, (background noises)  
Without even looking back, he left; so wash the black laundry cleanly, wash the white laundry brightly.  
Returning home, I opened the love gate, only to see the concubine’s certificate placed in front.  
They had to put five-colored varieties of side dishes and alcohol, saying “You eat, I eat,” urging us to drink.  
I went up to the main room, wearing the seven-foot cloth around my neck,  
My breath was short and passing out; my mother-in-law said,  
(momentarily forgotten)  
My sky-like husband comes running on bare feet,  
“Hello, hello, come here!”  
The concubine’s affection lasts three years, but the first wife’s affection lasts a hundred years.  
(Background noises)

Breakfast, lunch,

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At my house, a chicken used to peck inside the rice granary,  
But when it came to someone else's house, it treated it like a river spring.  
If the river spring is water, it’s like a refreshing mountain stream,  
If the river spring is not water, it can't be a mountain stream.  
If the fallen leaves look like rice cakes, they are sure to sprout mold,  
If the fallen leaves do not look like rice cakes, they can't sprout mold.  
If the pearl fishing net is gathered, it will catch many fish,  
If the pearl fishing net is not gathered, it cannot catch many fish.  
Oh, laborer, wash your hands; the midnight star is shining high.  
No matter how high it rises, when morning comes, it will fade away.  
Master, where have you gone? You don’t seem to know about the midnight snack.  
There is a midnight snack, but no time to serve it.  
If there is no time to serve, then bring the bobbin fruit.  
There is bobbin fruit, but the branches are too high to pick.  
If the branches are too high to pick, then dig for ginseng in the ground.  
There is ginseng underground, but the vines are too many to dig.  
If there are too many vines to dig, then fetch cold water.  
There is cold water, but no container to fetch it with.  
If there is no container to fetch, then dig up pumpkins from this year's field,  
And use the shells as containers to fetch it.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, crying out loud,  
Trying to be strong, leaving me behind,  
Abandoning everything,  
Planting me on this mountain,  
Have you forgotten me? Have you forgotten me?  
I can't live, I can't live,  
Take me away, take me away,  
Just take me away from this place.

translation:
Living as a daughter-in-law was truly hard to endure,  
I couldn’t live without eating wild greens,  
Living as a daughter-in-law was truly hard to endure,  
I couldn’t live without visiting my family’s village,  
Living as a daughter-in-law was truly hard to endure,  
I couldn’t live without weaving twelve bundles of hemp thread,  
When I called the twelve bundles, my bright red skirt  
Was worn out from being put on and taken off so many times,  
Living as a daughter-in-law was truly hard to endure,  
At night, I go to the factory and collect hemp floss.  

— A song about the hardships of living as a daughter-in-law

Brother, cousin, brother, how was married life?  
As I lived through it, the taste of lunch felt strange.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Oh, my fate is so frustrating—  
In the deep night,  
I sit alone—  
Under the tail feathers,  
This stitching with no thread,  
Day and night, all day long I do it,  
To prevent the rascals from slipping away.  
My love, my love, you wicked one,  
Where did you go leaving me behind?  
Until my fingernails and toenails wear thin,  
Night after night,  
Until dawn,  
Stitching like this,  
To prevent any gaps,  
Day and night, this is my situation.  
Oh dear,  
I can't live like this, I can't live like this.  
I miss my love, I miss money,  
I miss food, I just can't live.  
If I tighten my waist belt,  
Even if I hit and touch,  
And try to sew—  
Would anyone pay me ten won more for one piece?  

- Sewing Song

translation:
Meeting as my beloved,

Looking over the steamed rice,
Packing lunch in the garment strings,
Wrapping side dishes in arrowroot leaves,
Saying they were going to the distant mountain trees,
Under the roof of this house,
Scraping up a handful of awlwort,
Caught on a mosquito's hind leg and died.

translation:
Three days after coming to the husband's house, the new husband went away.
Next to the flower basket, placing it there, going to the hill behind.
Ascending the fern, the fern that comes to you,
Breaking off bit by bit, putting a small amount into the pot.
Gently in boiling water, lightly boiling Arirang.
Placing silver spoons and silver knives,
Placing brass spoons and brass knives,
In the brass bowl, neatly piled up, in the silver bowl, neatly piled up.
In the silver bowl, placing silver chopsticks, in the brass bowl, placing brass chopsticks.
A small wooden tray, neatly filled.
Father, please get up, get up and have breakfast.
Father-in-law, look at your movements, he is stirring, he is stirring.
Stirring because the vegetables are new, stirring, then turning around and coming out.
Opening the large room door, mother-in-law, generation after generation,
Please get up and have breakfast, mother-in-law, look at your movements,
She is stirring, she is stirring, stirring because the rice is cold,
Then turning around and coming out. Generation after generation, brother-in-law,
Please get up and have breakfast, brother-in-law, look at your movements,
He is stirring, he is stirring, stirring because the rice crust is cold.

translation:

If there’s a scent or a sound, come quickly.

translation:

Climbing Junyeongtaesan  
High peak, Sangsanbong

Looking at the mountains and rivers

B.

Our fate

translation:
At one year old, my mother died  
At two years old, I lost my father

Oh, my poor fate  
Why has it come to this?

Will you come, my love?  
My love, oh my love  
You came when you left

How pitiful is my life

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Laundry time, laundry time, laundry time at Ok Nang River.  
At the old wooden bridge, carrying laundry in a bamboo basket,  
Carrying pine tree laundry in the hand and heading to Ok Nang River,  
At Ok Nang River, scrubbing and washing the laundry.  

Suddenly, the washerwoman dances in front of me,  
Drifting, drifting, drifting in the clear water,  
Washing hands and feet in the clear water, offering the clean water,  
Not eating and leaving, after washing the black laundry and the clean laundry,  
The white laundry is washed white and comes back home.  

After only three days of laundry, the sound of happiness resonates,  
Feet swell, feet swell, the feet swell outside the house,  
The sound of happiness is shaking and the main gate clangs,  
Hearing that sound, the father opens the gate hurriedly,  
The twenty-five-year-old mourning man stands with his feet together.  

The front leader says, "Hurry up and come here,  
Bow once, bow," but no bow is made,  
Even after bowing three times, there is no reaction.  
The father says, "Son, son, my son,  
Come and bow, I will give you three thousand nyang,"  
But even after bowing three times, there is no response.  

The front leader says, "Bring your daughter in,"  
"Bring your daughter in."  
When the daughter is brought in and bows three times,  
Even the footprints fade. The mother says,  

"My daughter, my daughter, when I said go do laundry,  
Why did you go wash white cotton clothes and put on a white jacket,  
And hurry to go ahead,  
Please hurry up and wrap up. Oh, how frustrating, my fate is like this,  
Should I loosen my hair and lament that I saw the one I loved?  

When going over the nine hills, twisting and turning,  
After bowing on the ninth hill, entering home,  
Building a fence with nuruk (fermentation starter), making a fence with pine needles,  
Using thick needles, living for three years,  
Fingernails and toenails all fallen off after living for three years,  
Even hair has all fallen out, makeup is gone from the face,  
Why did my face turn yellow?

translation:
Growing up under my parents' care,  
I proudly said life lasts a hundred years,  
But before I knew it, I turned eighty.  
What use is there for leftover stones after building a castle?  
Before leaving, before departing,  
Let's have some fun and go sightseeing.

translation:

translation:

Like a half moon, I will go, what kind of half moon are you?  
A crescent moon is a half moon, brother, brother's cousin,  
How is married life? Hey hey cousin, don’t say that.  
After living three years in marriage, my hair is like a three-step braid,  
Even the strands are all broken,  
My hands like split bamboo have worn the rings of a knife,  
My face, like a wildflower, has bloomed with water parsley flowers.  
Brother, what have you prepared?  
The front house made five porridge, the back house made seven and five porridge,

The front house ate five porridge, the back house ate seven and five porridge,  
This house ate five porridge, altogether fifteen porridges were all served on elder brother’s table.  
Brother, brother, a pancake like elegance, placed on rice like cherries in a field,  
Ferns from the sunny side and silver ferns from the shaded side,

Sowalf (a closing word or signature)

we make a hat and cut our hair… then bow and go.

tear another to wrap around the waist,  
tear another to make a carrying bag,  
tear another to tie a bundle.  
Climbing up, climbing up,  
going up high to find a monk in the mountains.  
Is it in our family tradition, when going north,  
to cut hair and bow before going?

There is clothing in every valley  
Consider me, consider me  
Even if you come, consider me  
In Igangja, Jakang field  
The heliotrope is old  
Dragonflies eat the water fleas  
And hang them in your room  
When I asked to see the insects,  
The little sister-in-law  
Held a sharp knife in her bosom  
And tore everything apart  
If it is to be torn, then tear it  
But tear it so it’s easy to pick up  
If it is to be torn easily,  
Why should I be torn?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, daughter-in-law mother,  
Did you criticize me for looking good?  
When I spoke, you responded,  
Did you criticize me after taking a whole bundle?  
I can’t live, I can’t live.  
When you spoke, you told me to only watch the birds on the mat,  
But you spoiled everything,  
Because of my shortcomings, I can’t live.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
A: At my home, my beloved is like an unfortunate person embraced in my arms.  
By day, we walk equally; by night, we walk madly.  
Meet only at the neck, meet only at the neck.  
At thirteen, the socks meet only at the neck.  

B: I can’t do it, I can’t do it, I can’t handle this servitude.  
I don’t want to work, let’s go to the Namsadang (traveling performers).  
I don’t want to eat rice, let’s go to the meat market.  
The rain is on the mountain ridge.  
Let’s tie a cowbell around the waist and fix the soil in the field.  
Some people have good fate, live harmoniously with their parents in a grand palace,  
But I am cooking like this.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Climbing, climbing up this mountain  
When will grass or trees grow on this mountain?  
Carrying the sun on my back, when will I reach our home?  
Oh dear, I'm so distressed and troubled.  

When climbing this mountain—  
If there is a spirit in the grass and trees, if there is a spirit,  
Carrying a load, the place where our home sits,  
I come and sit down to eat.  
(The latter part was not recorded)

label: Lament_lament
translation:
It’s my fate, it’s my fate  
Because I couldn’t become a warrior  
Why couldn’t I become a follower?

Who could have known my fate would turn out like this?  
Why couldn’t I become a follower?  
What nonsense is this follower?  
Who could have known my condition would turn out like this?  
Only heaven knows, only the earth knows  
Who would know my condition would turn out like this?  
Who, who would understand?  
It’s my condition, my fate  
I can’t do it, I can’t do it  
I can’t become this kind of follower

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Living as a daughter-in-law among twelve family members,  
My husband left me and, after only three months, said he was going to the store and left.  
Among the twelve family members, I threshed barley,  
Pounded it hard and then gave the rice,  
What it means to be a daughter-in-law —  
A wide field like a pure, vast barley field,  
Like the earth itself, I, alone, cultivated a whole spot in that field.  
In this remote place, after plucking a handful and eating lunch,  
I came back home and saw my sister-in-law,  
She made bean porridge, served soup, then thick porridge, served soup,  
Pushed this way and that on the birchwood shelf,  
And that's when I broke down.  
Living in a world without a husband, I can’t live just eating soup.  
Let’s go, let’s go. Since we have to leave anyway, let’s take the middle road and go.  
When I went down the middle road,  
Half were taking naps, half were wearing shoes,  
“Hey you, cut my hair,”  
When one side was cut, tears I hadn’t had before came out naturally,  
When both sides were cut, great wailing came out naturally.  
After living for two or three years,  
Like a gust of wind, my husband came to find me.  
“Let’s go, let’s go, go home,” he said, and holding the doorframe was a baby  
Crying, “Mommy, daddy,” that baby was dear too.  
“Hurry, let’s go, my dear,”  
“I can’t go, I can’t go,”  
Since my hair was already cut, how could I go down the middle road again?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three years after getting married, my mother-in-law said,
"Go spit out the baby," and when I went out to the field,
Why were the ridges in the field as long as a mountain?
After tending one ridge and the space between ridges, all the shoots came out,
Even after tending two ridges, the field looked like a mountain,
Even after tending two ridges, others' lunches appeared, but mine did not.
I was so hungry I thought I’d die, so I went home,
But my sister-in-law, like a poisonous snake, came inside without tending the field.
I came in because I was hungry.
No matter what, I can’t live in this in-law’s house.
After three years, they gave me old soybean paste on a plate,
And sticky barley rice in a bowl.
Eating this, no matter how much I think, I can’t live—I can’t live in this house.
When I came to marry, I tore one piece of clothing to make a bundle,
Tore two more pieces for my bag,
Tore one more for my headscarf,
And tore twelve pieces to make a quilt and a bag, and then I shaved my head.
I went back to my parents' village and visited my parents first.
"Why did you come back so soon?"
When I said I was going home, they said, "The dog is barking. It’s barking."
I gave you everything, yet you don’t even recognize me.
I came to see you, the one I gave rice to.
My mother said, “Dear, why can’t you live in that house?
How did you end up like this?”
I packed my sacks with bundles and scarves and went back,
My mother’s eyes darkened, saying, “Oh, why can’t you live in that house?”
No matter how much I think, I can’t live there.
Maybe it’s because I chose the wrong husband, where is that husband now?
How could he be so cruel? “That’s just how it is.”
Mother-in-law, after leaving that proud one behind, you took me in?
“When a daughter-in-law is like that, that’s what the mother-in-law says.”
If you left that proud one and took me in, you shouldn’t have troubled me so much.
You cooked and cooked, why did you trouble me so?
No matter how much I think, I can’t live.
“That’s how it went. It’s a hardship.”

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Like a square blanket neatly spread in the room, a jade lamp is lit,  
A mandarin duck bedding is spread out,  
Sitting, waiting for the guest to come, lying down, wondering if the lover will come,  
Beyond the bedding is the Han River,  
A pair of ducks and a pair of geese are flying away.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mom, mom, oh mom, when you raised me,  
You didn’t even burn the golden rice cake, nor the jade rice cake.  
As an only daughter, how could you raise me like that?  
Loyal father wished for a son-in-law, loyal father wished for a son-in-law.  
At Hwadang Hill, you crossed over, crossed over,  
Crossing over Hwadang Hill, crossing over Hwadang Hill,  
Tears fill the Han River water when my mom calls me.  
Is there a letter coming to my parental home today or tomorrow?  
Counting the days waiting for a letter telling me to come home, but no letter comes.  
Then a notice arrives that my mother has died.  
Mom, mom, my dear mom, selling half a rice cake to buy tangerines,  
Selling barley to buy citron, to serve my mom.  
I waited and waited so eagerly.  
What is this? Selling half the rice cake and barley to buy tangerines and citron.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Why did it happen, why did it happen, in this shape, in this state, why did it happen?  
At one or two years old, not knowing anything, I left my parents' care,  
And my fate turned out like this, enduring countless hardships and storms,  
In this shape, in this state, I have grown old.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The story of the daughter of the Jeolla inspector

Hong Gang-jin, whether it rains at dawn or not, whether she sleeps in the arms of the family head or not,
Clumsily, like an insect, Hong Gap-sa fell into dementia, put on and took off, everything falls apart / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How was the newlywed life?  
Don't even mention the newlywed life,  
The sandy rice field is no longer a rice field,  
The back field is no longer a field,  
The fence post is no longer a post,  
Every day is newlywed life,  
Don't mention it, don't mention it.

translation:
Mother, mother, daughter-in-law, mother  
Where did you put the sword?

Did you kick me with your foot?

translation:

Living with in-laws for three years  
Three-year-old fermented shrimp paste  
Spread on the edge of the plate

Spread on the edge of the dish

Father-in-law turned into a Jindo dog

Carrying a front basket and a back basket  
Lunchtime is getting late  
Breakfast is getting late  

The rice eaten just yesterday and the day before

Three-year-old fermented shrimp paste

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after coming to the husband's house, I was asked to look after the housework.  
I went down to the mill to borrow a silver cup,  
But I accidentally broke that silver cup. The mat cover is a bitter burden.  
Sitting quietly in the back porch,  
Oh, you daughter-in-law, if you go to that house,  
Borrow a silver cup for me.  
The sharp-tongued mother-in-law suddenly opened the door wide,  
Oh, you daughter-in-law, if you go to that house,  
Wrap your sleeves tightly, and borrow a silver cup.  
The mother-in-law with a blue skirt is busy going in and out,  
Oh, you daughter-in-law, if you go to that house,  
Wrap your sleeves tightly, and borrow a silver cup.  
The eldest daughter-in-law is going here and there, tangled up,  
Seeing this, that young wife went into her room,  
Laid out the mat, not putting on the fine hemp clothes,  
Father-in-law, please sit here.  
Mother-in-law, please sit here.  
Eldest daughter-in-law, sit here and listen to this.  
On the front veranda, in the long field, your son,  
When he socialized with me, changed into new clothes,  
Wore an eight-fold skirt, and pushed a wooden plate,  
How important is a silver cup? Farewell, take care.  
When I held the silver cup, how important it was.  
In the middle of the night, when the moon was high, and when no one knew,  
I revealed my whole body, but only my whole body was filled,  
Please repay me with a silver cup, father-in-law.  
Don’t worry, no one will know. What a dutiful daughter-in-law, what a dutiful daughter-in-law!  
I will build a three-room shrine on the back hill,  
Don’t go, just wait, see that lady’s behavior.  
She shaved off six locks of hair, wore an eight-pleated jacket,  
Hung an 108-bead rosary around her neck, held a folded paper piece in her hand,  
Wearing tied straw shoes, with twelve thousand ears and eighty-nine stitches,  
That widow who returned to the Buddhist temple hall.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Like a seed in a field,
Like fire in a field,
Called a field,
I came into the house,
Under the gardenia tree shelf,
I gave sour porridge as an appetizer,
I gave bean porridge as an appetizer,
I met my beloved,
But my husband went to Seoul for an official position,
The mother-in-law was harsh,
I couldn’t live like that.
I went down to the inner room,
Beating the wooden drum,
I tore one piece to make a cone hat,
Tore two pieces to make a basket,
I couldn't endure life as a daughter-in-law,
I thought I must leave to the monastic life.
I was told to go to the temple,
“Follow the monk, go straight,”
“Neither the monk in front nor the monk behind,
Just walk a little bit each day.”
Following the monk, I went to the temple,
“Cut! Cut! Cut your hair!”
I cut my hair,
After cutting one side,
Thoughts of my beloved grew intense,
After cutting both sides,
Thoughts of my hometown grew intense.
I lived in the temple for three years, five years or so,
Then I was told to beg for alms,
I was sent somewhere,
As my senior went riding a horse,
I took a quick glance that way,
My beloved came down riding a horse from Seoul,
“Beloved, beloved, don’t go,
Look at me before you go.”
He got off the horse,
“Why are you here,
Just manage somehow,
You came here and October passed.”
If that was the case, I couldn’t go home.
I went home,
Called out “Mother,”
“Child, child, are you coming?”
When asked, “Where is your wife?”
“No one knows where she went.”
Sick and delirious,
My husband was delirious,
Until he died,
I contacted my wife,
“If you are sick, take medicine,”
After writing a letter,
I wrote that he died,
“Take off one of his old inner garments to cover him.”
Three years after my husband’s death,
I went down to my hometown,
In the mother-in-law’s graveyard,
Wild thistles widely bloomed,
In the father-in-law’s graveyard,
Wild cudweeds widely bloomed,
When I entered my beloved’s graveyard,
The hibiscus flowers bloomed fully.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Song Baek-su, carrying a high rack of green branches,  
Beautiful women in green and crimson robes are lounging around,  
But our friend does not know the Day of the Double Fifth.  
Water spirit wine, straw pants, ramie cloth, and blue hemp fabric—  
Even if all the seasonal clothes are prepared, he does not know how to wear them.  
They say the road is long, once you go, you cannot return.  
They say that door is not a door, that you cannot open and close it.

- Repeated call  
- Lament of a widow. Part of a "dalgeori" (traditional Korean folk song).

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Long, long ago, in times long past,
At Tuk-Tuk Bari So-Yeon’s home,
Unable to finish the rice on the plate,
A female calf was born with a bell,
A yellow calf was fitted with a horn,
When I was born and the day passed,
I too was born, but
Who would have known my fate
Would turn out like this?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Gangnam-ddangddang Gang-nim wished to get married,  
But just three days after getting married,  
He told me to hide the rice seedlings.  
When I hid the seedlings and went inside,  
My father-in-law looked out and said,  
"Ah, granddaughter-in-law, wash your hands and feet and come in."  
When I washed my hands and feet and went inside,  
My mother-in-law looked out and said,  
"Ah, granddaughter-in-law, wash your hands and feet and come in."  
When I washed my hands and feet and went inside,  
My sister-in-law looked out and said,  
"My brother, my brother, please wash your hands and feet and come in."  
After washing my hands and feet and going inside,  
I went to the room across the way.  
In the room across,  
I placed my hands over my head,  
Lay down for a nap,  
And then, suddenly, someone came, someone came—  
A scholar from the village school came.  
Even though my life is unsettled,  
What business do I have taking a nap?  
Try to feel, try to feel—  
Feel this pulse here.  
When I tried to feel the pulse,  
It was gone, it was gone—  
Gone to the afterlife.  
Father, please listen,  
Mother, please listen,  
Even you, statue, listen,  
At my young age of twenty prime years,  
I cannot live without a flower.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Oh mother, oh mother of mine,  
Why did you give birth to me?  
Are you asking me to do what I cannot?  
When it’s a man’s time, I also give birth,  
When it’s a woman’s time, men also give birth,  
Why then is it like this?  
Some people have a fortunate fate,  
Living in grand, luxurious houses,  
With desks filled with books,  
Studying letters and learning,  
But I, I have so, so much,  
Nothing to do, and yet such a humble servant,  
Was I made for this, I wonder—  

-Song sound-  
>

label: Lament_lament
translation:
When the two of us met,  
I was only sixteen years old.  
Wearing a thin silk jacket,  
with twelve folds and dyed hemp pants,  
whispering softly  
you stood on that side,  
and I stood on this side.  
With blue and red threads on the cup,  
we passed them back and forth,  
making a vow for a hundred years.  
But before the hundred years were complete,  
we had lived together for only fifteen years.  
How regrettable those days were,  
I regretted being thirty years old.  
Our youth,  
once gone, never returns.  
The world is round like a pumpkin,  
round this way, round that way.  
Living recklessly,  
I have grown old without purpose,  
grown old without seeing much.  
Leaving things undone,  
those days have come to an end.  
Alas, ten thousand years!

label: Lament_lament
translation:
When I was young, I was just like everyone else when I was young, but whose fate is so fortunate to live in an ancient, spacious house?  
With a high house and a parasol moonshade hanging,  
Every time the southeast wind blows,  
The sound of the parasol is loud, but my body feels weak.  
In early summer, the intense heat,  
What is this? Is there no cure? Is there no cure?  
My heart feels so stuffy, is there really no cure?  
In early summer, the heat is like a mountain.  
Why should I carry this burden on the field?  
Oh, how frustrating, my fate!

label: Lament_lament
translation:
When the castle walls collapse, the people scatter,  
When the intact walls in the yard collapse, the floorboards improve,  
The chapel in the middle of the yard only looks intact on the outside, but inside it is damaged,  
The coal-burning kiln emits no smoke but only ash,  
The water agonizingly boiling now only produces smoke. / Sop'al

translation:

My youth is gone

I can’t stop the white hair  
I can’t stop that white hair

Mother-in-law

translation:
Across the field of abundant grain,
A pair of prosperous birds settle.
Is it the spirit of my dear one who has passed?
It weeps sorrowfully just by looking at the day.
I should have become a swallow over the southern river,
And sat by my dear one's drinking room.
I should have become a flower across the river,
And blossomed in my dear one's hands.
On the road to Seoul,
Sitting among the pine trees,
I should have become the playful fingers that drum,
And been caressed by my dear one's hands.
Oh, how delightful!

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seong-a, Seong-a, cousin Seong-a, how is married life treating you?  
Round and round, using the watermelon dish to serve rice feels warm and affectionate.  
When seeing the in-laws’ table, placing the spoon is also full of warmth.  
The unkempt father-in-law, scratching his head and talking,  
Even speaking about that feels difficult.

translation:

translation:

Is eaten grilled when it’s not the season.

translation:
Comrade, comrade, a thousand comrades,  
How is life as a bride?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was married life like?  
Don't even mention married life, shaking my head at the straw-hat house.  
In a house with no shelter, shaking my head inside the small table,  
It's hard to keep fidelity. Married eyes are blind for three years,  
Deaf for three years,  
And dumb for three years.  
After living those three years,  
The three-layered front cloth becomes my hair,  
The rice-straw dance is all worn out,  
Like a weathered face,  
The white hair flowers have all bloomed.  
It can't be helped, it can't be helped,  
A woman’s body, it can't be helped.

translation:

If the sewage is mine, is the sake mine too?  
If the scorched rice is mine, is the dog mine too?  
I never knew that such things existed in the world.

translation:

Life in this world is tough.

Troubled by life in the in-laws’ house,

translation:

The spicy chili-like hardships

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Trimming the Gangnam embroidery,  
Stitching it on the Haedong robe,  
Following the Donghae flower’s gentle glow,  
Following the scent of Mencius' ointment,  
When I try to wear it, it gets stained,  
When I spread it out, it becomes wrinkled,  
On the hill behind, an old tree,  
Hanging branch by branch,  
You see me, I see you,  
The wife who took the room,  
With the husband asleep,  
Torn thread by thread,  
At the end of the rock called Gakseol,  
Please take care of your younger brother,  
Even if you take care, he won’t listen,  
If he goes alone, can I live without him?  
Did I see a house worth a thousand bags of rice?  
Did I see one worth ten thousand bags?  
I came to see my small older brother,  
If so, go and look at the chokeberry flowers.

translation:

How was married life?

Married life lasts three years  
Hot pepper soup and ten different porridges  
It’s all soaked with tears and snot  
Brother, what side dishes will you prepare?  
Ferns under the shade  
Ferns on the sunny side  
Porridge at our house  
Porridge at the back house  
Porridge, porridge, ten kinds of porridge  
All brought for brother’s side dishes

label: Lament_lament
translation: When my mother gave birth to me, she wanted wild chervil; even now, it is full of sorrow.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The person from the village is fortunate by fate.  
This fellow's true nature is revealed.  
The eunuch who prays to the mountains and trees boasts.  
Golden child, jade child,  
Unbelievable, gently blowing the wind bell / Sophal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after getting married,  
I was told to weave five fields of hemp,  
Having woven five fields of hemp,  
I lost my appetite for food.  
One corner turned sour—  
That was the stingy father-in-law,  
“Go away, you wicked woman,  
Take your anger and leave,” they said.  
Another corner turned sour—  
That was the stingy mother-in-law,  
“Go away, you wicked woman,  
Take your anger and leave,” they said.  
One corner turned sour—  
That was the sharp-tongued sister-in-law,  
“Go away, you wicked woman,  
Take your anger and leave,” they said.  
When I came,  
Did I come seeing a thousand sacks of rice?  
Did I come seeing ten thousand sacks?  
You small-minded old woman,  
Did I come to see just one sack?  
Dang-gi dung-dang-ae dung-dang-i de

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
Trying to be splendid, I stepped forward  
Was it difficult at the great river?  
Slowly spinning the silk thread  
Stretching the strings of the shuttle  
Holding the shuttle in my hand  
After working a whole day  
I pulled out twelve threads  
Who could not do this?  
I cannot, I cannot  
In the field sown with the main crop  
In the fire-like burning field  
The spindle whirrs swiftly  
Carrying one bundle, carrying two bundles  
Carrying three bundles  
Even if friends' sincere hearts come out  
My sincere heart does not come out  
Ah, I cannot talk about it  
Going into the house saying it’s a home  
To whom can I tell what’s on my mind?  
There is no one to talk to  
Mother, mother, I cannot do it  
Ah, I cannot stand it

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, why did you send me out like this?  
When my mother was preparing for me to get married, she played all sorts of games, but didn't we also sing the Gomgomcho song?  
When I think deeply about Gomgom and Sansan, I feel like I can't live anymore.  
Mother, mother, whether my mother was preparing me or my mother-in-law was preparing her daughter,  
if you think about how they struck the wooden tray as if sealing water,  
there is no one who can live easily after marriage.  
Mother, mother, please take me away now.  
My love, my love, even when we sleep under the same blanket,  
you don’t understand my feelings.  
My love, my love, don't say anything about having affection just because we grew close,  
when it comes to parting, everything becomes impossible to say.  
Mother, mother, when my mother planted me, she didn’t do it lightly.  
At the end of the steep ridge, she planted me, but my roots couldn’t spread, so I feel I cannot live.  
Mother, mother,  
if in life you find it impossible to live with attachment, then clap, clap, clap your hands,  
and I will go out and live decently.  
Mother, mother,  
though all that’s left is words like a skirt,  
all that’s left is a jacket, just wearing these and holding my luggage,  
I’m going without hesitation. Mother, mother,  
if you want to see the world I’ve lived in, come into my room now.  
Though all that’s left are words like a skirt and a jacket,  
even pierced by the spaces in the field, look at me and the one I see.  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
I am leaving now, if you want to find me,  
under the thirty-six planks of the boat’s bottom, inside the small room is my room.  
Mother, mother, look at me.  
A tree laden with fruit can never have calm winds,  
and our parents, with so many children, never have a peaceful day.  
-/Sopal

-Hungul song
