label: Lament_lament
translation:
My mother used to feed me bracken fern shoots,
Bit by bit, it was sorrowful.
My mother used to feed me balloon flower root shoots,
Round and round, it was humiliating.
My mother said I couldn’t endure married life,
When I go to my parental home, my father chases me away with a stick.
Drowned in the straw-covered water of the Han River, I die.
You die and become a fluttering spring butterfly.
I die and become a lotus flower, sitting as if blossoming.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On the neat square stone foundation, I wash with a thump-thump sound,  
My beloved comes, my beloved comes, the one who went to Seoul comes.  
I place the unwashed laundry underneath, the washed laundry on top,  
Put them on the main wooden floor, then the one who suffered poison dies and disappears.  

Silver river, silver river, eastern silver river, where has your bride gone?  
Are you eating alone?  
The sleep I had last night only lasted until dawn.  
Wake up, wake up, bring your bride back.  
I try to wake her, but she says the hardships of married life are bitter.  

When I opened the door and went inside, it was three layers deep because of the hair grabbed,  
Hair strands were all loosened, the one who suffered poison dies and disappears.  
The moon rises over the window; the sun rises over the three-year-old gate,  
In the small back room, only the night lingers, and the one who suffered poison dies and disappears.  

Mother, please sit here, father, please sit here,  
The one who suffered poison dies and disappears.  
The villagers know, in spring the five-colored robes are splendid,  
That household over there knows too, their shamanistic rites are magnificent.  
Mother, father, I am going. / So-pal  

- In the style of a courtesan’s lament  
- Refers to Dongdaemun?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother, why do you call me out?  
What do you want to do by sending me off to the countryside?  
Like fire in the sun, like sweat in the field,  
Even the sea breeze fills up the valley, yet you ask for a song?  
Husband, my husband, has gone to work in the fields,  
Wind, blow, blow for three months and ten days.  
My neighbors’ husbands ride bicycles,  
But the man in my house just eats pollock soup and lingers around.  
Oh, oh, hey, aren’t you my love?  

The song about longing goes back to Wonsan, Hamgyeong Province,  
They say the original song comes from Japanese merchant ships.  
Oh, oh, hey, aren’t you my love?  
The other household’s husband wears nice shoes,  
But the fool in my house leads a poor life.  
Oh, oh, hey, aren’t you my love? / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The federal bamboo that rose to the sky,  
Oh, the person who constantly picks it,  
Seventy guests leaving their parents,  
Leaving behind their young children,  
The raft's end gone without a trace.  
If you come looking for me,  
In the pine forest of Manseok,  
Under the thirty stone slabs of Jongwoo,  
Inside the forty-two slabs of Hongdae,  
A door locked without a key,  
There is absolutely no way out.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
After living in a house with no fences or boundaries for three years since marriage,  
What the mother-in-law said was,  
"My dear child,  
If you meet the nobleman from Jinju,  
Go do the laundry by the Jinju River."  

When going to wash clothes by the Jinju River,  
He wore a hat like the sky,  
Rode a horse as red as a chestnut,  
And passed by as if he hadn't seen her.  

Seeing that, make the white laundry whiter,  
And the black laundry blacker,  
Returning home,  
The mother-in-law said,  
"My dear child,  
If you want to meet the nobleman from Jinju,  
Go into the small room."  

Going into the small room,  
She found the Jinju courtesan beside him,  
Playing the Korean zither (gayageum).  

Seeing that (voice omitted),  
She went down to the back room,  
Took medicine of five colors (voice omitted, forgotten).

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Baby, baby, my daughter, how was married life?
Married life was good, but at the table,
it was difficult to place the spoon properly.
It was hard to even serve rice in the round stoneware bowl.
My brother-in-law, who was naked, was difficult to even talk to.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Time, oh time, do not come and go so carelessly.  
The mountain baby’s white hair, in the late autumn southern wind,  
Even if carried away like a sack of rice,  
This darn white hair is useless white hair.  
Shall I hope to use it as an application fee for the afterlife university?  
If the afterlife university entrance fee is covered,  
I would throw down the half-eaten bottle gourd and push away the dog,  
Hand over the family scroll to my son,  
And leave my affairs to the neighborhood.  
Using the soot as clothes, and the soot roots as friends,  
Making lifelong friends among the young lads,  
I go, I go, I am going,  
I will go hoping.  

Time, oh time, do not come and go so carelessly.  
If you want to go, go yourself, do not take my youth with you.  
Just the other day I heard the words of a young boy,  
Saying the white-haired baby was elevated on the back hill, beneath the old tree.  
When I was young and in youth,  
All sorts of birds would fly in,  
But now the tree is old and withered,  
Not even a single blind bluebird flies in. / Sop’al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even if alcohol and cigarettes understand my feelings,  
My husband at home does not understand my feelings.  
Eyadiya ehei eya  
Eyadiira Sanajiroguna

label: Lament_lament
translation:
If I can't live with my in-laws, they blame me harshly; if I can't go to my parents' house, I stay with my in-laws.  
Having entered my husband's family, I can't live because of my mother-in-law's nagging.  
The husband they call mine never even says a word to me in his lifetime. / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Aga aga, Minul aga,  
They say it's a field, but it's all tangled up.  
Every little corner is covered with sesame,  
Seaweed is gathered on the hills.  
Each head is tied tightly,  
One bundle, two bundles,  
Even if you gather three bundles a day,  
All the officials have come and gone.  
But no one like Yone (a righteous man) appears.  
Aga aga, Minul aga,  
Step back, this path—  
They say it’s a matter of work.  
Looking for the right time and season,  
What is given as food  
Is three-year-old barley rice,  
Stuck to the bowl’s edge.  
What is given as the sauce  
Is three-year-old dinggi jang (fermented sauce).  
The plates are covered in dirt,  
And the spoons are just thrown away  
Ten or five ri (Korean miles) off,  
Twelve widths of cloth,  
One width torn into a cone hat,  
Eleven widths packed in a basket.  
Entering the bamboo grove,  
Leaning on the old fence,  
Mother and father, please receive my bow,  
I take my leave and step back.  
One watering turn passes, over a hundred seeds tremble,  
Two watering turns pass, all the dry corn trembles,  
Three watering turns and  
My husband who has gone to Seoul  
Holds a brush in his mouth,  
A book tucked at his side.  
My dear, my beloved,  
I am going, please don’t go.  
May my parents live a thousand years and ten thousand years,  
Leaving you behind, I find my way back to the temple.  
Master Jung, Master Jung,  
Is the place for poetry begging?  
Going to the place for poetry begging,  
Mother, please give a little alms.  
Though you do not give alms,  
My child’s face shows through,  
Like a newborn child—  
Not that word, please give a little more,  
Oh child, please give alms,  
Glutinous rice and millets are all done,  
Give a hand of millet alms,  
The bottomless sack receives the alms.  
Getting up, the fly falls,  
I slap with my hands in rejection.  
I slap with the gourd too,  
Filling a whole basket with that guy.  
Waiting for Aunt’s husband,  
He comes making steamed rice dishes,  
The bottomless sack, did you come for alms?  
Giving a fool’s gift, then leaving,  
As time passes and I come again,  
The household is ruined,  
In front of father-in-law’s rice storage,  
Pumpkin flowers are in abundance,  
In front of mother-in-law’s rice storage,  
Only withered flowers have bloomed.  
In front of Dongshi’s rice storage,  
Poison flowers bloom profusely,  
In front of sister-in-law’s rice storage,  
Cherry blossoms bloom profusely.  
On the husband’s mother’s place,  
Full blooms of cabbage flowers,  
Cabbage, oh cabbage,  
Looking at me, you bloom fully.  
Why do you bloom so fully?  
With that sound, the cabbage flower split apart,  
And entered the mountain alive.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
What a fortunate person’s fate,  
Living in a grand, high palace.  
What kind of fate is this fellow’s, I wonder?  
Oh dear, oh dear, what am I to do?  
What will become of my own fate?

translation:
Brother is coming, brother is coming  
Brother is coming through Bulgogae, who will go to greet him?  
Brother, younger sibling, you will go  
Brother, brother, cousin brother  
Where is the in-law life? Child, child, don’t even speak of it  
Plant chili peppers in the back field, plant eggplants in the front field  
Even if the chili and eggplant are spicy, it is spicier than marrying into the family  
Pounding duck-shaped rice cakes, boiling medicinal water  
Lighting fires under twelve pots, folding blankets in twelve rooms  
Who will understand? Even if it is difficult to cross a single-log bridge  
It is harder than the mother-in-law  
Although the leaves are green  
More feared than the mother-in-law  
Father-in-law is like a tiger bird  
Mother-in-law's scolding is like the bird's piercing call  
Brother-in-law is a nagging bird  
Husband is a foolish bird  
Younger brother-in-law is a chasing bird  
A child is a crying bird  
For three years, my eyes did not see  
For three years, I could not speak

After living three whole years  
My body is like three boards tied together  
My hair is all in a combed style  
My face has become like a pear blossom

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Using fire on the lamp wick,  
Hanging it on the jade cup,  
Lighting the front and back,  
Folding both sleeves,  
Even doing that, it was not enough.  
They say go, they say go,  
Oh, the world is unbearable.  

Going down to Aritbangjuk,  
Catching a small fish,  
Burning it with straw fire,  
When sleep comes, it’s gone.  

They say he’s coming, they say he’s coming,  
The husband is coming.  
Leaving behind all ailments,  
Entering his own house,  
Greeting his father,  
Greeting his mother,  
Nine family members,  
One family member is missing.  
Is he in the province? Where could he be?  
Going into the province,  
Wearing worn-out straw shoes,  
Kicking here and there,  
Kicking three times repeatedly,  
When sleep comes, he’s gone.  

Going upstairs to the wife,  
The father is disappointing,  
The mother is disappointing,  
When sleep comes, he’s gone.  

Setting stakes in the front field,  
Placing a coffin in the back field, decorating the mourning,  
Please conduct the funeral well.  
If the father-in-law and mother-in-law hear this,  
They will scold me like a thief.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Living with the in-laws involves a lot of talking and a lot of work.  
At the stream's ford, there are many bridles. / Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
If it’s one, then Kim Jong-ok, growing up in Hana West,  
Day by day, he struggled for his parents.  
If it’s two, then after two tries, our parents give permission.  
At seventeen or eighteen, he is sent off to marry.  
If it’s three, then if this body becomes a man in this world,  
Could he leave his parents and siblings behind?  
If it’s four, then you all, take care, I am leaving.  
Reluctantly, Kim Jong-ok departs.  
If it’s five, then parting from dear friends,  
It is truly hard to say goodbye to boyhood friends.  
If it’s six, then Young-nam, if you had your family,  
Wouldn’t you finish your days and leave?  
If it’s seven, then among seven friends, I learned myself.  
With mountains unknown and waters unfamiliar, this family,  
If it’s eight, then why must a woman become a woman,  
To be pressured without mercy by in-laws and siblings?  
If it’s nine, then at the age of nine, that man forcibly  
Cannot freely go to the hometown he wants.  
If it’s ten, then day and night, working hard,  
Only made to work, only made to work,  
This body like youth  
Has withered, has withered.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seonbang, having done all the laundry,  
In the room with the water bucket,  
Lying down on a mat, lying on a board,  
Even laying down the sleeves and the two handles,  
When the hawk fell into the empty room,  
I lay down there just a little,  
Like a cicada's harsh parents,  
Soon enough, they'll understand,  
The sound of placing the chamber pot,  
The evil demon and the rain demon all crying,  
Inside the room, that child,  
An elder at the village school in the lower room,  
Take off your shoes, that wife,  
Did you come looking to cause trouble?  
Seonbang, having done all the laundry,  
In the room with the water bucket,  
Lying down on a mat, lying on a board,  
Even laying down the sleeves and the two handles,  
When the hawk fell into the bare room,  
I lay down there just a little,  
Soon enough, they'll understand,  
Like cicada's harsh parents,  
The sound of placing the chamber pot,  
The evil demon and the rain demon all crying,  
I should have a silver tool on my head,  
Even if my head sometimes changes,  
Will only the two of us change?  
You have a silver ring on your hand,  
Even if the water changes to water,  
Will only the two of us change?  
At fifteen years old, sister-in-law,  
Sent off to another family,  
Let the two of us live together,  
If our parents, at eighty years old,  
Go to the lotus courtyard,  
Let the two of us live together.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The elder brother is coming, the elder brother is coming  
To Bungogae, the elder brother is coming  
Who will greet the elder brother?  
I, the younger brother, will go  
Brother, brother, cousin brother  
How is the life of a bride in her husband’s house?  
The life of a bride in her husband’s house is like a woman’s life  
In the front yard, they plant perilla seeds  
In the back yard, they plant peppers  
Even though peppers and perilla seeds are spicy  
The life of a bride in her husband’s house is spicier  
On the duck path, fetching water  
Stoking the fire in nine pots  
Crossing twelve rooms  
The eldest son-in-law is like a tiger bird  
The mother-in-law is like a biting bird  
The brother-in-law who takes off pants and socks  
Is hard to talk to  
One younger brother is a wanderer bird  
The mother-in-law is a biting bird  
The husband is a Maitreya bird  
One child is a crying bird  
One younger sister is a sorrowful bird  
On the longest night of winter,  
Crying throughout the night  
Is it a caterpillar?  
A pair of tears, a pair of worries  
The pair separates and departs  
On the longest night of winter,  
After crying all night  
Wiping tears and wiping nose on the edge of a cloth  
When did everything rot away?  
Three years of having sore eyes  
Three years of having sore ears  
Three years of being unable to speak  
After living for three years  
The stick’s surface is my heart  
When did everything rot away?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seong-a, Seong-a, cousin Seong-a, how is the life of a daughter-in-law?  
The thin son-in-law, should I do this or that? Even speaking is difficult.  
Layer upon layer, placing hand-pulled dough flakes on the serving dish is also difficult.  
Round and round, filling the watermelon-shaped bowl with rice is difficult too.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Naju Yeongsan Dan Melon is said to wither just to leave seeds behind,  
But why would a thousand-year-old widow wither just to leave something behind?  
Does she wither in her later years to become a tear-soaked sea of longing? / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Hey, where will you go, hey, where will you go?  
Over the ridge of Seowangsan, where will you go?  
If today you go and rest somewhere,  
Tomorrow, while going, where will you sleep?  
My fate, oh my fate,  
This wretched fate is so unfortunate.  
Hey, where will you go, hey, where will you go?  
Over the ridge of Seowangsan, where will you go?  
The wind roars, blowing fiercely,  
The heavy rain pours down,  
Saddening songs burst out all at once.  
Even when only flowers bloom, I think of it.  
Hey, where will you go, hey, where will you go?  
How will you go along the thousand-foot road to Hanyang?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
To be admired, you raised me  
Why do you make me suffer so much?  
When I was born, you raised me cute as the youngest daughter  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Thinking about it drives me crazy  
Mother, mother, for having plenty of food, you cherish me  
Even when there is none, there is a bowl of rice; even when there is none, there is a bowl of rice  
Did I waste the rice?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin, cousin, how is married life?  
They say married life is good, but the mother-in-law's house is like a strict fence.  
Wiping tears and wiping runny nose, everything is soaked.  

When the ox-cart goes around once, the dog barks,  
When the ox-cart goes around once, the white snow hen cries,  
Older brothers say the writing is good, so don’t worry,  
But they didn’t report a single thing to me.  
Go back quickly, go back quickly to the house,  
Please at least see your mother’s face, still, I tell you to go quickly.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Living as a daughter-in-law in this household, there are many words and many hardships.  
You die and become a butterfly, and I die and become a flower.  
Next year around this time in early March, I will meet my beloved.  
My mother-in-law in our house scolds me and pushes me away.  
Living as a daughter-in-law in this household is so difficult that I can’t endure it.  
Namhae Geumsan, Geumsan’s master, ruled over ten thousand people.  
My parents in our house couldn’t help me.  
They kept pushing me away, pushing me away—pushed me away about twenty times.  
Oh, how good that is! Truly, my heart burns inside.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Sung-nim, Sung-nim, adolescent Sung-nim,  
How is life in your marital home?  
After living three years married,  
The laundry skirt feels like a burdensome plate.  
Wiping away tears, everything falls apart,  
My hair is wild like an enemy in front.  
Dancing the dagger dance with the Jeonju rhythm,  
My face is like a fragrant blossom.  
Adorned with flowers from Iral-ri with the Jeonju rhythm,  
My face is like white jade.  
Adorned with flowers from Iral-ri with the Jeonju rhythm,  
My delicate wrists,  
Why are there two boils?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
My face like a spikenard flower, can it be compared to a water dropwort flower?  
My hand like white powder, it’s like the Big Dipper.  
The head like white powder at the Three Halls,  
Climbing up the back hill,  
The flesh of dried fish compares to a hand that can fend off dementia.  
Don't leak out, door, door.  
I’ll patch a thin sheet for you,  
Mother bird, don’t cry.  
I’ll fetch hot water and cook porridge for you,  
Barking dog, don’t bark.  
I’ll pass down the meal I received,  
Chicken, don’t cry.  
I’ll accept the new flesh, baby.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On Sandu Gap Mountain, wild goose rice is good whether it's "olgicholgi" or not.  
Here, the big rice grains' stalks are good in all four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, and winter.  
Oh, oh, oh, everything gets soaked, crushed, and mixed up in the swing and sway.  
I've become a penniless wanderer.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On that uneven hill over there, something is there  
If we too die, it will be that grave  
With pine and bamboo, enclosing a fence, and within the thirty-two slats  
My body is buried, making it a resting place like a tomb  
What kind of friend would come to visit me?  

— Heunggre Taryeong

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, cousin, how is life living in the in-laws’ house?  
Hey, hey, hey, don’t say that—on this tiny little stage,  
It’s hard even to keep one’s fidelity; on this tiny little watermelon field,  
It’s hard even to serve meals. Even if a handful of chili is said to be spicy,  
They won’t realize it’s spicy. Even if a handful of salt is said to be salty,  
They won’t realize it’s salty.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The mother-in-law nags a lot about the car parked at the chest.
At Namsan Peak, the eagle owl sits, hooting, brother-in-law.
In the back field, peppers are planted, spicy and salty, delicious friend.
In front of the tavern, fishes hide, wriggling and fluttering, dear sister-in-law.
The swallow sits on the nest, building a house, sister-in-law.
In front of love, flowers are planted, buzzing softly, my dear.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
O maiden sleeping in a house without walls or doors,  
Who could possibly melt soy sauce to look as beautiful as you do?  
If you are a spinning wheel, you hum gently; if you are a fishing hook, you catch fish,  
Whether it’s a sickle or a scythe, all sorts of men only melt soy sauce. /Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Look at the behavior during the healing ritual
It's a muddy swamp, performing the Danso Gut
When it’s supposed to be given, it asks for the time to give
If it’s farming, it asks for the farming season
Dressed in fine silk for the makeup
Wearing a waist sash around the hips
With a black magpie's feather string
Stepping firmly on the frozen path
Outside the gate of a thirty-three-room house
It has settled quietly.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Cousins, cousins, how is living in the husband's house?  
Oh my, don't say that. On the kitchen floor,  
It's hard even to set down the spoon. From the middle elder brother-in-law,  
It's hard even to speak. From the elder sister-in-law of the wife,  
It's hard even to put up the blue paper. Oh my, don't say that.  
At the house with the conical hat,  
In the rotten house in the rain and snow,  
In the house where the wind blew and stopped,  
When I entered the room,  
In the Blue Dragon, Yellow Dragon, and Giraffe room,  
In the newly built green-and-blue remaining room,  
Oh my, even if you say the words are harsh,  
Is living in the husband's house so harsh?  
Even if the neighbors speak harshly,  
Is living in the husband's house so harsh?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Oil lamp, oil lamp, in the jade oil lamp  
Fill it to the brim with dam-baekji (a type of oil)  
Light the lamp that will be used  
Even if I weave a whole bolt of satin  
They say to make it smaller and go out  
If my father hears this  
He would push aside the meal set before him  
Oh, poor my dear child  
If my mother hears this  
She would stop spinning the thread on the spindle  
Oh, poor my dear child  
If my older brother hears this  
He would close the book he was reading  
Oh, poor my younger sibling  
If my elder brother hears this  
“Have you ever lived far away?”  
“I have also lived far away.”

label: Lament_lament
translation:
They say living with the in-laws is hard, but the chili pepper is even spicier.  
Brother, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law, living in my in-law’s house is this difficult.  
I secretly cried at night.  
During the day, I served my mother-in-law and father-in-law,  
and I shed even more tears.  
At night, I woke my husband and said I wouldn’t live with the in-laws anymore.  
Please understand this from the broadcasting station.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
(Just as Grandma Choi was starting to speak, Grandma Kwon stepped in)

Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law,  
How is life married into the family?  
They say married life is good,  
But wiping tears and snot from the best dishcloth makes everything sag.

A head like a three-tiered lunchbox,  
Shall I weave it into a sharp dance?  
Hands like stolen goods,  
Shall I weave them into the Big Dipper pattern?  
A face like a walking body,  
Shall I weave it into the water parsley flower?

(Other song follows)  
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law,  
Rain, rain, don’t come,  
Our brother-in-law’s rosy dishcloth will get stained (NG).

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even though Baekdu Mountain is high,  
It cannot surpass the voice of my father-in-law.  
Even though whales and tigers are scary,  
They are not as frightening as my mother-in-law’s voice.  
Even though the full moon is bright,  
It cannot be as bright as my father-in-law’s eyes.  
Even though streetcars and trains are fast,  
They cannot be as fast as my sister-in-law’s mouth.  
Even though the fields are vast and wide,  
They cannot compare to the reach of my husband’s hand.  

“But now, I have reached the point of being driven away,  
Because I am a woman repeatedly,  
I just endure everything as it comes.”  

On a wide handkerchief,  
I embroidered the character for love,  
Hiding it deep in my heart to give when my beloved comes,  
But the handkerchief is stained too much.  
What is this talk of separation and parting?  

The old tree on Ditdong Hill,  
Rots inside just like me,  
Since it is rotten inside, which gentleman would  
Give me a certificate (recognition)?  
Only when the outside rots can others know.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The donggae donggae donggae girl  
One parent fell ill  
There was no cure at all  
Crossing the street, crossing the street  
Turning the corner by the pharmacy  
Crossing over to the other pharmacy  
Making a medicinal plaster  
She earnestly applied it  
If it was something severe  
After a short nap  
She was gone, she was gone  
Gone in the new moon night

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after getting married  
She was asked to provide five measures of sesame seeds, five measures of perilla seeds, and two measures of beans.  
She was told to grind them in a wooden bowl and roast them in a cast iron pan.  
Because it was unripe and watery, the wooden bowl and cast iron pan broke.  
Her stern father-in-law got very angry and said,  
"My dear, my dear daughter-in-law, go back to your home quickly,  
Even if you have to sell time, buy a wooden bowl and a cast iron pan."  
Her stern mother-in-law also said,  
"My dear, my dear daughter-in-law, go back to your home quickly,  
Even if you have to sell time, buy a wooden bowl and a cast iron pan."  
Her little sister-in-law came out and said,  
"Elder brother, elder brother, our elder brother, please go down quickly,  
Even if you have to sell a cow, buy a wooden bowl and a cast iron pan."  
Place the middle blue cloth and receive the middle meal; place the upper blue cloth and receive the upper meal;  
Prepare twelve cloths and serve twelve plates,  
My beloved, my sweetheart whom I meet with a nod,  
My steadfast body has been worn out like old paper,  
If you cherish my fragile body like spring skin,  
I will bring home the wooden bowl and the cast iron pan.  
My dear, my dear daughter-in-law, abandon all other talk,  
And live as a proper wife.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Jujube tree by the window,  
At the thatched roof house,  
Click-clack, as I weave,  
The dog in the front yard barks, and looking out,  
A letter has come, a letter has come.  
Holding a single sheet of stationery, I see  
News of my parents' death has arrived.  

Entering the front room,  
Slowly, slowly, father-in-law,  
News of my parents' death has arrived.  
Hey you, shameless woman,  
Out in the back hill,  
You left all the barley fields uncultivated and went away.  

Come out to the front room,  
Slowly, slowly, mother-in-law,  
News of my parents' death has arrived.  
I wove all the fine hemp cloth,  
If you want to leave, then leave.  

Having woven all the fine hemp cloth and preparing to leave,  
My older brother, who has loose hair,  
Though he is well-educated, didn’t even send a letter.  
Though my family is renowned for weaving silk,  
I didn’t even receive a single handkerchief.  

Entering the room where mother died,  
There’s nothing left, only a pile of ashes remaining.  

Dear husband, listen to my words,  
I am a daughter.  
Build a mound on the front mountain,  
Build a mound on the back mountain.  
Oh, the wailing and crying resound,  
Who could be crying?  

The villagers gather,  
Oh, how miserable and pitiful,  
The daughter of this house has come.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How is life after marriage?  
Even if the chili pepper is said to be spicy,  
It is spicier than that.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How has life been in your in-laws' house after three years?  
Don't say things like that.  
They said chili peppers are spicy,  
But living with the in-laws is even spicier.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, my mother,  
Why did you give birth to me?  
I cannot live, I cannot live,  
I cannot live because of sorrow.  
When my mother raised me,  
She fed me milk sitting down,  
She fed me rice standing up.  
Baby, baby, grow quickly,  
Grow quickly and grow stout.  
I was raised well and properly,  
So why am I like this?  
I pity my parents,  
When they raised me,  
The spot they did not know, I lay on,  
The spot they truly knew, my parents lay on.  
When giving rice porridge, they gave me the poor porridge,  
My parents ate the good porridge.  
I was raised well and properly,  
But where have my parents gone?  
They do not recognize me.  

—Hungal Song

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At one year old, my mother died; at two years old, my father died.  
When I, Si-u-shi, was fifteen years old, my father-in-law was coming and going.  
When I got married, my sky-like father-in-law  
scolded me for being small, scolded me for being short.  
Look at my mother-in-law's walk, how hurriedly she goes out,  
scolding me for being small, scolding me for being short.  
In the men's quarters, father-in-law was sunning himself in the glass room.  
He washed his face in the washroom and ate breakfast.  
"Oh, you wicked woman, take it yourself or give it to the dog,"  
In the women's quarters, sister-in-law was sunning herself in the glass room.  
She washed her face in the washroom and ate breakfast.  
"You sly woman like a pollack, a woman who behaves like a plate,  
take it yourself or give it to the dog; such a sorrow, such a sorrow."  
I took the burden, such a sorrow, and entered the temple.  
The old monk was sleeping, the young monk was making shoes.  
"Monk, monk, great monk, please shave this child's head."  
Shaving is no problem, but the family line is noble, so it cannot be shaved.  
Although the family line is noble, please shave this child's head.  
After shaving one side of the head, thoughts of my parental home came to mind.  
After shaving the other side, thoughts of my parental home came to mind even more.  
"Monk, monk, great monk, with the 108-cord rosary around my neck,  
let's beg near my parental home, please beg, please beg.  
My daughter goes to do laundry, daughter-in-law, please beg."  
"Monk, monk, great monk, going to the bamboo grove in the forest,  
there is no one there."

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Oh my, oh my, my mother  
Why do you push me to do this  
Should I say I have this kind of illness?/Sopyal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, how was married life in your in-laws' house?  
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
how was married life in your in-laws' house?  
Oh, woman, don’t say that.  
On the slippery, unstable floor,  
even placing the spoon was difficult.  
Oh, woman, don’t say that.  
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
stop talking about married life in the in-laws' house.  
Don't even talk about it.  
The younger brother-in-law with the red bean stalk, don’t speak,  
the younger sister-in-law with the bean stalk, don’t speak either.  
Don’t talk about married life in the in-laws' house.  
The cloth washer used as a tray cleaner, they take it all away.  
Don’t talk about married life in the in-laws' house.  
After ten years of marriage, returning to my parents’ home,  
even the mountains and streams have changed.  
Don’t talk, don’t talk, don’t talk about married life in the in-laws' house.  
My father-in-law's words were bitter,  
my mother-in-law’s words smelled fragrant,  
don’t talk, don’t talk, don’t talk about married life in the in-laws' house.  
The village in-laws' house is an in-laws' house,  
and the family in-laws' house is also an in-laws' house.  
Don’t talk about married life in the in-laws' house.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even if living with in-laws is good,  
The real flavor is in loving quarrels.  
Even if the pumpkin shoots are blue,  
Is it right for sisters-in-law to quarrel like that?  
Bitterness is hidden in the front yard,  
Bitterness is hidden in the backyard.  
Even if the bitterness and hardship are sharp,  
Will it be as sharp as the bond between sisters-in-law?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On a scorching hot day like fire,  
The mountain, like a field plowed,  
Tilling one furrow after another,  
An obituary came, an obituary came,  
The news of my mother’s death came.  
Hair undone and disheveled,  
Taking off the raindrops and sticking them into the ground,  
As one furrow turns around,  
The crows caw and the grasshoppers chirp,  
As another furrow turns around,  
The oxen sound all around,  
As another furrow turns around,  
The sound of the drum naturally arises.  
It is sorrowful and makes one feel bitter,  
This hateful life of living with in-laws.  
I was only ten years old when I went,  
My husband treated me poorly,  
The mother-in-law and father-in-law,  
The mother-in-law is like a female dog,  
The father-in-law is like a male dog,  
Living with in-laws like this,  
Now the news of my mother’s death has come.  
Have you ever heard such a thing?  
(Stopped in the middle) “I can’t do it.”

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how is married life?  
It's difficult to set the table properly on a slippery surface.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Some people are lucky and live long lives,  
But why is my fate like this?  
Climbing the back hill, banging on the wooden crutches,  
Oh dear, oh dear, why is my fate like this?  
Now lifting the crutches, crossing over towering mountains.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Even when a close friend, a swallow, speaks, it is difficult to understand.  
Even placing a handmade mat on the board is difficult.  
Even when a close friend, a swallow, says "Hey, come here, come here,"  
it is difficult to understand.  
When tears come to my eyes, blood flows from yours.

label: Lament_lament
translation: - A sharp mind like a three-step knife

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after marriage, I went to weed the field.
I weeded the field like the ancestral village, the field I inherited from Samsigol.
The lovebird’s tail kept circling inside the bowl of broth.
After eating this, I cannot live.
Like a three-layered comb, I shaved one side of my head.
When I shaved one side, it became like an ox beyond the ridge.
When I shaved both sides long and wide, the ridge became like a river.
That river, they say, has a pair of ducks, a pair of geese,
floating lightly.
Dressed and dressed, wearing robes and gowns,
carrying peonies,
hanging the twine,
I was about to go to Songgwangsa Temple in Suncheon to work as a monk.
The lord who was going to Seoul rode a graceful horse,
entered calmly and peacefully.
Bowing on horseback, flat and low, then he got off abruptly.
Why would a monk bow to a rider?
Dear lord, dear husband, I do not know if it could be so.
He got off the horse abruptly, then grabbed his wooden staff,
wearing a long robe made of twelve patterned panels, what kind of monk is this?
What is the silver hairpin on his head?
What is the silver ring on his wooden staff’s neckpiece?
What is an ox-hair brush on his foot?
Let’s go, let’s go, go home.
What kind of life is this to live like this?
After three years, I will go.
When I entered your house and opened your door,
all the wooden furniture and woodenware were gone.
After living three years and coming home, the yard has become a mugwort field.
I went to my father-in-law’s grave like a lantern,
lantern flowers bloom bright, broom flowers bloom bright.
At mother-in-law’s grave,
Evening primroses bloom brightly, broom flowers bloom brightly.
At my sister-in-law’s grave,
Evening primroses bloom brightly, broom flowers bloom brightly.
When I went to my husband’s grave,
Love flowers bloomed brightly, peonies bloomed brightly.
Dear lord, dear husband, after living three years, open the door.
The door opened wide, and I stepped inside.
Having sons and daughters, I lived well for a hundred generations.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On the first full moon of the first lunar month  
... they started a procession

They knocked it off, it broke  
They knocked it off

After three days of digging pits  
They came

Turn over, turn over  
Turn over to your four directions

So, after three days  
They flew back

They attached it, they attached it  
They attached it like flying arrows

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
Is our mother a swallow?  
She only builds a house and then leaves  
Is our mother a butterfly?  
She only lays eggs and then leaves  
Is our mother a sunspot's house?  
Is the sparrow a friend?  
She heartlessly only lays eggs and then leaves

label: Lament_lament
translation:
How is your life in your in-laws' house? Plum blossoms, like a sign of troubles and dementia,  
Hung on the end of the perch, folding all the tears that came and went.  
Oh my dear, how harsh is this life of living in my in-laws' house.  
My crying is not without reason.  
There are many hardships in this high-placed life, and many words about living with in-laws.  
If you can't endure living in your in-laws' house, you keep cutting and cutting, cutting your hair.  
I tore twelve pieces of cloth and sewed them, tore five pieces to make a sack.  
My husband wears a long robe and a pointed hat, begging like a monk.  
Should I go be a monk's assistant?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, why do you cry so much?  
Did you give birth to me just to struggle?  
You gave birth to me with warm rice soup on the cold floor,  
With steamed rice mixed with oxygen,  
You gave birth to me,  
But why am I like this now?  
When you raised me,  
You were surprised when I cried,  
You raised me holding me half-heartedly,  
But why did my fate and life turn out this way?  
Did my mother give birth to me just to struggle?

- Singing voice  
>

label: Lament_lament
translation:
My husband  
was buried in the pits of all things,  
but our old man, who died after a wild boar’s hind foot struck his chest,  
was left only with a few measures of hemp cloth in Mapo.  
That corpse was left neglected.

-Heunggeuretaeng (a type of traditional Korean song)  
-Reprise

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In March, at Jinjin Sea, the maiden heads to the Jiseon field,  
Should she carry one bundle or two bundles?  
Having carried three bundles, a letter arrives, a letter arrives,  
A letter comes from her parental home. She takes it with one hand,  
Receiving it with both hands, it’s a letter announcing her mother’s death.  
Father, father, a letter arrived about our mother’s passing.  
“Put on your hemp clothes and go,” says the mother-in-law,  
“Mother died, there’s a letter.” The mother-in-law says,  
“Have some food before you go.”  
Asking her husband,  
“If you don’t go, who else will?”  
Taking off her raincoat and holding it close,  
Letting down her hair and walking slowly,  
Taking off her shoes, holding them in her hand,  
Turning once, the crows cawed loudly,  
Turning again, the sound of the threshing board echoed,  
Turning once more, the wailing resounded,  
Entering the courtyard of her parental home, the sound of street vendors echoed.  
Eldest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“You should push them away; if you keep messing, you came here,”  
“I want to see my parents’ faces once more.”  
Second sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“You should stop causing trouble; you came here,”  
“I want to see my parents’ faces once more.”  
Youngest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“Open the gate a little,”  
“Open the gate and go inside,  
Walk around the room once,  
The room is wide and empty, like an empty banquet hall.”  
Eldest sister-in-law among nine siblings,  
“If you clear the salt field,  
You’ll eat and I’ll eat too.”  
“There’s some leftover purge water,  
You get your share, I get mine.”  
“When the scorched rice is done,  
You have yours, I have mine.”

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seventeen or eighteen years old, came here as a bride  
With a plain face, married to a man  
With a small face, married to a man with a small face  
In a cramped room was the newlywed wife  
As the wife, she was young  
How should I live on?  
My dear, my dear, how can I live?  
Neither water nor mountains are kind  
In this place, living is hard  
Turning and turning on the floor  
Even using chopsticks is hard  
Breaking a round watermelon  
Even serving rice is hard  
Carrying a bundle of chestnuts on my front  
Should I go this way or that way?  
When I think about it, tears overflow  
Choked by tears, I cannot go on  
Wanting to go to my maternal home  
But I cannot get past the gate  
Whether I go this way or that way  
I feel completely lost, giving up everything  
Ah, I wish I could go back to the factory  
Where would be best to go?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Dori dori, the conical hat house  
Raised their daughter Hanna beautifully  
In Jeollanam-do, in the village of Sau  
Just three days after getting married  
All the men are stepping out quietly  
If they say step out, we step out  
If they say hide, we hide  
In the cleanest single cloth  
What is the meaning of the neat street?  
In hands stained by silver rings  
What is the meaning of the bundles of nails?  
In hair stained with gold powder  
What is the meaning of the topknot?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
I was scolded again and again to make adult-sized straw sandals.  
Not knowing the middle character for "make," I ended up making them wrong.  
My father and mother scolded me.  
But in the end, I made the straw sandals.  
After making them, I found that walking on the snowy field was difficult because they were not made well.  
However, since my father and mother told me to make shoes with proper soles,  
I made those, and they turned out well.  
After that, I made shoes with proper soles and wore them around,  
and my arms became strong.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
When it’s a bit chilly, come into my arms,  
When the bamboo fence is tall, lean on my arms.  
With mandarin ducks, a golden hairpin, and a pine bamboo fence placed by the pillow,  
A brass chamber pot placed neatly by the bed.  
Looking up, there’s a conch shell tray; looking down, a patterned straw mat.  
On the patterned straw mat in the sleeping room’s floor—what’s going on?  
Why is there a pillow in the rice measuring box where you used to tuck your head?  
Why are there iron chains on the handcuffs you used to wear?  
Why is there a red hemp jeogori over the clothes you wore?  
Why is there a straw shoe for the sharp pointed shoes you used to wear?  
Oh, let’s live on with the sound of the side drum and the clatter of the earthenware jar.  
Oh, how good it is—this feeling I can’t deny.  
When is sleep ever at ease? Just now, I was blowing on it for warmth.  
Oh, this feeling—I cannot deny it.

— When playing, lamenting about fate?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
- A three-layered good head  
- Called again

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At Daechon, a vast sea  
A naturally grown old pine tree  
If you count its branches, there are twelve  
If you count the leaves, there are three hundred  
On those branches  
What fruit has grown?  
The sun and the moon have grown  
They picked the sun and supported it from outside  
They picked the moon and supported it from inside  
They picked the big star and placed it at the head of the table  
They picked the small star and placed it in the middle  
They spun the thread of double knots  
They tied the thread of outer knots  
Going to sell it at the Seoul market  
Who made this pouch?  
A Seoul lady, I made it  
The one who made this pouch  
Whether given silver or gold  
I don’t want silver or money  
For a hundred years, living and dying  
Is it the youthful guesthouse or the colorful market?  
Is it the willow that used to tether a donkey?  
In the wide fields of green water  
Is it the place where my beloved tied up?  
Where my beloved tied up is on fire  
The cup where I drank has rust stains  
Sitting, thinking, lying down, thinking  
Only thoughts of my beloved come naturally

label: Lament_lament
translation:
A bout of hiccups and a vast rice field,
One bundle, then two bundles,
Suddenly a wind blew,
And a letter flew in.
With one hand, I caught it flat,
With both hands, I unfolded it,
The news of my parents’ death had arrived.
I threw down the hoe,
And entered the guests’ room,
Dear father-in-law,
The news of my parents’ death has come.
Go, go away,
How can I live without you?
I went into the main room,
Dear mother-in-law,
The news of my parents’ death has come.
Go, go away,
How can I live without you?
Sister-in-law’s family,
The news of my parents’ death has come.
Cleared the dining table,
Cleared the big table,
Cleared the side table,
And filled the kettle with water.
Go, go away,
How can I live without you?
In the kitchen,
The young master working hard,
The news of my parents’ death has come.
If the young mistress leaves,
Who will decorate the back room?
If the young mistress leaves,
Please return soon.
After one full lap,
The wailing echoed,
After another full lap,
My elder brothers cried,
Good-looking youth,
Don’t take away my letter,
Elder brother’s wife,
Good weaver, don’t take away the handkerchief.
After one full lap,
The dog of the afterlife barked loudly,
After another lap,
The rooster of the afterlife crowed,
After one more lap,
The funeral sounds echoed.
(This funeral is called Geumosa. When the grieving relatives attend the funeral of the deceased parents, the head is shaved, and they enter the temple. They live there for a while, but when they return, all have passed away, leaving only the grave. It's said that those who lived well bloom beautifully, and those who did not, bloom poorly. That’s the story.)
Let’s go see, let’s go see,
To the hometown, let’s go see.
When I went, all had passed away,
Only the grave remained.
At father-in-law’s grave,
The tiger lily blooms beautifully.
At mother-in-law’s grave,
The acacia flower blooms beautifully.
At sister-in-law’s grave,
The halong flower blooms beautifully.
At sister-in-law’s grave,
The lotus flower blooms beautifully.
At husband’s grave,
The rosehip flower blooms beautifully.
(They lived well and happily.)

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, cousin brother-in-law,  
How is life in the husband’s house?  
They say life in the husband’s house is good,  
But at every word’s end,  
This hand like a scolding woman’s,  
Has become like a grinding hook.  
This hair like a chrysanthemum,  
Has all turned into bristly pig’s hair.  
Brother-in-law, brother-in-law, how is life in the husband’s house?  
A face like a bindweed flower  
Has become like a daylily flower.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The ache in July and August knows its time and trembles,  
But the pest in my house doesn't know the season and causes trouble.  
I'm scared of the harsh in-law life, I can't live like this.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after getting married, I was told to go hoe the field.  
With a folded towel around my neck and wearing the silk hat from my in-laws,  
Carrying a sickle on my shoulder, I stood on the hill behind the village.  
I picked grass leaves, lit a fire with them, broke small branches, and made a small support.  
I went to the long furrow in that field and listened.  
After one round of hoeing and looking back, the wild geese were crying and flying away.  
After two rounds and looking back, a letter of condolence for the mother-in-law's death had come.  
When I returned home, my mother-in-law said,  
"Cook some barley rice and put it on the old straw mat that’s been there for three years."  
My mother-in-law said, "Your mother passed away, but you should at least eat this rice."  
Twelve layers of folded silk handkerchiefs were piled up thickly.  
I tore off one layer, wrapped it around my neck, and went begging somewhere.  
They gave me ash-rice, but I spilled that ash-rice.  
I just took that ash-rice and went nowhere with it.  
I lay down in a wealthy house's storage shed.  
Looking this way, there was the moon; looking that way, the sun.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Seong-nim, Seong-nim, cousin Seong-nim  
You said you’d come out, but you disappeared  
If only you had given me one measure of rice  
Seong would eat, and I would eat  
If the New Year's water is thick  
Am I the master of the Seongso, or are you?  
If something sagging comes out  
Am I the master of Seonggae, or are you?  
If chaff comes out  
Am I the master of Seongdak, or are you?  
Dungdangae, all dungdangae  
Dang-gi, dungdangae, dungdangae  
Who made the dungdangae sound?  
The cheeky big kid, I made it.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother died when I was one year old,  
Father died when I was two years old,  
At three years old, I got married,  
When I opened the main room door,  
There was a mother-in-law like a hen,  
When I opened the love room door,  
There was a father-in-law like a tiger,  
When I opened the laughter room door,  
There was a sister-in-law like a parrot,  
Going from this room to that room,  
I laid out twelve panels of blankets,  
Carrying seven panels on my back,  
Wearing four panels as a skirt on my head,  
I'm going, I'm going, I am going,  
Grumbling, I am going.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Jujube tree by the window  
At the bamboo fence house  
Click-clack, weaving away  
A dog barks under the floor  
Opening the window  
A letter has come, a letter has come  
Holding the letter  
It’s news of a parent's death  
Entering the front room  
Softly, softly, father-in-law — () again  
The news of a parent's death has come  
At the back yard, barley field  
Please harvest it all and go  
Entering the front room  
Softly, softly, mother-in-law  
The news of a parent's death has come  
Please finish weaving the hemp cloth and go  
As the front corner turns  
The royal carriage sways  
As the second corner turns  
The mourning procession is coming ()  
As the third corner turns  
The peddler’s voice is heard  
As the fourth corner turns  
The twelve elder brothers  
Wails resonate deeply  
Oh peddler going ahead  
Oh traveling merchant behind  
Please leave this traveling merchant alone  
Hey, you reckless woman  
You ought to have come by now  
Though my elder brother writes well  
I haven’t received even a letter  
Though my elder brother wove nicely  
I didn’t even receive a handkerchief  
Entering the place where my mother gave birth  
Only ashes remain  
As the wails resound  
The neighbors gather  
Saying the daughter has come and gone  
It’s so heartbreaking, so heartbreaking  
So painful that my parents have died  
As the third corner turns  
The peddler’s voice is heard

label: Lament_lament
translation:
At Hanyang, they exchange bed sheets, bustling about tidying up.
With lively stitching, they walk to Baekgwang Temple.
They fasten red sleeves and lay them out to dry in the dew.
At Eundaeru, they hang the night carriage outside the gate.
Scholars going up, please pay respects to the mid-summer offering.
Mid-summer offerings are good, but without money, I cannot see them.
Scholars coming down, please pay respects to the mid-summer offering.
Mid-summer offerings are good, but without money, I cannot see them.
A little young sister-in-law holds a thistle knife in her arms,
Willing to tear apart the mid-summer offering, to tear it apart.
If you are to tear it, then tear it properly.
Planting hot pepper shoots in the front field, and horseradish in the back field.
Even if hot pepper and horseradish are spicy, can they be as spicy as a sister-in-law?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother,  
How was married life?  
Hey, don’t say that,  
That talk causes dementia and death.  
Wipe your tears, it’s all over.  
Older sister-in-law had a good married life,  
They brewed nuruk liquor.  
Our married life wasn’t good,  
They brewed fermented fish sauce.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother, how was married life in your in-laws' house?  
This hair of mine, here and there, has all fallen out.  
These hands of mine, like branches, have become rough and worn out. /Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Clear and bright, clear and bright, I endured the arbitrary hardships of my love.  
With a sprout, the root spread, and upward, the branch extended.  
Breaking off a pair of branches, I hung them in my lover’s room.  
Is the flower better, or is my lover better? The flower is better, or is my lover better?  
Ah, this wretched woman, this cunning woman.  
Live well with the flower. / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In the vast fields as wide as the sky,  
Farming like a bird's nest,  
Extinguishing like the clouds,  
Pressing down like a half moon,  
Placing beside the rice container,  
It's even more painful to endure hunger.  
Oh bridegroom, inside the silence, inside mimicry,  
If you hate seeing me, then abandon me.  
Water-green, muddy-colored dementia,  
Before it turns dark, it splits me apart.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, dear brother,  
Coming over Bungogae, brother comes.  
Who will go to greet brother?  
I will, with a half-moon shell.  
What side dishes shall I prepare for brother?  
Pickled peppers like ox horns,  
Torn into pieces like this and that.  
Cook red beans like cherries,  
Cook glutinous rice like sticky teeth,  
And pack them in layers neatly.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
It's my fate, my fate  
Who would have known  
That my life would turn out like this?  
Because I couldn't serve the ancestral rites  
What does it matter if others serve?  
Why couldn't I serve the ancestral rites?  
What does it matter if others serve?  
Only heaven and earth know  
Who would understand my situation?  
Who would understand?  
It's my fate, my life  
Why did my mother  
Leave me here on this island  
And go somewhere else?  
It's my fate, my life  
I can't do it, I can't do it  
I can't serve the ancestral rites  
Who would have known  
That my life would turn out like this?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Older brother, older brother, cousin brother-in-law  
How is living with the in-laws?  
Don’t even mention living with the in-laws.  
Even if the skewered food is said to be spicy,  
Living with the in-laws is not as spicy as that.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Placing it next to the rice container, my inner self aches with sorrow.  
Placing it next to the rice container, my big bone aches with sorrow. / Sopal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Dori dori Satgatjibi  
Raised daughter Hanna beautifully  
She cried and cried  
When she went to the island region  
Only three days after marriage  
She’s told to weed the rice seedlings  

When she wraps twelve folds twice  
Wrap, wrap and put on  
She goes to the field to work  
Sits on the front field  
A tiger sits in the back field  
The tiger in the front field is sleepy  
Only the sound of the wind blows softly  

The narrow field edge  
Is left about half a crescent  
When she enters the house  
Her mother-in-law softly  
Carries a bundle of firewood  
Comes out to check the water channel  

"Maeneul-aga, Maeneul-aga  
Which baby, this is not the time for the ‘Jeongsim’ (traditional meal time) yet  
Which baby will come in now?"  
Softly, the mother-in-law  
Comes to the front door banging  
"This is not the time for Jeongsim yet  
Which baby will come in now?"  

When she urgently asks  
The petite sister-in-law  
Says, "Brother, Brother, our brother  
It is not the time for Jeongsim yet  
Which baby is coming in?"  

"I have to take care of the house  
Go across the next room  
Look at the door curtain  
Come here, come here  
Mother-in-law, come here"

Yesterday at the big market  
The emergency ladder was hung  
They went across the market  
Put up a patch-like jinseongjang (a type of shield)  
And floated the riverside laughter  

When the scholar’s guardian came  
And opened the talking place  
The scholar’s guardian didn’t come  
She took a sip here and there  

The thick pants loosened  
The thin pants got torn  
She took two sips here and there  
Went away, went just like that  

The scholar’s guardian came again  
"Get up, get up  
A pitiful married life  
Why take a nap?  
A pitiful married life  
Why take a nap?  

Get up softly here  
Get up softly there"  
Though told repeatedly, she didn’t get up  
She went across to the next room  
"Sire, please come in too  
Mother, please come in too  

Whose front storehouse is this?  
The front storehouse is yours too  
Whose back storehouse is this?  
The back storehouse is yours too  

The front storehouse will be leased and leased  
The back storehouse will be leased and leased  
When the lease is full  
I will cross over, I am going"

label: Lament_lament
translation: - Older brother, older brother, cousin older brother

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mom, mom, our mom,  
Don’t study every day,  
You can’t even do the three-bow ceremony properly.  
Dad, dad, our dad,  
Don’t study every day,  
You can’t even study writing properly.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, why did you give birth to me?  
Did you give birth to me only to make me suffer?  
After I married, when I went to work in the fields a little,  
Under the blazing sun, I worked hard in the fields,  
From dusk until dawn, I worked, but I couldn’t finish even half the furrows.  
When I went back home, look at my mother-in-law moving around,  
Using one grain of rice to make porridge to plant the sprouts,  
I just couldn’t eat it, so she said, “Dog, dog, you eat it.”  
Even when she gave some to the dog, the dog wouldn’t eat it.  
I can’t live this married life; with twelve lines of wrinkles,  
I’ve shed all my tears. Mother, mother, our mother,  
Take me away, take me away, just take me away.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother is coming, brother is coming, at Mungogae, brother is coming  
Brother's pasture, who took it? Like a half-moon, I took it  
How can you be a half-moon? A bluish half-moon you are  
After living three years in marriage, a three-layered veil appears on the forehead  
The seedlings, the seedlings all wither away  
Tiny cracks, tiny cracks in the sandalwood bridge  
Walking steps were difficult  
The crouched younger brother-in-law  
The place where words were spoken was difficult

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother, cousin brother, what do you do weaving hemp cloth?  
When I go to my in-laws, won't you even light a candle?

Brother, brother, what do you do weaving hemp cloth?  
The cloth woven at night is moonlight cloth, the cloth woven during the day is sunlight cloth.  
Weave both the sunlight cloth and the moonlight cloth, but only make my product.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, look at the sacred hall. After weaving fabric, she comes down and eats all the leftover rice in the back yard.  
Don’t say that again just now; are you full after eating the leftover rice?  
Why don’t you wear the clothes made from the fabric you wove? / Sop'al

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother is coming, brother is coming, at the gate, brother is coming  
Brother's village, someone said, like a half moon, I go  
How are you a half moon? It’s a dark blue half moon  
After living three years in the in-laws' house, the three-layered skirt's hem is frayed  
Worry, worry, all falling out, fine cracks, gray hair  
Walking is difficult  
The small brother-in-law, crouched down,  
The place where he spoke was difficult.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Fate, fate, my fate  
When my mother and father were alive,  
What did they eat, and how did I grow up?  
I couldn't live well in this cruel world.  
Leaving the mainland and all its hardships behind, where does one go?  
Mother, mother, my mother,  
When I was born, and also when others are born,  
Though men and women come into this world,  
What kind of destiny is so harsh?  
Living life,  
Though I give birth to sons and daughters,  
Unable to raise them properly,  
There is endless lamentation about fate.  
Child, endure, this is my destiny.  
If I die, I am still young,  
If I live, it is full of hardship.  
Children, when you were born,  
After ten months in the womb,  
I lay down in the real place,  
And you lay down in the empty place.  
Though I fed you three meals a day,  
What has appeared from that?  
Such is the world.  
When I lived in this world,  
There was only a small fire in the yard,  
If it burns only on the outside, is that the person?  
If it burns only inside, is that not the person?  
Look at life in this world.  
The fire in my heart,  
Should I try burning it like the fire on Namsan?  

– Heunggeul sound

label: Lament_lament
translation:
On a hot day as fiery as fire, when I weeded a field as sharp as a needle, I weeded one row, two rows, three times, but unlike other lunches, this lunch never came out. 

When I went home and asked for rice, my sister-in-law became angry and said, "Is this work or what? Did you come here to eat lunch?" 

My mother-in-law became angry and said the same thing, "Is this work or what? Did you come here to eat rice?"

Eating three-year-old barley rice and three-year-old soybean paste with chili, I said, "Damn you, get angry."

After eating that, tears poured down like rain.

After eating that meal, I tore one piece to make a pointed hat, tore another piece to make a bag, and sang, "I’m leaving, I’m leaving, I'm really leaving."

Returning home after ten years, I found the field overgrown with mugwort.

In front of my mother-in-law’s grave, wild ginger flowers had bloomed.

In front of my sister-in-law’s grave, coltsfoot flowers had bloomed.

In front of my father-in-law’s grave, a crown flower had bloomed.

In front of my husband’s grave, love flowers had bloomed. (And so, I was ruined.)

label: Lament_lament
translation:
The mother-in-law nags a lot in the car near the solar plexus.  
On Namsan peak, Bonghak sits and hoots like an owl, brother-in-law.  
In the back field, we plant gourds, spicy and salty, tasty things.  
In front of the tavern, sushi hides, twisting and turning like a stir.  
On the sushi crab, a swallow lands, paying for the house, sister-in-law.  
In front of love, plant flowers, mumbling and mumbling, my dear.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, mother, our mother  
There is much talk and many hardships in married life  
There is much hard work and much talk  
I can’t live like this–  
Do they feed me or clothe me?  
No matter what I do, I can’t live like this  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Please take me away, please take me away  
I came out to live freely  
Was this household so harsh?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
A.  
Mother, mother, our mother  
You gave birth to me in a difficult time  
And now everything is so bitter  
Mother, mother, our mother  
Why did you bring me into this world?  
I can’t live, I really can’t live  
I simply cannot endure this  
Oh my-

Mother, mother, our mother  
Our mother like an open field  
Why did you give birth to me?  
Everything is bitter, bitter, bitter  
I can’t live, I really can’t live  
I honestly cannot live  
Words fail me, tears fall  

B.  
Our mother  
Why did you bring me into this world?  
If you were going to give birth to someone like me  
It would have been better to give birth to a crimson rose  
Rather than me, who has to wear tattered clothes  
I simply cannot endure this-  
Oh, the pain and sorrow have no limit  
There is no end-

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Brother, brother  
Brother is coming  
I, like a half-moon, will go to meet him

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three-Character Phrase, Single-Wrapped Handkerchief  
Even if soaked like dew  
There is no one who knows me at all  
Buying a day without papers  
Placing it in front of the gate  
Where to go, not coming  
Clever rooster, don’t crow  
Barking dog, don’t bark  
It all hurts my heart  
Where has the beloved gone  
Will the barking dog not bark?  
Will the crying rooster not cry?  
In the market of life, roosters crow  
Living life,  
The black crow caws harshly  
Is today a far-off day?  
Tying the single-wrapped handkerchief  
Hanging it dripping  
My love, my dear love  
In the time of courting for a hundred years’ life  
Where has the promise gone?  
Leaving brothers and parents behind  
Leaving the Yangcheon parents beside  
Leaving the evergreen tree beside  
Promised to live a hundred years together  
No news from anywhere  
When the moon rises, I think  
When the sun sets, I think  
There is no dark night at all  
Suddenly and inexplicably  
The black crow caws harshly  
What news could come today?  
The crow caws joyfully  
The old color dims  
Looking at the world,  
On the way to Bodujip, as morning breaks  
Even if I starve from three meals and seven times  
The sound of the black crow’s cry  
Even happily, the hand goes away  
After making some noise  
The messenger came, the messenger came  
What messenger has come?  
Putting aside front and back doors  
I heard that the beloved is coming  
Even the dried-up rice is  
Salty but sweet  
No matter how much the Yangcheon parents  
Carefully arranged like young iron  
You said to live a hundred years  
Will this ever come true?  
The six children, sons and daughters  
What era will they face?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Wheel, oh wheel, wild grass wheel  
Oh, spin round and round, wild grass wheel  
Yang Seol-joo, Gonggul-dong, a sound with a good tune  
Loading half a catty, the playing sheep still knows the young master’s heart / Sophal

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Mother, Mother, our Mother  
When our Mother passed away  
With nine strands of hair tied up  
Under twelve folds of satin  
Receiving the midday and evening prayers  
(Unable to transcribe) as she left  
They vowed to live together for a hundred years  
So how could I be like this?  
Mother, Mother, our Mother  
Even so, it is frustrating  
When will I also live on  
Give birth to a son and have a daughter  
And live supporting each other?  
Mother, Mother, our Mother  
She never comes once to the river  
Leaving me like a rice sprout  
In the yard all tidy and neat  
Like a flower petal, our Mother  
She used to come when she left  
But she never comes once to the river  
Last night in a dream  
My deceased parents came  
When I woke up from the dream  
I was alone in the empty room  
Hurriedly opening the wooden window  
The busy servant got upset  
Covering the dishes  
I went up the back mountain stream  
Calling out “Mother”  
The mountain echoed back in reply  
Calling three times repeatedly  
At the edge of the straw mat cushion  
The water in the stream replied  
Coming down to the house  
The rain cleared and I lay down  
The rain stopped, and it was a river  
That is a river  
A pair of ducks and a pair of geese  
Floating leisurely, making noise

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Oh mother, oh mother, my central son, my central son,  
What am I to endure for hundreds of years in the high sky?  
Why am I sent to the high sky in the midst of millions of homes?  
Oh mother, oh mother, every village, every village is mine,  
Every alley, every alley is mine,  
Even thousands of li away, I am exiled.  
Living as a daughter-in-law is so difficult,  
When I go to my parents-in-law’s room,  
The mother-in-law's face,  
When I go to the big room, the father-in-law's face,  
When I enter the relatives, the sister-in-law is strict,  
Oh mother, oh mother, I cannot live like this,  
Please take me away on the day of respect,  
I have no energy to live,  
Am I to be exiled thousands of li away?

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Three days after getting married,  
My father-in-law went to the mountain, and my father went to the big mountain.  
Pouring alcohol in front of the river and mountains, giving my husband glances,  
I woke up, I woke up, breaking the village’s sorrowful drinking bowl.  
What my father said,  
If you give money, you can buy the village’s sorrowful drinking bowl,  
But the morning dew on the balsam flower only lasts once when it goes away.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
In Jeongseon-eup, the waterwheel keeps turning day and night on the corkwood raft,  
But where has my husband gone?  
Arirang Arirang Arariyo,  
Over the Arirang Pass, over the hills we go.  

The one who went to the communal grave only comes back during the funeral rites,  
But my husband, does he ever come back?  
Ariari-rang sseuri-sseuri-rang arariyo,  
Let me cross over the Arirang Pass, over the hills.  

Follow me, follow me, just follow me,  
Even if it’s a thousand miles of thorny path, just follow me.  
Arirang arirang arariyo,  
Where can I go to find my dear husband?  

I bore this son when I was thirty, at twenty-six I had him,  
The younger son and the elder son were born when I was twenty-two,  
Arirang arirang arariyo,  
Over the Arirang Pass, over the hills we go.  

In a strange land, I got married,  
I got a bad reputation, wandering from house to house just to get a meal,  
Still, when young, I was so restless,  
Restless to the point I’d cough every day and just stay home,  
Arirang arirang arariyo,  
Over the Arirang Pass, do I go?  

Now I have two children,  
Yet I don’t even scratch the peaceful places.

label: Lament_lament
translation:
My husband  
looks like a barren field  
Wind, blow  
Blow for just three months and ten days

My husband, that rascal  
On the fourteenth day of August this year  
When the rice grains were all ripening  
Got his chest crushed by a wild boar's hind foot and died  
Our late husband left with a three-foot-long hemp cloth in a hemp sack  
Now, all that’s left is to cover the corpse

label: Lament_lament
translation:
Hinga hinga cousin hinga, how is married life?
Oh no, no, don’t even mention married life.
It’s hard to handle small tasks on a tiny kitchen shelf.
It’s hard to wash a small watermelon or serve rice.
It’s even hard to talk about the dowry received.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Blow, blow, blow, blow  
What kind of iron is this iron?  
Even the Yellow River is iron from Jaeryong  
Blow, blow, blow  
Fluttering well, blowing well  
Is the iron strong, does it blow well?  
Blow, blow, blow  
The iron is good, it blows well  
A wealthy man has appeared in Jang’an  
Blow, blow, blow  
Fluttering well, it blows well  

»

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Hush-a-bye, hush-a-bye  
Our baby sleeps well  
Hush-a-bye, my baby sleeps  
Our baby sleeps well  
If our mother were to come  
She would come to breastfeed, right?

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Woorijajang Woorijajang  
Jajangjajang Jajangjajang, you sleep well  
Our baby sleeps well  
Golden child, silver child  
If given gold, I will buy you  
If given silver, I will buy you  
On weekdays, harmony and friendship prevail  
Jajangjajang Woorijajang  
Our baby sleeps well  
Our baby, jajangjajang  
Be as deep and firm as Mount Taesan  
Be as strong as reconciliation  
Our baby sleeps well  
Silver child, golden child  
If given silver, I will buy you  
If given gold, will I buy you?  
Be as strong as Mount Taesan  
Be as deep and deep as reconciliation  
Silver child, golden child

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Dunggae dunggae, dunggae-ya  
This dunggae is whose dunggae  
Look here, it's my dunggae  
Look there, it's my dunggae  
No matter how you look, it's my dunggae  
Dunggae dunggae, dunggae-ya  
Float gently, grow big.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Is the seed core the fruit core?  
Is the fruit core the seed core?  
Is the golden belt the waist?  
Is Mr. Samho the head?  
Is Mr. Tissue the foot?  
Is the hand holding a brush?  
Behind the award, shall I place a daughter?  
Under the blue paper, shall I place honey?  
Both female and male dogs have two jars,  
Ferns and rice wine also have two jars.  
Is the square and neat thing tofu?  
Is the faraway fern a jujube shoot?  
Are there flower buds on this mountain and that?  
Is the estuary fertile chestnuts?  
Are there bonds of brotherly love among siblings?  
Is there a sense of community in the village?  
And filial piety toward parents?

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
-Lullaby, lullaby, go to sleep  
Our baby, go to sleep  
Our baby will sleep well  
Lying down in the flower field  
That child cannot sleep  
Lying down in the dog poop field  
Baby, baby, go to sleep  
Our baby, go to sleep  
Hurry, hurry and put to sleep  
Pricking the barley tassels  
Feed our elders  

-Baby, baby, go to sleep  
Our baby, go to sleep  
Our baby will sleep  
Lying down in the flower field  
That child will not sleep  
Lying down in the dog poop field  
Baby, baby, go to sleep  
Hurry, hurry and put to sleep  
Pricking the barley tassels  
We will feed you all

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Oh, my grandson, step carefully and firmly.  
Oh hey, hey, don't walk unsteadily.  
It's not just "don't walk,"  
It's the big "don't walk" from Gyeongsang Province.  
Step carefully and firmly.  
In a snail shell, there is weight,  
And in a stone crab, there is wind,  
Even in a dung crab, there is wind.  
Oh grandson, my grandson,  
Step carefully and firmly,  
The big "don't walk" from Gyeongsang Province.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Lullaby, lullaby  
Sweet lullaby, quiet lullaby  
Is she your daughter or my daughter?  
Is she crossing the ditch with a bundle?  
Lullaby, lullaby

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Lullaby, lullaby, our baby, go to sleep  
The dog that lay under the earth  
Will help our baby sleep  
Oh dear, oh dear, our baby  
Sleeps soundly, sleeps well  
Our baby, go to sleep  
Did you fall from the sky?  
Did you sprout from beneath the ground?

Mother, mother, our baby sleeps so well.  
Wongi's pride, Wongi's pride, Wongi's pride, Wongi's pride.

Fire, fire, bulmeya, eolssigu, you’re good at dancing

Blow, blow, bulmeya, eolssigu, you’re good at dancing  
Where is charcoal from? It’s charcoal, a beggar, oak charcoal from Bongsan  
Blow, blow, blow, blow, bulmeya,  
Let’s blow and drink, the kitchen is crowded with firewood  
Bijeo Hill is sweaty, fire, fire, bulmeya

Round and round, mogae, don't die, live on  
Before the pottery kiln, a half-child; before the porcelain kiln, a servant  
Round and round, grow up well

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Eunsadong, Geumsadong, Yeojidong, Yeonhadong

Respect to the noble one, loyal servant Hyodong  
Devoted subject to the winged one

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Rock-a-bye, our baby sleeps so well.  
Our precious descendants like gold, where should we pass them on?  
No matter how I look at it, I can't forget, no matter how I look at it, I can't forget.  
Rock-a-bye, I raised you—what kind of movie was I watching?  
If I had known it would be a day like this, would I have raised you like this?  
When raising you, my tears often fell like needles, but I still raised you.  
Rock-a-bye, our grandson, never imagined it would be like this at all.  
The hardships are finally over here, you live, and I live too.  
Our grandson has grown up; grandmother, live long, long.  
Raising you was such a hardship.  
Eat a lot, even if I do everything for you—  
You lose your appetite and can't eat, it's utterly pitiful.  
I should die well without hardship, whether sick or sorrowful.  
One must be born with the fortune to die, but now, this and that,  
Not knowing any pleasure, I just wish to be born with the fortune to die.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Lullaby, lullaby, sleep well
Our baby sleeps well
Silver child, gold child
If I give gold, will I buy you?
If I give silver, will I buy you?
Be filial to the country, child of filial piety
Our baby sleeps well

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Lullaby, lullaby, our baby sleeps well.  
The black dog next door also sleeps well.  
The white dog across the street also sleeps well.  
Our baby sleeps well.  
Lullaby, lullaby.  

When our baby grows up,  
When our baby grows strong,  
Observing the Five Relationships and Three Bonds,  
Being loyal to the country,  
Being filial to the parents,  
Having brotherly affection,  
Having harmony in the family,  
Lullaby, lullaby, sleeps well.  
Our baby sleeps well.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Silver child, jade child,  
Gallopy, oh hill is a treasure hill.  
Even if given money, can it buy you?  
Even if given jade, can it buy you?  
Be filial to parents,  
Be loving among siblings,  
Be harmonious with relatives,  
Have a loving relationship between husband and wife,  
Be cherished by all around the neighborhood,  
Be loyal to the nation.  

At Dongmang Mountain, returning to the highest peak,  
A pair of phoenix cranes descend,  
In the deep water of the Han River,  
Blue dragon and yellow dragon fly by,  
In the middle of the Daechun Sea,  
Goldfish float drifting around,  
At Bitnae River, baby carp  
sleeping under the stone,  
At the front stream, baby loaches  
sleeping beneath the water.  

Like us, little children,  
Gently and happily growing in their mother’s arms.  
As time flows by, reaching twenty or thirty,  
When married off into another family,  
If you bear a son,  
May he be an outstanding scholar.  
If you bear a daughter,  
May she become the esteemed eldest daughter-in-law.  

It rains, it rains,  
Heaven and Lord,  
Surrounded by the Four Seas Dragon Kings,  
The words spoken by our parents:  
The old shrine collapses,  
A flower blooms on the carefully built tower,  
Within that flower, fruit blooms,  
Swaying gently, dancing gracefully, how wonderful.  

Carrying or holding a baby. Chant in the style of a gisaeng’s song.

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
Silver child, gold child, lacquerware bright and clear, treasure child  
If I give silver, will I buy you? If I give money, will I buy you?  
In the courtyard is an inner house, is it a burnt house or a flowing one?  
Is the courtyard round like a watermelon? Is it a fertile land?  
Is it inside the courtyard? It’s Cheonjiyeon’s work.  
To the country, you are a loyal subject; to parents, you are a filial child.  
Among siblings, there is brotherly love; among relatives, there is affection.  
Even if I give silver and money, how can you be bought?  
The round watermelon rind, grow strong and big,  
The old house is like a thousand bowls—my mother’s eternal resting place.  
Raising a daughter beautifully, I send her to another’s house.  
Shedding tears time after time, receiving sorrow time after time.  
Having nothing to give, I clung to my mother.  
My mother said, “How did you come to this?  
I would rather die myself; it is better.”
