Blow surely and firmly  

(singing briefly, then stopping)

label: Lullaby_lullaby
translation:
When I went to Seoul along the Seongdal River,  
I was given one night’s stay in a scrap attic.  
A black-headed baby rat ate everything, leaving only the shells.  
I boiled it in a bottomless barrel, drained it with a ladle, and soaked it in barley wine to make it.  
As for the meat, I offered it to my grandparents, saying they have no teeth.  
I gave the bones to my mother and father.  
Let’s mix it together and eat among ourselves.  
Seongdal River, Seongdal River, Seongdal River.

It’s fragrant and delicious, it’s fragrant and delicious. / Sop'al

How did he die?

He was eating rice cakes,  
When a black dog bit him on the genitals,  
And he died.  
What kind of business did he do?  
He carried goods on a shoulder pole.  
Who cried?  
The female dog and the male dog cried.  
What kind of cane did he use?  
He used a poker.  
What kind of rice cake did he make?  
He made red bean rice cakes.

label: Ritual_funeral
translation:
@Eohoya Eoh-eoya

Ehenoha Ehenoha  
Among all things of mankind  
What is this talk of parting, parting?  
Hwal-yang Naki1) a thousand miles away  
In the region of So-tong2), separation at the border  
Jeong-gak-gwan-sang3) melting charms  
Uhee Wol-nyeo4) couple’s parting  
Jeong-gak-gwan-sang melting charms  
Yongsa5) brothers’ parting inside  
Seo-chul-yang-gwan6) an innocent person  
Parents’ parting in Wi-seong7)  
Let’s go, let’s go, hurry and go  
What is this Bukmang Mountain and rivers8?  
Outside the window is Bukmang Mountain and rivers  
The young youth all grow old  
Before living fully until old age  
Let’s pick flowers and play  
Since it's hard to come twice again  
The flowers blooming year after year  
Are but a cluster, a few in number10)  
Oh, why is this life so  
Passing through year upon year  
Though time lasts, it means nothing  
The departed spring returns again  
Blessings increase with each passing year11)  
Spring fills the universe12) and blessings come  
Among all things in heaven and earth  
Is there anything besides people?  
I borrow bones from my father  
I borrow flesh from my mother  
I pray for blessings from God  
I pray, I pray  
I pray to God  
Myeongsa ten-ri9) sea roses  
Do not grieve because the flowers have fallen  
If next year in March they come back  
Will you not bloom again?  
When life passes away  
There is no way to see again twice  
Heartless time passes entirely  
Oh dear, oh dear, the hearts of the world  
Will they change day by day?  
Flower, flower, do not push away your color  
Do not chase away the coming butterfly  
The spring light is meaningless  
Though our love also knows this  
When the green grass and wild plants grow thick  
Which butterfly will look for you?  
Life at seventy, they say, is old age  
Eighty is elderly years, ninety, spring flourishing  
How long does a person live?  
If you live well  
You live about a hundred years and then pass

Notes:  
1) Hwa-rang Naki (和樂落日)  
2) Yunnan Province area in northern China  
3) Jeong-gak-gwan-sang (正客觀相) - a concept or charm  
4) Uhee Wol-nyeo (우衣越女)  
5) Yongsa (龍沙) - outside the Great Wall of China  
6) Seo-chul-yang-gwan (西出陽關)  
7) Wi-seong (危星), one of the 28 lunar mansions  
8) Bukmang Mountains and rivers (北邙山川)  
9) Myeongsa Ten-ri (明沙十里) - a beach in Wonsan, beautiful with soft sand and sea roses  
10) Clustered in bloom  
11) Increase in life span  
12) Spring fills the universe

In the middle of the month, the Northern Fairy descended to the Jade Emperor’s court,

In a deep cave of the copper mountain, building a house with reed mats.  
Wrapping it carefully, watering the Milky Way,  
After boiling the mulberry silkworms, carefully removing them one by one.  
Tying and untying knots, stretching the thread across the vast sky.  
Chattering back and forth in the cold morning breeze and dew,  
Separating the knots and loosening the warp threads,  
After combing the fibers for three days, stretching out the sprawling arrowroot on the back hill,  
Hanging the spinning wheel’s thread, both the old and young village headmen  
Sit in turn, talking loud and clear.  
Using the sharp stone spindle, sending it in one place.  
Dressing it in the yard, in the deep room of copper mountain,  
Giving off golden light, standing opposite the jar of fermented sauce,  
Grinding and mixing carefully, washing it thoroughly,  
Drying it in the sunlight, then rolling up the sharp stone spindle,  
Gathering thread by thread, pinching it with ten fingers like birds pecking.  
Stretching it out in the yard, gently twisting it,  
Turning the large and small beam cranks here and there,  
Like the stork-shaped dotumari (type of loom),  
Setting up the loom, waiting for the loom’s legs,  
Placing the front leg on a spot, the back leg on another,  
Hanging the warp threads, the pressing bar is the hoburebi (a kind of measuring bar).  
The eye edges are two brothers, the warp threads three brothers,  
The endless, headless dried pollock carries eggs like dragon’s eggs,  
Flying here and there, tears dripping, the crude dog (dog’s tail thread)

The sound of the bodi (drum) is like thunder in the deep mountains,  
The crying sound of the dragon’s head is like the bird calls in the deep mountains.  
The very crooked new wood is hung with a noose like worn-out cloth,  
The coming and going sheep is like the stork-shaped dotumari.  
Hit here and there, fall down, weave the net until finished,  
Why weave the net? When my brother goes to the market,  
Tie the saddle stirrups around his feet, what more to do?  
When our father goes mountain hunting, make him a hunting coat,  
When going back home, when my mother goes back home,

Gathering all the weavings gathered there,

Last year’s itinerant storyteller  
comes to your doorstep offering blessings,  
please kindly give some alms generously.  

When I hold the character for one or the number one,  
the sun and moon shine in pairs,  
the time of night is clearly evident.  

When I hold the character for two,  
in just two months, a president.  

When I hold the character for three,  
there are thirty million compatriots.  
We eagerly await peace’s arrival.  

When I hold the character for four,  
the world is busy in a vast, busy road,  
even a short break is delayed.  

When I hold the character for five,  
there is the general Guan Yu on the battlefield,  
riding his Red Hare,  
going to meet Master Zhuge.  

When I hold the character for six,  
there is a general of the army,  
writing letters and going everywhere.  

When I hold the character for seven,  
with a troubled mind,  
I can’t go out because of a headache.  

When I hold the character for eight,  
eight brothers,  
even without reading a single book,  
all become magistrates of Pyongyang.  

When I hold the character for nine,  
a ninety-year-old white-haired elder  
collapses in the top scholar exam.  

When I hold the character for ten,  
there is the master clown (Gwag Gwang-dae),  
the elder among clowns.  

To this house and to that house,  
to the sacred houses,  
please kindly give generously.  
May you receive abundant blessings.

Let this person complain and lament their fate, let’s have some fun.  
Eolssigu ssigu, here it comes, jeolssiggu du na enters.  
Last year’s storyteller hasn’t died and has come again.  
Poom poom baeneun, hagudu na, well done.  
The sun and moon in the thirty years and the new moon of March; when the sun sets, the moon rises in the east; the fire turns—our people love to play.  
Ehe eolssigu comes, jeolssigu du na enters.  
Let’s welcome eolssigu du and enjoy our jangtaryeong (folk song). Oh, how nice.  
When we return through the mountains and rivers, even though the mountains and trees cry, our village does not leave.  
Last year’s storyteller hasn’t died and has returned; just lend me a spoonful of rice.  
I am tired of seeing the person who wore the hat before; let’s walk instead.  
With the sun and moon, when the wind blows in mid-month,  
In the second month, listening to the green dawn and the young buds of grain,  
By the third month, looking back at the mountains and trees that have come and gone,

Holding five or six letters: on the way to O-gwancheonjang, riding a red horse sidesteps to visit Master Je-gal.  
Holding six or seven letters: on the wooden floor of six rooms, the village ladies play a game called Dadimidol.  
Holding seven or eight letters: in the great cold of seven years, royal water falls over the mountain peaks; the great cold season dances.  
Holding eight or nine letters: our brothers are eight in number, learning to read at the same school, but seeing the exams is delayed.  
Holding nine letters: an old monk in his eighties wears white prayer beads around his neck, wishing to become Buddha.  
Holding ten letters: in the pine forest, a roe deer enters; the first hunter is brought; if you cannot shoot, I will.  
Holding ten letters, I see things I have not seen for over ten years; where else would we find our hunter?  
Eolssigu na, jeolssigu du na, even the acrobatics of Pumba are well done.

Eighteen mountains are useless; pride and power serve no purpose.  
Gripping my sword and standing up, all around are only losses.  
I wander and wander; even if I go, what can I do for you?  
Hesitating at the Three Treasures, pressing the Five Treasures,  
The superior army disperses, and my heart is scattered.  
Even the ducks of Pengsheng lament, covering their great valley,  
Heading east of the river, the defeated Paewang burns in fire.  
How can I raise my face again and see my parents anew?  
How can the people of Chu see this? Hundred generations of heroes and great men.  
Listening to the battle cry in Chu’s capital, it is all meaningless.  
Is pure heart the highest? The Han band and the hundred thousand troops  
Under the Copper Mountain, surrounding the great camp.  
When luring the sleeping Paewang, the good strategist places the mountain well.  
In the autumn night of Mount Guimyung, the jade flute laments mournfully.  
When the eight thousand disciples are scattered, that song was pure white.  
Deep in the night of Guqiu, the sky high and the moon bright,  
The wild goose cries out in the clear sky.  
It seems to stir a traveler’s sorrow, amidst the borderlands’ deadly battleground.  
Oh, soldier bidding farewell, now that your Paewang has fallen,  
War means death, and your wives and children  
In the cold wind of Hansan’s sunset, oh, how can I leave you?  
Will news come today? Will a letter come tomorrow?  
A face as beautiful as jade, a grieving husband’s deep sorrow,  
Rotting tears flow day and night.  
Placing my hand on my forehead, looking toward the departing path,  
Will I become a stone of mourning? Under Nam Mountain, constantly,  
The blowing wind, which courtesan will shield me?  
The good wine before the showdown, who will taste it?  
The son calls his father, the mother’s liver melts bend by bend.  

When General Lee Nam left, holding hands at the gate,  
Tears shed and early words spoken, leaving youthful beauty behind.  
“I will return in September next year,” a vow as firm as gold and stone.  
Firmly set in the village, “Don’t forget,” but  
Eight years of hardship have passed, and has our General Lee Nam died or lived?  
In the silent war chamber’s empty room, the loneliness of solitary mourning deepens evermore.  

– Song of Chu and Han
